papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD methods—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to feature- and relation-level imitation—work across modalities and tasks and integrate naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, maximizing KD’s benefits requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; left unaddressed, challenges such as representation misalignment, degraded rare-token behavior, and robustness or privacy losses can limit gains.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Best-Practices Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. When engineered to the task and deployment constraints and combined with complementary techniques (e.g., representation alignment, data strategies, pruning/quantization, and multi-teacher schedules), KD yields strong size–performance tradeoffs. However, practitioners must design distillation pipelines to address capacity mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, bias transfer, and data-privacy constraints to produce robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language, distillation strategies—matching logits, internal features, attention or relational structure, or using synthetic or public data—enable large reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical deployments combine distillation with other compression tools, online or distributed training regimes, and privacy-aware variants, but face persistent challenges in aligning internal representations, retaining robustness and fairness, and operating under data or resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, faster students so models can be deployed under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Distillation methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or ensemble outputs), how training data are used (original, augmented, synthesized, or absent), and how distillation is combined with orthogonal compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results show KD can preserve substantial teacher performance when pipelines are tailored to student capacity, data availability, and deployment needs; open challenges remain around robustness, fairness, domain shift, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision and NLP, KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance when combined with representation-level transfer, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Practical application requires matching transferred signals to student capacity, addressing data-availability or privacy constraints, and evaluating robustness and fairness under distribution shift. Best-practice pipelines use task-aware signals, staged training or annealing, pretraining of compact students, and complementary compression to maximize deployed performance.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, higher‑capacity teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Methods span matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, designing teacher training to ease transfer, selecting or synthesizing distillation data, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can retain much teacher performance when carefully applied, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to handle student capacity and data heterogeneity, and how to mitigate teacher imperfections and robustness or fairness tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, teacher selection strategies, data-aware techniques, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD yields compact models that recover much of teacher utility while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Real-world success requires attention to student capacity, data mismatch, optimization dynamics, and societal risks such as bias or privacy leakage.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. These techniques are applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), deployment scenarios (edge devices, federated learning), and objectives (accuracy preservation, efficiency, interpretability, fairness). Advances include theoretical reframings that connect KD to regularization, a range of strategies for aligning outputs and internal representations, methods that restructure or progressively replace model components, and practical systems that enable heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments. Despite clear empirical gains, open problems remain in understanding when and why different distillation targets (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior) are most effective, and how to balance compression with robustness and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Effective, Flexible, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully—matching what is transferred to student capacity, combining logits- and feature-level objectives, and integrating complementary techniques like low-precision numerics or architectural redesign—KD consistently yields compact models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints such as privacy or heterogeneity, so practitioners must adapt KD components and pipelines to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, faster students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across modalities, KD includes matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and distilling relational or attention signals; it is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Effective KD requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distillation targets, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and evaluation for robustness and fairness. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, and preserving long-tail behaviors, which motivate context-sensitive, pipeline-oriented compression practices.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Sampson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD operates by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (for example softened logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals), and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task- or data-aware training protocols. Practical success requires matching distillation signals to student capacity and deployment goals, careful handling of data availability (including data‑free or synthesized approaches), and safeguards for robustness, long‑tail behavior, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features, using multiple teachers or online cooperative training, and operating with original, public, or synthesized data. In practice KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student preparation, and data strategy. KD can substantially reduce inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but it can also propagate teacher weaknesses (distributional biases, low-frequency errors) unless these are explicitly addressed.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical center of model compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably yields compact, lower-latency models while retaining much of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on deployment context. Best outcomes arise when KD is paired with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), careful choice of distillation signals, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most pragmatic and versatile foundation for compressing large deep and NLP models for deployment. When KD is broadened beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher schedules, data strategies, and integration with pruning/quantization, it yields compact students that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is not a silver bullet: careful signal design, student capacity matching, and complementary compression techniques are required to handle domain shift, rare-token behaviors, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—using richer targets than logits, aligning intermediate representations, and combining with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search—KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of a teacher's performance. KD also adapts to constrained settings (few-shot, federated, or data-free) and supports robustness and domain adaptation when pipelines are designed to match task and deployment constraints. Realizing KD's full value requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their effectiveness. When combined with task-specific adaptations (layer mapping, data-free synthesis, federated protocols, quantization, or self-supervision), KD enables deployment in low-resource, privacy-sensitive, and domain-specific settings. Success depends on designing appropriate alignment mechanisms, data strategies, and fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. The practice has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift challenges.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs, and it integrates naturally with feature-level matching, data-free synthesis, online and federated protocols, and teacher-design strategies. However, its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (logits, features, attention), data availability and domain match, teacher–student capacity alignment, and objectives like robustness, privacy, and fairness. Real-world deployment requires matching distillation techniques to constraints and explicitly addressing robustness, bias, and data-privacy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Engineering-Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer outputs, intermediate representations, relationships, or curricula and supports data-free, multi-teacher, and online variants. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation) and careful teacher–student alignment, KD reliably reduces inference cost and storage while often preserving generalization. However, its success depends on design choices—what to transfer, how to handle limited or private data, and how to align capacities and optimization—so KD should be treated as a core component of a compression pipeline rather than a plug-and-play remedy.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a family of methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). These approaches aim to retain predictive performance while reducing model size, latency, or enabling deployment under privacy or communication constraints. Recent work broadens distillation beyond logits to intermediate features, attention maps, multi-teacher setups, and data-limited or privacy-preserving regimes, producing task- and domain-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across modalities and deployment regimes, KD can be adapted to match soft outputs, internal representations, or training dynamics, and it plays well with complementary techniques (architecture changes, pruning, data augmentation, and online/distributed protocols). However, realizing KD's benefits in practice requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to produce or curate training data, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. I argue KD should be treated as a central component in compression pipelines while being combined with representation-aware objectives, deployment-aware protocols, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring predictive and representational information from large ‘teacher’ models into smaller ‘student’ models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate representation imitation, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, and data strategies including synthetic or data-free approaches. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though limits remain around domain shift, rare-token behavior, robustness, and the propagation of teacher shortcomings.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods reduce the computational and memory cost of large neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller students. Approaches vary from using soft logits to matching internal representations, attention maps, or generator outputs; they have been adapted for modality transfer, privacy- or bandwidth-constrained settings, and specialized architectures (e.g., transformers, GANs). Empirical work shows that representation-level objectives, architectural design of the student/bridge modules, and careful training protocols can preserve most of the teacher’s performance while dramatically reducing size and runtime. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, deploying under strict privacy/bandwidth constraints, and automating architecture search for compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention-based signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and when tuned for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch between teacher and student, preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors, transferred biases and brittleness, and distillation under data- or heterogeneity-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques for transferring information from large, often expensive teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models so they retain much of the teacher's performance while reducing inference cost. KD methods operate at different levels (logits, intermediate features, modules or entire architectures) and are applied across domains including vision, speech, NLP and federated settings. Contemporary work has advanced new losses, layer-alignment strategies, module-replacement schemes, robustness-aware procedures, and analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Important practical challenges remain around heterogeneous data, strong teachers, and preserving properties such as robustness, generalization across distributions, and multimodal capability.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables reduced storage and faster inference while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle when training data are unavailable or misaligned with deployment distributions, and interact subtly with optimization and architecture mismatch. A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies—feature- and layer-level objectives, data-free or synthesized-data protocols when needed, curriculum or sample-weighting policies, and hardware-aware pruning or architecture search—to maximize efficiency without sacrificing robustness or task-specific fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a dominant approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It operates by transferring information from a teacher to a student using a variety of signals and workflows, and it is routinely combined with other compression techniques to meet practical latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teachers performance, its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability or synthesis of data, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD can be adapted across modalities and constraints—by matching soft logits, intermediate representations, or attention maps; by using ensembles or teacher optimization; and by operating with or without original training data—making it well suited to real-world deployment needs. Because its effectiveness depends on representation alignment, teacher–student design, and data regime, KD is best applied as a component in broader compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware choices) and selected to fit the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides a flexible set of supervision signals and workflows that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful design around data, architecture alignment, and evaluation, produces compact models that retain most of the teacher’s utility while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful deployment requires explicit attention to capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy limits, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic, widely applicable pathway to convert large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and by combining with complementary compression primitives, KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success is design-sensitive: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness determine whether distillation yields reliable, production-ready models.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Best-Practices Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. When engineered to the task and deployment constraints and combined with complementary techniques (e.g., representation alignment, data strategies, pruning/quantization, and multi-teacher schedules), KD yields strong size–performance tradeoffs. However, practitioners must design distillation pipelines to address capacity mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, bias transfer, and data-privacy constraints to produce robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD comprises a family of methods — from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or privacy-prespecting variants — that together enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and power while retaining much of teacher performance. Its success in production settings depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle scarce or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign).

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Engineering Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities, but it is design-sensitive: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or domain shifts determine outcomes. Framing KD as the central tool within a broader compression pipeline — combined with feature-level objectives, multi-teacher or data-synthesis strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) — leads to more reliable and deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Malone
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a central element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques, KD enables deployments that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing those gains in practice requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to data and optimization mismatches, and explicit evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach has expanded from soft-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, self-distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical deployments succeed when distillation objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and task-aware choices are tuned to the application; remaining challenges include preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, handling distribution shift and data scarcity, and ensuring robustness and privacy in deployed students.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. Across vision, language, and cross-modal tasks, KD is used both as a stand-alone compression method and in combination with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical strategies include logit (soft-label) matching, feature-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or label-synthesis when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows that distillation can recover most of a teacher's performance while enabling much smaller and faster models, but outcomes depend strongly on choices such as teacher quality, the form of distilled signals, augmentation and synthetic-data generation, and whether low-precision or domain-specific constraints apply.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Principled Path to Efficient, Adaptable, and Responsible NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a general framework that enables smaller or specialized models to inherit useful behaviors from larger teachers while controlling generalization, efficiency, and social impact. When combined with layer-wise and representation-level matching, task-aware architecture search, thoughtful input augmentation, and deployment-aware protocols, KD supports high-performance, resource-frugal NLP systems that can be adapted to heterogeneous devices and sensitive application contexts.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance when its objectives, data regime, and teacher–student alignment are chosen to match deployment constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, careful combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-token or domain-shift behaviors. I argue KD should be treated as the central technique in model-compression pipelines, applied with engineering rigor and complementary methods to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and deployment cost while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensembles), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Across vision and NLP tasks, distillation enables practical deployment of compact models but requires careful handling of representation mismatch, data availability, optimization schedules, and potential amplification of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When framed as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output transfer with intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies, teacher-aware optimization, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design)—KD enables deployment of high-performing, smaller models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity, attention to data and distributional issues, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and rare-token failures.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated technique for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teachers. When integrated with complementary methods — such as progressive module replacement, data-free synthesis, adversarially-aware training, and task- or domain-aware curricula — KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints and enables domain adaptation and robustness improvements. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distillation signal, data strategies, and careful pipeline design to preserve robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic training trick into a broadly applicable, practical toolkit for compressing large models for deployment in constrained environments. KD enables substantial size and latency reductions while retaining much of teacher performance; it supports different transfer signals (logits, features, attention), works with or without original training data, and can be adapted to preserve robustness or meet privacy constraints. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students (including pre-training), how to handle limited or heterogeneous data, and how to mitigate transferred biases or adversarial vulnerability. Combining distillation with complementary strategies—layer-aware matching, feature-level mimicry, data synthesis or augmentation, teacher optimization, and robustness-aware objectives—gives the most reliable practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. When matched to task needs and combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and robustness or privacy-aware adaptations, KD enables small models to retain much of teachers' performance across modalities. However, KD is context-sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the chosen distillation signal determine outcomes. A pragmatic pipeline blends logit and feature matching, targeted data augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods to achieve robust, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns
