papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal information. Methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features or relational structure, and KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows strong practical gains across vision and NLP, but challenges remain around representation alignment, robustness, rare-token fidelity, privacy, and data heterogeneity — motivating richer distillation targets and deployment-aware pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented approach for shrinking large models into deployable students. When applied as a toolbox — not a single recipe — KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while meeting real-world constraints. Practical effectiveness hinges on choosing which signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Careful pipelines that address data availability, optimization mismatch, domain shift, and bias/robustness concerns enable KD to be the central component of reliable compression workflows.

papers_seen.author: Villa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is most effective when treated as a central component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses architecture-aware design, data curricula, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Real-world success requires careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data regime, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes such as degraded rare-token modeling and privacy-sensitive transfer.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Combinations, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and pragmatic method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving much of a teacher’s performance, but its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), how teacher–student alignment is addressed, and how distillation is integrated with pre-training, architecture design, and other compression tools. I argue that KD should be treated as the central component of an engineering pipeline for efficient NLP and deep-learning systems: it provides flexible transfer mechanisms, enables many successful combinations (multi-teacher, layer mapping, data synthesis), and yields strong practical results, yet it must be paired with complementary strategies and careful choices to manage teacher imperfections, representation mismatch, data limitations, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from teachers to students and are effective across modalities and tasks when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Success depends on principled choices about distillation targets, student capacity, data selection or synthesis, and mitigation of distribution-shift, rare-token, and bias-amplification failures. KD therefore functions best as a central, design-sensitive component of end-to-end model-compression pipelines that balance accuracy, latency, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Armstrong
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to include intermediate-representation and attention transfer, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, data-aware curricula, and combinations with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher’s utility across vision and language when its signals, data, and student capacity are chosen deliberately; remaining challenges center on capacity mismatch, distribution shift, robustness, fairness, and data- or privacy-limited regimes. Best practices emphasize aligning distilled signals with student capacity, using pre-training for compact students, and integrating KD with complementary compression techniques for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, practitioners apply KD to reduce model size, latency, and resource cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Variants of KD extend beyond soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, cross-modal transfer, and data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. Effective distillation typically combines careful choice of transfer target, student architecture and pre-training, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization). Open challenges include principled data selection or synthesis for distillation, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling distillation to large distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployable approach for compressing large neural and language models into smaller, faster students. By transferring information beyond hard labels—through softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals, or self-generated examples—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Real-world success requires combining KD with task-aware objectives, data strategies, and hardware-aware compression methods; attention to representation alignment, rare-token fidelity, and robustness is necessary to avoid common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning student capacity and architecture, and combining distillation with complementary compression steps—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and distributional or privacy concerns require targeted design choices and evaluation to produce robust, fair, and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Barker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD spans soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer-wise objectives, and data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches). When combined with architecture-aware choices, pruning/quantization, and task- or data-aware training curricula, KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, its benefits are contingent on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy; KD should therefore be treated as a core, composable element of compression pipelines rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Powerful but Not Sufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone, KD enables on-device deployment, domain adaptation, ensemble condensation, and improved efficiency with modest performance loss. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, transferred biases, poor handling of rare or low-frequency behaviors) and must be combined with complementary compression techniques, robust data strategies, and evaluation under deployment constraints to be reliably effective.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features, using multiple teachers or online cooperative training, and operating with original, public, or synthesized data. In practice KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student preparation, and data strategy. KD can substantially reduce inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but it can also propagate teacher weaknesses (distributional biases, low-frequency errors) unless these are explicitly addressed.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context-Sensitive for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can be applied across modalities and settings to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and serve as a core component of broader compression pipelines. However, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, data regimes, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a dominant approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It operates by transferring information from a teacher to a student using a variety of signals and workflows, and it is routinely combined with other compression techniques to meet practical latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teachers performance, its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability or synthesis of data, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large models and transfer knowledge across models, modalities, and tasks. Practitioners use KD to produce smaller, faster student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, to regularize training via self-distillation, and to enable multi-task or resource-heterogeneous deployment. Despite strong empirical results across vision, speech, translation, and question answering, distillation exhibits failure modes—e.g., propagation of teacher errors or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena—that motivate variants such as multi-teacher schemes, feature-level objectives, projector layers, and teacher-student co-training. The literature combines empirical recipes and growing theoretical analysis to guide when and how to mix soft teacher signals and hard labels, design teacher architectures, and choose representation vs. logit distillation for best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, and generative settings shows KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployability costs. Best results arise when KD is combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher–student design, data-aware strategies (including augmentation or synthetic data), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). KD has clear limits — e.g., it can transfer undesirable teacher behaviors, struggle with rare-token or data-mismatch regimes, and interact with privacy constraints — so production use requires principled pipelines that mitigate these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field encompasses a range of techniques—from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals—and integrates with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, the availability and curation of data (real or synthesized), and deployment constraints such as latency, memory, robustness, and privacy. Persistent challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and ensuring generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layerwise and many-to-many mapping, relational and curriculum schemes, self- and multi-teacher approaches, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and tuned to deployment constraints (latency, memory, robustness, and privacy), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, though open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and using synthesized or augmented data—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Applications of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more costly models to smaller, deployable models. Modern work expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include distillation of internal representations, feature-level imitation, privacy-preserving and data-free strategies, task-adaptive compression, and adaptations to specialized architectures (e.g., GANs, detectors, and transformers). These methods aim to preserve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency (compute, memory, or communication) while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices or in privacy-sensitive and distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practical Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations, enabling reduced latency, memory footprint, and energy use while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective KD combines choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to supply or synthesize training data, and when to integrate complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization). Success depends on task- and data-aware engineering: careful teacher selection or synthesis, student capacity matching, and mitigation of distributional and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching into a flexible toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention-level objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free workflows, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When applied with task- and deployment-aware design choices (what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and what data or augmentations to use), KD routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs in vision and NLP. Practical deployments require careful engineering to handle capacity mismatch, imperfect teachers, privacy constraints, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Core of Model Compression — and How to Use It Safely
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high-impact approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller students suitable for deployment. KD can transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, or training dynamics to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. Effective, production-ready compression treats KD as the central engine but pairs it with complementary techniques (representation alignment, projectors, pruning/quantization, privacy-aware protocols and ensemble or multi-teacher strategies). KD yields strong size–performance tradeoffs in both vision and NLP when engineered for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; however, practitioners must also manage limitations such as transferred biases, capacity mismatch, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD can transfer predictive behavior, representations, or task-specific inductive biases; when combined with pre-training, architecture search, or careful data handling, it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of what is distilled (logits vs. features), how teachers and students are chosen or trained, the availability and quality of data (including synthetic or unlabeled public data), and auxiliary techniques such as projectors, multi-teacher weighting, or meta-learning to adapt the teaching process. I argue that with these design choices attended to, KD is a broadly applicable and cost-effective strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Malone
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a central element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques, KD enables deployments that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing those gains in practice requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to data and optimization mismatches, and explicit evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a central, flexible component of model‑compression pipelines rather than as a single canned technique. By transferring richer forms of supervision (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational or attention signals) and by being combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD enables deployment of compact models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful distillation requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. When applied with task‑aware design and safeguards against optimization and bias failure modes, KD provides a practical road for compressing large models for real‑world NLP and deep‑learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, KD functions as a toolbox: it can transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; be combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization; and operate with or without original training data. KD delivers substantial reductions in size and latency with modest performance loss when methods and signals are chosen to match student capacity, task requirements, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context-sensitive: success depends on handling teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness concerns, data availability, and optimization choices. The most reliable pipelines therefore combine multiple distillation signals, data-aware strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as bias transfer and rare-token degradation.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers learned behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and sometimes improve regularization and robustness. A diverse toolkit has emerged—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention and channel-wise supervision, data-aware strategies including synthetic or public-data distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical deployment emphasizes task-aware choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers and data, and how to combine compression techniques), while open problems include theory of when distillation helps, handling rare-token behavior in NLP, distributional shift, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods provide practical mechanisms to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students suitable for real-world deployment. Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners use KD to trade off capacity and efficiency while aiming to preserve task performance, often in combination with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Success depends on aligning teacher signals, student capacity, data strategy, and optimization schedules; remaining challenges include handling domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior, and operating under privacy or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Schwartz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to internal representations and relational objectives—KD composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Successful application requires careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit validation for robustness and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables retention of teacher capabilities across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. Effective deployment requires matching distillation targets to student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy limits, and combining KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning or architecture search. This paper argues that KD should be the central component of modern compression pipelines and outlines practical principles to maximize its benefits and mitigate common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Gross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, or relational signals, and are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. Empirical work shows that KD typically narrows the performance gap between teacher and student across modalities, but practical success depends on careful choices about distillation targets, teacher preparation, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture-aware design, data augmentation, and privacy mechanisms), KD consistently yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to select or synthesize data, and how to mitigate transferred harms (bias, privacy leakage). This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, flexible tool for model compression while emphasizing practical design principles and known failure modes that practitioners must address.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A spectrum of distillation targets—soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals—and workflows—offline teacher supervision, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula, and data-aware synthesis—have demonstrated strong empirical trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. Remaining practical issues include student–teacher capacity mismatch, preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable biases or teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer behavior from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision and language, practitioners match softened outputs, align internal representations, or transfer relational signals, often combining distillation with quantization, architecture adaptation, or data selection to meet deployment constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the distilled signals chosen, data availability or synthesis, and strategies for aligning heterogeneous architectures and preserving robustness.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential, versatile method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining softened-output supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies, and architecture-aware design—KD regularly yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, its success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of transfer signals, data availability, and deployment constraints determine outcomes. Real-world adoption therefore requires pipeline-oriented practices that combine KD with complementary compression techniques and targeted evaluation for robustness, domain shift, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design‑Sensitive Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment objectives and combined with complementary compression methods, KD can recover most of a teacher’s utility while delivering substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy. However, distillation is context‑sensitive: the distilled signals, student capacity, data regime, and privacy or fairness constraints all shape outcomes. Treating KD as an essential but configurable toolbox—rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm—yields the most reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach for turning large pretrained models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher’s capability. When combined with representation-aware objectives, student pre-training, and complementary compression techniques, KD delivers substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy use while enabling deployment across language, vision, and multimodal tasks. Real-world success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, managing data (or synthesizing it), and applying safeguards for robustness and privacy, but the accumulated evidence recommends treating distillation as a central, configurable tool in compression pipelines rather than an isolated recipe.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The literature frames KD as a toolkit that includes soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-representation alignment, layer- or module-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and curriculum schedules, data-augmentation or data-free approaches, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance when signals, data, and architectures are chosen deliberately; however, limits arise from capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, distributional shift, and the potential to transfer undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, spurious correlations). Practical pipelines therefore co-design teachers and students, select appropriate transfer signals, and pair distillation with data and system-level strategies to meet deployment constraints. Remaining research directions include better theoretical understanding, distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, student-aware teacher design, and fairness-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, engineering-centered approach for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models. Over the last decade KD has expanded from soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-level transfers, multi-stage and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioner choices align teacher signals, student capacity, and available data. Common failure modes—capacity mismatch, distributional shift, degraded behavior on rare or long-tail phenomena, and transfer of teacher biases—motivate careful design, diagnostics, and hybrid pipelines for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Strengths, Limits, and How to Apply It
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—combining logits and representation matching, adapting teacher and student designs, and addressing data- or privacy-constrained settings—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a cure-all: optimization difficulties, teacher imperfections, data mismatch, and distributional limits require targeted strategies (e.g., feature-aware losses, data-free synthesis, online or multi-teacher schemes) to make distillation robust and production-ready.
