papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining predictive performance. Methods vary from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, using teacher ensembles or meta-learned teachers, and operating under constraints such as missing data, privacy, or heterogeneous devices. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student generalization relative to training from scratch in many settings but interacts with optimization, data availability, and teacher imperfection; practical deployments benefit from task-aware choices of distillation targets, architectural adapters, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile empirical framework for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and structured prediction, KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (e.g., softened outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure) and is commonly integrated with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical pipelines emphasize task- and student-aware design, careful teacher selection or training, and data-management choices; when applied thoughtfully KD can recover much of a teacher's performance but still faces challenges in robustness, domain shift, fairness, and theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Reyes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic, flexible pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. As a composable toolset rather than a single recipe, KD transfers soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational signals; composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; and can be adapted for multi-teacher, data-limited, and privacy-aware regimes. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, designing layer-aware objectives and curricula, and mitigating known failure modes such as data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, robustness degradation, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. The literature has expanded from simple soft-label matching to a broad toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free and zero-shot approaches, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, and combinations with pruning/quantization or architecture search. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints determine success; outstanding challenges include optimization dynamics, distribution shift, rare-token behaviors, and guaranteeing robust or fair behavior after compression.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. The practice has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift challenges.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Imperative for Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have driven major NLP advances but are often impractical for real-world deployment because of size, latency, privacy, and data-distribution constraints. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies enable retaining most of a large model's performance while producing models that meet latency, memory, and regulatory requirements. Effective KD encompasses diverse techniques — task-adaptive compression, feature mimicking, data-free distillation, teacher meta-learning, privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/continual distillation — which together form a practical toolkit for making state-of-the-art NLP useful at scale.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Tool for Compression in NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher's performance. In natural language processing, KD can operate at multiple granularities — from logits to intermediate representations or entire modules — and can be combined with pre-training, pruning, and low-precision inference to meet real-world deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, mismatches in internal representations, and task-specific redundancies can limit benefits unless methods are adapted to the model size, pre-training regimen, and downstream objectives. When applied thoughtfully (e.g., pre-training compact students, selectively transferring internal features, and using task-aware layer-wise matching), KD yields efficient models that generalize well across tasks and settings.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, and generative settings shows KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployability costs. Best results arise when KD is combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher–student design, data-aware strategies (including augmentation or synthetic data), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). KD has clear limits — e.g., it can transfer undesirable teacher behaviors, struggle with rare-token or data-mismatch regimes, and interact with privacy constraints — so production use requires principled pipelines that mitigate these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is empirically effective across modalities because it transfers richer signals than hard labels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational cues) and composes with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). However, KD is engineering-dependent: data availability, teacher quality, and student–teacher mismatch create failure modes that require task-aware choices. A pragmatic compression pipeline treats KD as one component among data strategies, architecture adaptation, and hardware-aware tuning to achieve reliable, high-fidelity compressed models.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from one or more teacher models into smaller students so they retain much of the teacher’s capabilities with lower compute, memory, or latency. The literature spans a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and common integrations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pre-training of compact models). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and inductive biases, what data to use (or synthesize), and constraints around deployment, privacy, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used set of techniques to transfer behavior from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" models so they can run with lower latency, memory, and cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. The field has diversified from simple logit-matching into a broad toolkit that includes feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, data-free or synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle data and domain mismatch, and how to address optimization and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves substantial teacher utility across vision and NLP, but theoretical and empirical analyses also highlight optimization limits, capacity- and distribution-mismatch risks, and the importance of pre-training and task-aware design for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used framework for compressing large, high‑performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure), and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as capacity mismatch, robustness degradation, privacy leakage, and poor long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Design-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and reliably improves student performance under resource constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: real-world deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including data-free or domain-adaptive approaches), and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to address capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. A broad family of KD techniques—matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, transferring relational structure, and using synthesized or public data—enables large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing data strategies (including data-free or synthesized data) when original data are unavailable, and combining KD with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Persistent challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, avoiding transfer of teacher biases, and aligning heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: In Defense of Knowledge Distillation as the Default Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it consistently yields large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance and is flexible enough to address diverse deployment constraints. KD's effectiveness depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to supply training signals, and how to align teacher and student architectures; when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and data-aware practices, KD produces deployable students for on-device, federated, and low-data scenarios. However, KD is not a panacea: its routine use must be accompanied by strategies to handle domain shift, rare-token fidelity, privacy, and architectural mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, teacher–student alignment, privacy constraints, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Treating KD as a central component of a broader compression pipeline — combined with architecture search, task-aware objectives, and privacy- or data-aware procedures — yields the most reliable path to efficient, deployable models.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational signals. Over the last decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching into a flexible toolbox—incorporating feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, data synthesis or data-free workflows, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures and capacities, what data to use (or synthesize), and how to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift problems.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Pillar for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables deployment on resource-limited devices, supports privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, and combines effectively with pre-training, data augmentation, and structured compression. I argue that KD should be a default component of any production-aware model compression pipeline, augmented by task- and data-aware techniques to preserve robustness and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable method for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. As a toolkit rather than a single algorithm, KD combines multiple signal types, training schedules, and data strategies and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and deployment-aware engineering. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, it has predictable failure modes that require careful pipeline design and targeted mitigation.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention/relational signals, and can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies (including synthesized or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely improves student performance when design choices are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints, but practitioners must address challenges such as distribution shift, low-frequency behavior loss, and transfer of undesirable teacher properties.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. When combined with representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware strategies, and architecture-aware design, KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency. Its effectiveness depends on careful handling of data availability, teacher-student mismatch, and ethical or robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for NLP Model Compression: Promise, Proofs, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large NLP and deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques—such as architecture-aware compression, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis—KD can deliver much of a teacher model’s performance while greatly reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation is not without limits: it can propagate teacher biases, depends on careful choice of what and how to transfer, and requires task- and data-aware engineering to be robust in low-data or privacy-sensitive settings. A pragmatic pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies for representation alignment, sample selection, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision and language tasks, the approach ranges from soft‑target/logit matching to feature‑ and layer‑wise alignment, attention or relational transfers, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑limited or data‑free regimes. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful design of teacher–student interactions, selection of distilled signals, management of data and optimization dynamics, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods range from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants that synthesize or reuse surrogate data. Applied across vision, speech, recommender systems, and NLP, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while enabling domain adaptation and robustness-focused objectives. Practical success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and NLP, KD has evolved from soft-target matching into a flexible toolbox that includes representation-level alignment, attention and relational signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data strategies such as augmentation or synthetic/data-free generation. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful engineering to match student capacity, select appropriate signals, and manage data or privacy constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, practitioners must address failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, degraded rare-token behavior, and propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides a flexible set of supervision signals and workflows that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful design around data, architecture alignment, and evaluation, produces compact models that retain most of the teacher’s utility while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful deployment requires explicit attention to capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy limits, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger pretrained or ensemble teachers in deep learning and NLP. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and aligning teacher and student architectures — KD recovers much of the teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioners explicitly guard against capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, and the propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical but Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data and architecture choices, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned, data quality and selection, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models by transferring information from larger teacher models, enabling deployment under computation, memory, or latency constraints. Across vision, speech, language, and recommendation systems, KD takes many forms — logit matching, feature mimicking, ensemble compression, and data-free synthesis — and is often combined with model pruning, architectural simplification, or curriculum strategies. Effective distillation requires choices about what to transfer (soft targets vs. intermediate features), how to supply or synthesize data, and how to schedule or regularize training; these choices shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller models by transferring predictive and representational information from teachers to students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical pipelines combine soft-target matching, representation-level imitation, architecture-aware design and search, and data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving synthesis). While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can enable students that are substantially faster and smaller, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and teacher quality; important open problems remain in robustness, domain shift, and theoretical explanation.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and multimodal tasks, distillation techniques—including self-distillation, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, and teacher adaptation—enable substantial reductions in model size and compute with limited accuracy loss. KD is complementary to other compression strategies (e.g., pruning and architecture search) and benefits from careful choices in intermediate-target selection, data augmentation, and teacher-student alignment. When combined thoughtfully with task adaptation and hardware-aware techniques, KD unlocks feasible deployment of advanced models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data augmentation), and when adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. At the same time, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are matched, and how to handle domain shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, deployment-oriented strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. When integrated with representation-level objectives, layer-aware alignment, data strategies (including synthesized or privacy-preserving data), and architecture-aware search, distillation enables compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Realistic use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, task-awareness, and data or privacy limitations to avoid predictable failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables production-ready compression of large deep and language models into smaller, faster students. KD succeeds across modalities by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations, and its effectiveness increases when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design. However, realizing robust, fair, and deployable compressed models requires attention to data availability, teacher quality, representation mismatch, and targeted mitigation of undesirable transferred behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. I argue KD should occupy a central place in compression pipelines because it reliably improves size–performance tradeoffs, but it must be adapted to task- and deployment-specific constraints (data regime, privacy, robustness, and fairness) and combined with complementary techniques to deliver robust, real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved from matching softened teacher outputs to a rich toolbox that includes intermediate representation transfer, attention or relation-level objectives, data-free and online methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when its signals, data strategy, and student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. Important open problems remain around capacity mismatch, long-tail or rare-token behaviors, distribution shift, and avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled, Practical, and Context-Sensitive Toolbox for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable systems. When treated as a flexible framework rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and domain heterogeneity. However, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to adapt to new domains or architectures, and how to select or synthesize training signals for the student.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal information. Methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features or relational structure, and KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows strong practical gains across vision and NLP, but challenges remain around representation alignment, robustness, rare-token fidelity, privacy, and data heterogeneity — motivating richer distillation targets and deployment-aware pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods enable transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teachers to smaller students so models can be deployed under computation, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature shows a spectrum of approaches — from matching softened output distributions to feature- and layer-level imitation, attention-guided alignment, data-free or zero-shot synthesis of training examples, and distributed or privacy-aware protocols — and demonstrates successful applications across vision, speech, recommendation, and many NLP tasks. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distillation signal, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student architecture alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include handling imperfect teachers, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and maintaining robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Deployment Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels — from softened outputs to intermediate representations — KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its greatest practical value lies in being a flexible, composable tool: KD integrates with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet diverse deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution; careful design is required to address data scarcity and privacy, teacher–student mismatch, optimization instability, and the preservation of rare-token or long-tail behavior. Practical pipelines therefore combine task-aware distillation targets, teacher–student co-design, staged training, and robustness and fairness evaluation to realize reliable compressed systems.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The family of methods includes matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures. KD is frequently combined with orthogonal compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work across vision, speech, and language demonstrates that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost, though practical success depends on student capacity, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Why and How Knowledge Distillation Enables Practical Compression for Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained and ensemble models deliver state-of-the-art accuracy in NLP and other deep learning domains but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide principled ways to transfer predictive behaviour and internal representations from expensive teachers into compact students. When combined with careful pre-training, feature-level matching, layer-mapping strategies, data augmentation, and curriculum design, distillation yields models that approach teacher accuracy while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude or more. This paper argues that KD is both necessary and practical for deploying high-quality compact models and outlines concrete, evidence-backed strategies to maximize its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design‑Sensitive Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment objectives and combined with complementary compression methods, KD can recover most of a teacher’s utility while delivering substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy. However, distillation is context‑sensitive: the distilled signals, student capacity, data regime, and privacy or fairness constraints all shape outcomes. Treating KD as an essential but configurable toolbox—rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm—yields the most reliable production results.
