papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language, distillation techniques—ranging from softened logits to intermediate‑representation matching and architecture‑aware schedules—enable deployment under compute, latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Distillation is most effective when combined with complementary compression tools and careful data or curriculum design; open issues include capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving rare or low‑frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large, high‑capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and graph settings, KD enables substantial reductions in storage and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is a context‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When integrated into a pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning/quantization, data strategies, and robustness checks, KD is the most practical and versatile method for producing compact models suitable for real deployment.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a family of methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). These approaches aim to retain predictive performance while reducing model size, latency, or enabling deployment under privacy or communication constraints. Recent work broadens distillation beyond logits to intermediate features, attention maps, multi-teacher setups, and data-limited or privacy-preserving regimes, producing task- and domain-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision and language tasks KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate feature and layer-wise alignment, adversarial and data-free generation, and task-aware layer mapping. Empirical evidence shows KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving or improving generalization, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or absent original training data. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods and careful data or curriculum design to balance accuracy, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match the signals, data, and architectures of a given deployment, KD frequently recovers substantial teacher performance while enabling large reductions in inference cost and memory. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: it requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle limited or private data, and how to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors. Combining KD with complementary techniques (multi-teacher schedules, architecture search, pruning, or student-friendly teacher training) and addressing data and fairness constraints yields the most reliable practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, engineering-centered approach for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models. Over the last decade KD has expanded from soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-level transfers, multi-stage and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioner choices align teacher signals, student capacity, and available data. Common failure modes—capacity mismatch, distributional shift, degraded behavior on rare or long-tail phenomena, and transfer of teacher biases—motivate careful design, diagnostics, and hybrid pipelines for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for reducing the computational and memory footprint of large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Work in this area has diversified beyond the original teacher-to-student soft-label matching to include self-distillation, online and distributed distillation, feature- and representation-level transfer, multi-teacher selection, and data-augmentation-aware distillation. These methods are applied across modalities (vision, speech, NLP, and graphs) and contexts (domain adaptation, continual learning, large-scale training, and on-device deployment), yielding a range of practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and model size. Current advances emphasize richer forms of knowledge (internal representations, relational signals), adaptive teacher weighting, and training-time strategies that improve student generalization, but challenges remain in reliably transferring rare-word or low-frequency behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and scaling distillation to extremely large datasets and models.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. By transferring supervisory signals beyond hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and safeguards for fairness and robustness. I argue KD should be treated as the central organizing method in practical compression pipelines, while noting concrete failure modes and recommending principled mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high-impact strategy for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and tasks by transferring soft targets, internal representations, and relational signals; it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; and it supports production constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. When applied as a carefully designed pipeline—choosing appropriate distilled signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, and addressing data or domain gaps—KD enables pragmatic trade-offs that make compression feasible in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations, transferring attention or relational signals, staged or progressive replacement strategies, and self-distillation. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data, teacher–student, and optimization choices to meet deployment constraints. Although KD often recovers much of teacher performance, persistent limits remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token behavior, bias transfer, and data- or privacy-constrained scenarios, so engineering and diagnostics are required for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A mature toolbox has emerged that includes soft-label/logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when teacher–student alignment, training curricula, and data availability are carefully addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, potential bias transfer, and robustness under distributional shifts; nonetheless, well‑designed KD pipelines routinely produce compact models that approach teacher performance across vision, language, speech, graph, and recommendation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Limits, and Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when practitioners match what is transferred (logits, features, attention), how data are used (original, synthesized, or distilled), and how students are architected or pre-trained. However, KD is design-sensitive: realizing its benefits in production requires complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization), careful handling of low-frequency behaviors and distributional shift, and explicit mitigation of privacy and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Approaches include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, mapping or projecting teacher layers to student layers, and operating in offline, online, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and designing curricula or multi-stage pipelines that reflect deployment needs. While distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance, open challenges remain in representation mismatch, amplifying teacher biases, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and NLP, KD has evolved from soft-target matching into a flexible toolbox that includes representation-level alignment, attention and relational signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data strategies such as augmentation or synthetic/data-free generation. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful engineering to match student capacity, select appropriate signals, and manage data or privacy constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, practitioners must address failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, degraded rare-token behavior, and propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention-based signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and when tuned for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch between teacher and student, preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors, transferred biases and brittleness, and distillation under data- or heterogeneity-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from high-capacity teachers to compact students via outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment workflows (on-device inference, federated learning, and data-limited regimes). While KD reliably improves efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance, robust application requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers and low-frequency behaviors, and how to combine KD with data strategies and architecture design to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully and combined with complementary techniques—layer- and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis or privacy-aware protocols, and hardware-aware downstream optimization—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's utility. However, its practical success is engineering-dependent: careful choices about distilled signals, student preparation, data availability, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases are required to realize reliable, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context-Sensitive for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can be applied across modalities and settings to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and serve as a core component of broader compression pipelines. However, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, data regimes, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Modern distillation expands beyond matching teacher logits to include intermediate representation matching, self-supervised and contrastive objectives, data-free and synthetic-data schemes, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- and deployment-aware protocols. These variants enable application across vision, speech, graph-structured data, and NLP, but practical deployment requires care about data availability, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from one or more teacher models into smaller students so they retain much of the teacher’s capabilities with lower compute, memory, or latency. The literature spans a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and common integrations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pre-training of compact models). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and inductive biases, what data to use (or synthesize), and constraints around deployment, privacy, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Cervantes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models that retain much of large-teacher performance. KD supports multiple transfer signals and workflows, composes effectively with orthogonal compression tools, and is adaptable to privacy- and deployment-sensitive contexts. Its real-world success depends on matching distilled signals and curricula to student capacity, combining KD with pruning/quantization or architecture design when appropriate, and explicitly addressing risks such as propagated biases, optimization mismatches, and long-tail or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, production-oriented approach that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a composable component within wider compression pipelines, KD enables effective trade-offs among accuracy, size, and deployment constraints; however, its practical success depends on careful design choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as distribution shift, bias transfer, and rare-token loss.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an engineering-centered, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teacher models. KD encompasses a range of signals (soft labels, intermediate representations, relational targets), training schedules (multi-stage, online, self-distillation), and data practices (original data, augmentation, or data-free synthesis). Its practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity and deployment constraints, and on combining KD with complementary compression methods when necessary. KD also acts beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve generalization and robustness, but it can propagate teacher imperfections and is sensitive to data and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Mechanisms, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable, engineering‑focused technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through multiple complementary mechanisms — transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure — and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, practical success requires careful alignment of teacher signals to student capacity, attention to data regimes and privacy, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, and generative settings shows KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployability costs. Best results arise when KD is combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher–student design, data-aware strategies (including augmentation or synthetic data), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). KD has clear limits — e.g., it can transfer undesirable teacher behaviors, struggle with rare-token or data-mismatch regimes, and interact with privacy constraints — so production use requires principled pipelines that mitigate these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger pretrained or ensemble teachers in deep learning and NLP. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and aligning teacher and student architectures — KD recovers much of the teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioners explicitly guard against capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, and the propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring predictive and representational information from large ‘teacher’ models into smaller ‘student’ models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate representation imitation, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, and data strategies including synthetic or data-free approaches. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though limits remain around domain shift, rare-token behavior, robustness, and the propagation of teacher shortcomings.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Reynolds
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature treats KD as both a compression mechanism and a training paradigm: it leverages richer supervision than hard labels, integrates with complementary compression methods, and requires careful matching of distilled signals, student capacity, and data regimes to succeed in practice. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but persistent challenges remain around domain shift, rare-token behavior, bias transfer, and data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. Best practices emphasize choosing what to transfer (soft logits, features, attention, relations), aligning teacher and student representations, using data-aware or data-free workflows as appropriate, and composing KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design to meet deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to student capacity, data availability, and task constraints, KD can yield large reductions in latency, memory, and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher's performance. Its practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, integrating complementary compression techniques, and addressing data- and distribution-related limitations through task-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under storage, latency, and privacy constraints. The literature converges on a taxonomy of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, self-distillation), and data strategies (original data, augmented or synthetic data, and data-free approaches). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when matched to student capacity, but success depends on choices about distillation signals, layer alignment, data availability, and complementary compression tools. Open challenges include preserving robustness under distribution shift, handling low-frequency phenomena, and aligning heterogeneous architectures, motivating task-aware pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-label matching and richer forms of transfer — intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data approaches, and online or mutual distillation. In practice, KD is most effective when its signal, data strategy, and architectural alignment are chosen with the task and deployment constraints in mind and when distillation is combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Despite strong empirical gains across modalities, limitations remain: teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and degradation on rare or low-frequency behaviors can reduce fidelity and robustness, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach has expanded from soft-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, self-distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical deployments succeed when distillation objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and task-aware choices are tuned to the application; remaining challenges include preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, handling distribution shift and data scarcity, and ensuring robustness and privacy in deployed students.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used framework for compressing large, high‑performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure), and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as capacity mismatch, robustness degradation, privacy leakage, and poor long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary component of practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it offers a flexible set of transfer signals and training regimes that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. However, KD is not a turnkey solution — its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When designers adopt representation-aware objectives, layer mappings, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit mitigation for capacity mismatch and long-tail behaviors, KD yields compact, deployable models that balance fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and NLP, KD has evolved from soft-target matching into a flexible toolbox that includes representation-level alignment, attention and relational signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data strategies such as augmentation or synthetic/data-free generation. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful engineering to match student capacity, select appropriate signals, and manage data or privacy constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, practitioners must address failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, degraded rare-token behavior, and propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across NLP and other deep learning domains. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling faster inference, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment; however, it has failure modes related to data dependence, teacher quality, and rare-token fidelity. Effective use of KD therefore treats it as a toolbox—combining multi-teacher schedules, data-aware augmentation, representation-level objectives, and privacy-aware protocols—to produce robust, task-appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, faster models that retain much of the capability of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit matching, modern KD leverages internal representation transfer, selective data strategies, and integration with pruning, architecture search, or federated protocols to meet latency, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables efficient deployment across modalities while posing clear methodological trade-offs and open challenges that guide future research.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central element of practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but it is not a standalone cure: to produce deployable, robust, and fair students practitioners must combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, architecture search, quantization), data- and curriculum-driven training, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias. This integrated approach yields efficient models suited to real-world constraints while managing known distillation failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on task, data availability, optimization choices, and robustness or fairness requirements. Practical deployment requires tailored curricula, representation-aware objectives, and integration with methods like pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Reyes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic, flexible pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. As a composable toolset rather than a single recipe, KD transfers soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational signals; composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; and can be adapted for multi-teacher, data-limited, and privacy-aware regimes. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, designing layer-aware objectives and curricula, and mitigating known failure modes such as data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, robustness degradation, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Costa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox that includes softened-output (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention-guided imitation, layer-wise and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data strategies ranging from use of original labels to synthetic or data-free curricula. KD often works best when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and when the distillation recipe is tuned for student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints. Practical challenges include handling imperfect teachers, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, alignment of teacher and student representations, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for shrinking large models into deployable students. KD is flexible in what it transfers (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), interoperates with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and supports privacy- or data-constrained settings via synthesized or data-free protocols. However, KD is engineering-dependent: realizing its benefits requires matching distillation signals to student capacity and deployment goals, addressing optimization and distributional mismatches, and mitigating risks like propagated biases or degraded long‑tail/rare‑token behavior. I argue KD should be treated as the central tool in compression pipelines, but only when used with targeted practices and safeguards tailored to the task and operational constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students. When applied beyond naive soft-label matching—by transferring intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, using multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and combining distillation with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search)—KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world success requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data regimes (including synthetic or public-data strategies), and robustness or fairness concerns; with those caveats, KD is an indispensable component of production compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: The Case for Versatile Knowledge Distillation: Compression, Adaptation, and Robustness in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and flexible paradigm for transferring information from large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple logit matching, distillation techniques can be adapted to operate without original training data, guide architecture search, improve generalization under limited data, support cross-modal and multi-task transfer, and preserve or even enhance downstream performance on specialized tasks. When combined with task-aware search, feature-level imitation, and data augmentation strategies, distillation enables deployment of compact models that remain competitive with their teachers while meeting real-world constraints such as privacy, compute, and latency.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from one or more high-capacity teachers. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft output distributions, intermediate features, relational structure) and how the transfer is scheduled or combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture modification). KD has enabled substantial reductions in model size and latency across vision and language tasks while retaining much of teacher performance, but its empirical success depends on student capacity, choice of distillation signals, data availability (or synthetic-data methods), and careful engineering to address optimization mismatch, distribution shift, and potential transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Data Regimes, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or data/privacy constraints. Over the last decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching into diverse objectives and workflows — including feature- and layer-wise matching, self- and online-distillation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and task-aware layer mapping — that together form practical compression toolkits across vision and NLP. Effective distillation depends on careful choice of transferred signals, data strategy, and alignment between teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad set of techniques has been developed — matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, mapping teacher layers to student layers, and operating in online, offline, multi-teacher, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is typically combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data, selective sampling). In practice, distillation often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory, but its success depends on student capacity, representation alignment, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers knowledge from larger, often ensemble or teacher models into smaller student models to enable efficient deployment and improved generalization under resource constraints. Techniques range from matching final soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging self-supervision, adversarial objectives, or curriculum and sample selection strategies. Distillation has been applied across classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and structured prediction, and it also offers avenues to transfer inductive biases, improve robustness, and preserve privacy. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when distillation helps, what kind of "dark knowledge" is useful, and how regularization-like effects of soft targets can be harnessed even without a superior teacher.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Toolbox Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables preservation of much of a teacher's capabilities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing that potential requires combining multiple transfer signals, designing student-aware architectures and curricula, and accounting for data- and deployment-specific constraints; it also requires awareness of limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Research and practice show a spectrum of distillation signals and workflows that make KD a flexible foundation of modern compression pipelines, but its success depends on task-aware signal selection, student design, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques span teacher design, student-teacher layer mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-aware and data-free workflows, and scalable/online training protocols. When combined with task-aware selection and domain adaptation, distillation enables effective deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and heterogeneous-device constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bowen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Power, Limits, and Responsible Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and can be combined with other compression tools to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and careful engineering to avoid degraded performance on rare or out-of-domain behaviors. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as the central mechanism but pairs it with curriculum design, multi-teacher strategies, representation alignment, and orthogonal compression methods while explicitly validating robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature frames distillation as a multifaceted toolkit — including soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols — that is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and data constraints, and on explicitly addressing failure modes such as transferred biases, optimization mismatch, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Careful, and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints; supports domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization; and can be combined with other compression techniques. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align layers and representations, how to generate or augment data for distillation, and how to mitigate propagated errors or biases from teachers.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression and fairness-preserving techniques. I argue that KD should be treated as a central component of a model-compression pipeline — one that is combined with architecture-aware methods, data and curriculum strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias — to achieve deployable, efficient, and responsible models in practice.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Methods extend beyond matching soft output logits to include intermediate feature/representation matching, layer-wise alignment, adversarial or curriculum-driven sample selection, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Distillation is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, language, multimodal) and use cases (on-device deployment, federated learning, low-precision inference), but success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to handle data availability or heterogeneity, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core, context-aware component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary tools — pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies — KD enables meaningful reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive performance. Success depends on explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or privacy-sensitive data, and how to measure robustness and long-tail behavior; a principled, deployment-aware distillation pipeline yields the best tradeoffs between efficiency and utility.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Deployable NLP: Power, Patterns, and Pitfalls
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic route to shrinking large NLP models into deployable students that retain much of their teachers' performance. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables real-world tradeoffs among accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy. Realizing those gains requires pairing KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and targeted diagnostics to address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and rare-token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.
