papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models to smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer objectives that align intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and it is commonly combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization. Success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, student capacity, training data (including synthesized or distilled datasets), and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. This article synthesizes core methods, empirical patterns, and practical recommendations that guide the use of KD in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller ‘‘student’’ models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing storage and inference cost. Distillation spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer forms that align intermediate features, attention maps, or decision-boundary information; practical deployments combine distillation with architecture-aware choices, selective data strategies, and complementary compression methods. The method is effective across vision and language tasks but has limits stemming from imperfect teachers, capacity mismatch, and data or distributional heterogeneity; careful method design and evaluation are required to realize robust, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD methods—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to feature- and relation-level imitation—work across modalities and tasks and integrate naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, maximizing KD’s benefits requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; left unaddressed, challenges such as representation misalignment, degraded rare-token behavior, and robustness or privacy losses can limit gains.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models so they meet constraints on latency, memory, and privacy while retaining much of teacher performance. KD operates at multiple granularities (soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Its effectiveness depends on choices about transfer targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (including synthesized or teacher-generated data), and explicit mitigation for robustness, privacy, and distributional or low-frequency failures.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed models (teachers) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models (students). KD has been used to (1) transfer inductive biases across architectures, (2) compress large pretrained language and vision models into task- or deployment-aware students, (3) combine and condense ensembles into single models, (4) enable privacy- or data-constrained distillation, and (5) improve student generalization via richer supervision beyond hard labels. Practical KD systems balance fidelity to the teacher, student capacity and architecture, data availability, privacy constraints, and deployment budgets; recent work addresses these trade-offs through architecture search, meta-learning teachers, multi-teacher designs, data-free synthesis, and specialized intermediate-feature matching losses. Despite broad empirical success, theoretical work highlights conditions where soft labels help (and when hard labels correct imperfect teachers), pointing to ongoing research directions in teacher design, student architecture search, privacy guarantees, and robust data-efficient distillation.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Duarte
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables large gains in inference efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression techniques and task‑aware engineering. However, KD is not a silver bullet: success depends on what is distilled, how teacher and student are matched, how data or privacy constraints are handled, and how robustness and fairness are evaluated and mitigated.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically effective approach for producing compact models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When framed as a central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques and data strategies, KD yields strong size–performance trade-offs while enabling domain adaptation and robustness improvements. However, realizing those benefits in production requires careful design choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to diagnose and mitigate transferred biases and rare-case degradation.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Practical Benefits and Cautions of Knowledge Distillation for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. When applied thoughtfully—using techniques such as data augmentation, multi-teacher training, teacher optimization, or data-free procedures—KD can preserve much of the teacher's utility while reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation can transfer or amplify undesirable properties of teachers (e.g., biases), and its success depends on choices like which teacher knowledge to transfer and which training samples to use. I argue KD is a powerful tool for NLP model compression but must be combined with targeted strategies for robustness, fairness, privacy, and sample selection to realize its full benefits in practice.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention-based signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and when tuned for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch between teacher and student, preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors, transferred biases and brittleness, and distillation under data- or heterogeneity-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practitioner-oriented technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones suitable for deployment. When paired with complementary methods (architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data augmentation, and privacy-aware protocols), KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to source or synthesize data, how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, and how to evaluate robustness and social harms under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible technique for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact student models. When combined with feature-level objectives, architectural transformations, teacher optimization, and data strategies, KD can recover much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on task and domain specifics, teacher quality, student capacity, and data availability; therefore, practitioners should treat KD as a toolbox to be adapted—not a single recipe—to obtain reliable compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD is applied across modalities and deployment contexts to reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines combine choice of distillation target, teacher and student preparation, data strategies, and complementary compression methods to meet constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. While KD is highly effective in many settings, it has known limits—capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and transferred biases—that require careful method and evaluation design.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, ensembling or self-teaching, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints, but effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signals, data and augmentations, teacher–student alignment, and task-aware pipeline design.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and NLP, effective KD combines multiple transfer signals and pipeline choices so compact models approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical KD is design-sensitive: benefits depend on teacher preparation, student capacity, data handling (including synthetic or data-free methods), and complementary compression techniques; remaining challenges include distribution shift, long-tail behaviors, and the risk of propagating teacher imperfections.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely one technique among many for model compression: when applied thoughtfully it is a central, practical lever for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance, robustness, and task-specific behavior of large teachers. Best practice couples KD with representation-level supervision, teacher-student co-design, data and privacy strategies, and complementary compression methods so that compact models meet real-world latency, memory and heterogeneity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. KD expands beyond matching teacher soft labels to include intermediate-representation and relational matching, multi-stage or online training regimes, and data strategies that range from using original training data to synthetic or data‑free approaches. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign) and careful engineering of teacher–student alignment and data curricula, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Key open problems include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving long‑tail or rare behaviors, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under severe data or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a central, flexible component of model‑compression pipelines rather than as a single canned technique. By transferring richer forms of supervision (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational or attention signals) and by being combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD enables deployment of compact models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful distillation requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. When applied with task‑aware design and safeguards against optimization and bias failure modes, KD provides a practical road for compressing large models for real‑world NLP and deep‑learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is empirically effective across modalities because it transfers richer signals than hard labels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational cues) and composes with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). However, KD is engineering-dependent: data availability, teacher quality, and student–teacher mismatch create failure modes that require task-aware choices. A pragmatic compression pipeline treats KD as one component among data strategies, architecture adaptation, and hardware-aware tuning to achieve reliable, high-fidelity compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Pillar for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables deployment on resource-limited devices, supports privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, and combines effectively with pre-training, data augmentation, and structured compression. I argue that KD should be a default component of any production-aware model compression pipeline, augmented by task- and data-aware techniques to preserve robustness and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, graph, and speech tasks, KD variants (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational transfer, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware procedures) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair KD with pretraining, sample-selection, and complementary compression techniques to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; however, challenges remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, multi-stage or online schemes) and composes well with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints. KD enables many deployment goals (reduced latency/memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training), but its effectiveness is limited by optimization dynamics, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift for synthetic data, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Engineering-Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer outputs, intermediate representations, relationships, or curricula and supports data-free, multi-teacher, and online variants. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation) and careful teacher–student alignment, KD reliably reduces inference cost and storage while often preserving generalization. However, its success depends on design choices—what to transfer, how to handle limited or private data, and how to align capacities and optimization—so KD should be treated as a core component of a compression pipeline rather than a plug-and-play remedy.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. A rich set of practical variants has emerged — from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or synthesized-data approaches — and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and deployment-aware design. Remaining challenges include optimization mismatch between teacher and student, distribution shift, rare-token or low-frequency behavior degradation, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to build students and teachers, and how to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. When engineered carefully—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD yields large efficiency gains while preserving most task performance. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data and curriculum choices, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a dominant approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It operates by transferring information from a teacher to a student using a variety of signals and workflows, and it is routinely combined with other compression techniques to meet practical latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teachers performance, its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability or synthesis of data, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, context‑sensitive mechanism in practical model compression. When carefully designed and combined with complementary tools — pruning, quantization, architecture search, synthetic or privacy‑aware data, and task‑aware curricula — KD produces compact models that retain much of a teacher’s performance across modalities and deployment constraints. However, KD is not automatic: success requires explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate harmful teacher behaviors. A principled KD pipeline that adapts to task, data, and hardware needs yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and utility.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Effective compression in practice requires matching the distillation technique to the deployment objective: using self-distillation or multi-teacher strategies to extract richer supervisory signals, combining KD with architecture search or pruning for task-specific efficiency, applying appropriate soft/hard label mixing informed by bias–variance tradeoffs, and controlling data and privacy considerations during distillation. When these elements are combined, KD can deliver substantial runtime and memory savings with minimal accuracy loss, making it central to deploying modern NLP systems under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Versatile Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and powerful approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple size reduction, KD enables transfer of capabilities across modalities, supports domain adaptation, improves deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and can be adapted to distributed training. However, benefits are not automatic: careful design of teacher-student alignment, training data, and distillation objectives is required to preserve task performance and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical backbone for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and supporting multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines—that, when combined with complementary techniques and context-aware design, yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. Realizing KD’s value in production requires explicit handling of teacher imperfections, student capacity, data regimes, and robustness and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Mcdaniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables preservation of much of a teacher’s capabilities while meeting real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and power. Its practical value comes from the variety of signals it can transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure), the ability to combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), and adaptability to data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires deliberate engineering: matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing distributional and rare-token failures, and integrating KD into broader compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Engineering Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities, but it is design-sensitive: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or domain shifts determine outcomes. Framing KD as the central tool within a broader compression pipeline — combined with feature-level objectives, multi-teacher or data-synthesis strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) — leads to more reliable and deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Beyond Compression to Fairness, Robustness, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to compress large models into smaller, faster students, but its potential extends much further. When applied thoughtfully—via feature-level mimicking, progressive module replacement, teacher selection and confidence-weighting, and by combining with automated search or divergence choices—KD can improve fairness, domain adaptation, generative model compression, and student robustness while preserving or even improving task performance. This essay argues that KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that should be matched to specific goals (efficiency, fairness, transferability, or generation), and gives concrete methodological recommendations informed by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and NLP, distillation transfers softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and training dynamics; it is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-aware data) to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and curricula, and evaluating robustness and fairness. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance and enables on-device or low-cost deployment, it also faces limits such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token degradation, and the danger of transferring teacher biases or errors.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. When applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline it reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Achieving robust, fair, and private deployments requires combining KD with architecture-aware design, appropriate data strategies (including data-free alternatives), careful choice of distilled signals, and systematic evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Engineering Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive behavior and representations while reducing latency, memory, and sometimes improving generalization in resource-constrained or domain-specific settings. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of distilled signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and attention to robustness, rare-token fidelity, and privacy. Best results come from treating KD as a central but composable component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses architecture-aware design, data curricula, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high‑impact route to compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques—feature alignment, data strategies, projector or adversarial mechanisms, and hardware‑aware design—it achieves strong size/accuracy/latency tradeoffs. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose limits such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and rare‑token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: French
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The approach spans matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and staged or online teacher–student schedules. KD is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or privacy-aware protocols), and complementary compression techniques such as pruning or quantization. Practical deployment requires addressing capacity mismatch, data or distributional shift, and the risk of propagating teacher errors; when these are handled, KD produces compact models that often retain much of the teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Design-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and reliably improves student performance under resource constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: real-world deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including data-free or domain-adaptive approaches), and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to address capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. When engineered as part of a broader compression pipeline—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning student architectures, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or low-precision training—distillation enables large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on careful choices about distilled signals, data regimes, and mitigation of teacher or distributional failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller ones that meet deployment constraints. KD reduces storage, latency, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher signals are generated and trusted, and how distillation is combined with other compression methods and fairness or robustness constraints. Effective deployment requires task-aware decisions about targets (logits vs. features), data (original, augmented, or synthetic), architectural alignment, and additional safeguards for bias and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible set of techniques for producing compact models that retain much of the behavior of larger, expensive teachers. Across vision, language, and other modalities, practitioners transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate-feature supervision, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher ensembles, and architectural or data-aware strategies. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression tools (e.g., architecture search, quantization, pruning) and when distillation signals, data strategies, and optimization schedules are aligned to deployment constraints. Important open problems remain — including robustness on rare phenomena, domain shift, privacy and data-limited regimes, and theoretical limits of transfer — but pragmatic pipelines that combine KD variants with deployment-aware design choices are the most reliable route to high-quality compact models.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical suite of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates by transferring richer supervision than hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). While KD routinely yields strong reductions in inference cost and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and deployment constraints and on mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on rare events, and sensitivity to distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable student models. KD techniques range from classic teacher-to-student soft-target training to recent advances including data-free distillation, multi-teacher strategies, meta-learned teachers, and compression combined with pruning or structural sparsity. In NLP applications KD is used to shrink pre-trained transformers, accelerate inference for production systems, enable non-autoregressive generation, and adapt large models to resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while producing models with far lower latency and storage cost, but theoretical understanding, sensitivity to data and teacher quality, and robustness under distributional shifts remain active research areas.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s utility under resource constraints, realizing its benefits in production requires deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred errors and biases. A pragmatic KD pipeline combines soft-target matching with representation-level supervision, architecture-aware adaptation, and complementary compression methods to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Mechanisms, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable, engineering‑focused technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through multiple complementary mechanisms — transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure — and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, practical success requires careful alignment of teacher signals to student capacity, attention to data regimes and privacy, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated via soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data-aware schemes. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data or augmentation choices, KD frequently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Practical success requires tailoring distillation signals, addressing teacher–student capacity and representation mismatches, and attending to data quality and distributional issues.
