papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, transferring intermediate representations or relational signals, and using teacher ensembles or self-distillation. Its effectiveness depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to supply or synthesize training data; when combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD forms the core of pragmatic compression pipelines. Despite strong empirical successes, open challenges remain in bias and error propagation from teachers, handling rare or low-frequency phenomena, robustness under domain shift, and distillation under data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses behavioral and representational knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature presents a broad toolbox—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and meta-distillation, data-free or data-scarce strategies, and layer- or relation-focused transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical and conceptual work shows KD can also regularize students and sometimes improve generalization or robustness, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student capacities are aligned, and how data (real, augmented, or synthesized) are used. Open issues include distribution shift, rare-token behavior in sequence models, privacy constraints, and principled objectives for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. When combined with representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware strategies, and architecture-aware design, KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency. Its effectiveness depends on careful handling of data availability, teacher-student mismatch, and ethical or robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing neural models to smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A spectrum of distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), training regimes (data-driven, data-free, federated, self-distillation), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) has been developed to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints in vision and language applications. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance while enabling substantial runtime and size improvements, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and optimization. Open problems include handling distribution shift, rare-token behavior, teacher–student mismatch, and robust/fair transfer under heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: robust, fair, and private compression requires careful choice of distilled signals, layer/representation alignment, data strategies (including synthesis or privacy-aware protocols), and combination with complementary methods like pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The KD toolkit ranges from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and it is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines with pruning, quantization, and student-aware architecture design. Practical success depends on careful engineering choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, which data to use or synthesize, and how to diagnose and mitigate limits such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and distribution shift. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher utility across vision, language, and domain-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Duarte
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables large gains in inference efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression techniques and task‑aware engineering. However, KD is not a silver bullet: success depends on what is distilled, how teacher and student are matched, how data or privacy constraints are handled, and how robustness and fairness are evaluated and mitigated.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a highly practical, versatile technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller students that retain much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary compression primitives and designed for the student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields deployable models with substantially lower latency and memory. However, KD is not a universal cure: effectiveness depends on what is distilled, how data (real or synthetic) are used, and how risks such as bias transfer, robustness loss, and privacy exposure are managed. I argue KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines but applied with explicit mitigations and task‑aware engineering.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision, language, and generative domains, methods range from matching teacher soft targets to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols. Practical pipelines commonly combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and attention to robustness and fairness; these trade-offs guide ongoing research and engineering practice.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field encompasses a range of techniques—from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals—and integrates with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, the availability and curation of data (real or synthesized), and deployment constraints such as latency, memory, robustness, and privacy. Persistent challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and ensuring generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer signals than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure—KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while recovering much of a teacher’s performance. Effective deployment treats KD as a component of a broader compression pipeline: select the appropriate distilled signals, align teacher and student architectures, use data-aware or data-free strategies as needed, and combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware pretraining. KD succeeds widely but has known failure modes—teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token fidelity loss, and bias transfer—that require principled engineering, diagnostics, and complementary techniques to address.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become core methods for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, practitioners compress models by transferring teacher behavior to smaller students, by architectural replacement, or by searching for task-specific compact architectures. Techniques differ in what is transferred (logits, intermediate representations, inter-class relations), how training data are used (original data, distilled targets, or synthetic data), and how robustness and task-specificity are preserved. Empirical work shows strong trade-offs between model size, runtime, and task performance; recent advances focus on task-adaptive compression, improved layer-mapping, data-free approaches, and preserving robustness under adversarial or distributional shifts. Important open challenges remain in handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous teacher ensembles, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Paradigm: Beyond Compression to Adaptation, Robustness, and Inclusive Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) began as a technique to compress large models into smaller, faster ones. Over the past decade it has matured into a flexible training paradigm that can shape student behavior via soft targets, intermediate feature alignment, and multi-teacher or self-teaching schemes. When designed with task, data, and deployment constraints in mind, KD can enable domain specialization, interpretability, privacy-friendly federated learning, and improved robustness while still supporting efficient inference.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods reduce the computational and memory cost of large neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller students. Approaches vary from using soft logits to matching internal representations, attention maps, or generator outputs; they have been adapted for modality transfer, privacy- or bandwidth-constrained settings, and specialized architectures (e.g., transformers, GANs). Empirical work shows that representation-level objectives, architectural design of the student/bridge modules, and careful training protocols can preserve most of the teacher’s performance while dramatically reducing size and runtime. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, deploying under strict privacy/bandwidth constraints, and automating architecture search for compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. It succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (e.g., softened logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals), and by combining with complementary techniques (pruning, low-precision inference, architecture search, and data augmentation). KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to adapt teachers and students to deployment constraints. Thoughtful design — including feature-level transfer, curriculum or selective-sample strategies, augmentation, and data-free synthesis when needed — makes KD a practical cornerstone of model compression for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. The field has diversified from logits-only matching to richer targets (intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), multiple training regimes (data-free, online, federated, multi-teacher), and task-aware techniques that address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. KD is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, multimodal, graphs, NLP) and is most effective when combined with data- and architecture-aware practices, but practical limits remain around representation alignment, rare-token behavior, privacy, and domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible, and production-ready family of techniques that enables large deep and language models to be compressed into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with complementary methods—representation matching, multi-teacher or online schemes, synthetic or data-free generation, and hardware-aware compression—KD delivers strong efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on careful pipeline design to address capacity mismatch, dataset or domain heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring or amplifying teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully and combined with complementary techniques—layer- and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis or privacy-aware protocols, and hardware-aware downstream optimization—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's utility. However, its practical success is engineering-dependent: careful choices about distilled signals, student preparation, data availability, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases are required to realize reliable, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Barker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD spans soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer-wise objectives, and data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches). When combined with architecture-aware choices, pruning/quantization, and task- or data-aware training curricula, KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, its benefits are contingent on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy; KD should therefore be treated as a core, composable element of compression pipelines rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high-impact strategy for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and tasks by transferring soft targets, internal representations, and relational signals; it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; and it supports production constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. When applied as a carefully designed pipeline—choosing appropriate distilled signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, and addressing data or domain gaps—KD enables pragmatic trade-offs that make compression feasible in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Modern distillation expands beyond matching teacher logits to include intermediate representation matching, self-supervised and contrastive objectives, data-free and synthetic-data schemes, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- and deployment-aware protocols. These variants enable application across vision, speech, graph-structured data, and NLP, but practical deployment requires care about data availability, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Mcguire
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, and especially NLP, distillation operates at multiple granularities — softened output distributions, intermediate feature or attention alignment, and relational or module-level transfers — and is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and student pretraining. While distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s utility in a fraction of the compute or memory cost, practical deployment requires addressing capacity mismatch, data- and domain-shift, rare-token degradation, and propagation of teacher biases through careful method choice and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, and its effectiveness depends on matching distillation techniques to data and deployment constraints. When combined with careful model and data design, KD enables practical deployment of advanced models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Efficient Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a pragmatic and versatile set of techniques to compress large neural models into compact, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and vision, modern distillation variants — including multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, teacher optimization, and task-aware layer alignment — address core challenges such as capacity gaps and task-specific redundancy. When combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, low-precision arithmetic, architecture search), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under tight resource or latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved from matching softened teacher outputs to a rich toolbox that includes intermediate representation transfer, attention or relation-level objectives, data-free and online methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when its signals, data strategy, and student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. Important open problems remain around capacity mismatch, long-tail or rare-token behaviors, distribution shift, and avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—using richer targets than logits, aligning intermediate representations, and combining with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search—KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of a teacher's performance. KD also adapts to constrained settings (few-shot, federated, or data-free) and supports robustness and domain adaptation when pipelines are designed to match task and deployment constraints. Realizing KD's full value requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Modern KD spans matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, layerwise and relational losses, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Empirical practice shows KD recovers much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design), careful data and curriculum choices, and explicit handling of capacity, optimization, and distribution-shift failure modes. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended workflows for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive capacity from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research over the past decade has expanded simple logit-matching into a rich set of variants—feature and layer alignment, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and privacy-aware ensembles—making KD a cornerstone of modern model-compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Armstrong
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to include intermediate-representation and attention transfer, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, data-aware curricula, and combinations with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher’s utility across vision and language when its signals, data, and student capacity are chosen deliberately; remaining challenges center on capacity mismatch, distribution shift, robustness, fairness, and data- or privacy-limited regimes. Best practices emphasize aligning distilled signals with student capacity, using pre-training for compact students, and integrating KD with complementary compression techniques for deployment.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can be applied across modalities and settings to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and serve as a core component of broader compression pipelines. However, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, data regimes, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals from a higher-capacity teacher to a compact student, KD enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of the original performance. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under storage, latency, and privacy constraints. The literature converges on a taxonomy of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, self-distillation), and data strategies (original data, augmented or synthetic data, and data-free approaches). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when matched to student capacity, but success depends on choices about distillation signals, layer alignment, data availability, and complementary compression tools. Open challenges include preserving robustness under distribution shift, handling low-frequency phenomena, and aligning heterogeneous architectures, motivating task-aware pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the most practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, language, and other modalities. When applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), designing teacher-student pairs, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) — distillation recovers much of a teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD also serves beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve robustness and generalization, but it is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization differences, and risks of transferring biases or vulnerability must be managed through targeted practices and evaluations.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Methods range from matching softened logits to imitating internal representations, attention maps, or channel-wise activations, and can be combined with quantization, low-precision numerics, architecture-aware design, and data- or teacher-aware training regimes. In practice, distillation is a multifaceted toolkit that must be tailored to deployment goals (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness), and remaining challenges include principled sample selection, representation alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths come from flexibility in what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, optimization signals), its compatibility with architecture search and other compression primitives, and its ability to operate under constrained or private-data scenarios. KD is not a one-size-fits-all remedy: practitioners should select KD variants and complementary techniques guided by task requirements, data availability, and deployment constraints to balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and language tasks, KD transfers information from teachers to students using softened outputs, intermediate representations, or auxiliary signals; it is commonly combined with data augmentation, architecture adaptation, and privacy-preserving or data-free procedures. When applied with care to teacher signals, data selection, and student capacity, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s performance, but meaningful limitations remain (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases) that must be managed in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Careful, and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints; supports domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization; and can be combined with other compression techniques. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align layers and representations, how to generate or augment data for distillation, and how to mitigate propagated errors or biases from teachers.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The approach spans simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, and it is commonly combined with other compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture simplification) and data strategies (public or synthesized data, selective sampling). KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to prepare data, and how to mitigate teacher imperfections and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Duarte
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables large gains in inference efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression techniques and task‑aware engineering. However, KD is not a silver bullet: success depends on what is distilled, how teacher and student are matched, how data or privacy constraints are handled, and how robustness and fairness are evaluated and mitigated.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When framed as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output transfer with intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies, teacher-aware optimization, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design)—KD enables deployment of high-performing, smaller models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity, attention to data and distributional issues, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and rare-token failures.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, production-oriented approach that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a composable component within wider compression pipelines, KD enables effective trade-offs among accuracy, size, and deployment constraints; however, its practical success depends on careful design choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as distribution shift, bias transfer, and rare-token loss.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models by transferring information from larger teacher models, enabling deployment under computation, memory, or latency constraints. Across vision, speech, language, and recommendation systems, KD takes many forms — logit matching, feature mimicking, ensemble compression, and data-free synthesis — and is often combined with model pruning, architectural simplification, or curriculum strategies. Effective distillation requires choices about what to transfer (soft targets vs. intermediate features), how to supply or synthesize data, and how to schedule or regularize training; these choices shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive power from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or more private student models while retaining most of the original performance. Work across vision and language has expanded KD beyond simple logit matching into data-centric methods (augmentation and mixup), layer- and representation-level transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, data-free and privacy-aware distillation, and unified pipelines that combine pruning or structural compression with distillation. The field blends empirical engineering (speed/size trade-offs) with emerging theoretical analyses that help explain when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that high performance can be retained under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across modalities KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer transfers of internal features, attention, or relational structure, and it is usually combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthetic, or data-free). Empirical results show large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest accuracy loss in many settings, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models across NLP and vision domains. When adapted to task and deployment constraints—via multi-teacher schedules, feature-level objectives, data-free synthesis, online protocols, or privacy-aware ensembles—KD both preserves quality and addresses communication, privacy, and compute bottlenecks. However, KD is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity and optimization mismatches can limit its effectiveness, so careful method selection and engineering are required for robust compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Villarreal
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of training paradigms that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. The literature frames KD as a multi-signal toolbox (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and frequent integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign). Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, handling available data (real, public, or synthesized), and adapting objectives and schedules to deployment constraints; open challenges remain in robustness, distributional shift, low-frequency behaviors, and the transfer of teacher biases.
