papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large models and transfer knowledge across models, modalities, and tasks. Practitioners use KD to produce smaller, faster student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, to regularize training via self-distillation, and to enable multi-task or resource-heterogeneous deployment. Despite strong empirical results across vision, speech, translation, and question answering, distillation exhibits failure modes—e.g., propagation of teacher errors or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena—that motivate variants such as multi-teacher schemes, feature-level objectives, projector layers, and teacher-student co-training. The literature combines empirical recipes and growing theoretical analysis to guide when and how to mix soft teacher signals and hard labels, design teacher architectures, and choose representation vs. logit distillation for best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical center of model compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably yields compact, lower-latency models while retaining much of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on deployment context. Best outcomes arise when KD is paired with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), careful choice of distillation signals, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used set of techniques to transfer behavior from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" models so they can run with lower latency, memory, and cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. The field has diversified from simple logit-matching into a broad toolkit that includes feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, data-free or synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle data and domain mismatch, and how to address optimization and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves substantial teacher utility across vision and NLP, but theoretical and empirical analyses also highlight optimization limits, capacity- and distribution-mismatch risks, and the importance of pre-training and task-aware design for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models by transferring information from a teacher to a smaller student so the student preserves much of the teacher’s behavior while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature shows a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and many practical integrations (pre-training compact students, combining with pruning/quantization, and curriculum or data selection). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability and selection of data, and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include capacity/optimization mismatch, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce settings.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students so systems meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets — softened logits, intermediate features and attention maps, relational structure, and iterative or multi-teacher curricula — and complementary methods such as pruning, layer skipping, module replacement, and data synthesis. Practical success depends on aligning what is transferred to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with architecture-aware design and validation to avoid optimization mismatches and unwanted bias transfer. Remaining gaps include robustness under domain shift, principled selection of distilled signals, and theoretical accounts that predict when KD will provide large gains.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. Across vision, language, and cross-modal tasks, KD is used both as a stand-alone compression method and in combination with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical strategies include logit (soft-label) matching, feature-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or label-synthesis when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows that distillation can recover most of a teacher's performance while enabling much smaller and faster models, but outcomes depend strongly on choices such as teacher quality, the form of distilled signals, augmentation and synthetic-data generation, and whether low-precision or domain-specific constraints apply.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Representation- and Deployment-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable core of compression pipelines and extended beyond logits to internal representations and deployment constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Effective application requires careful teacher/student design, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD serves as a flexible training paradigm that can be combined with pre-training, privacy-preserving workflows, and architecture-aware mimicry to preserve task performance while meeting latency, memory, and device constraints. A pragmatic KD pipeline aligns the choice of distillation signal, teacher design, student pretraining, and data strategy to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context-Sensitive for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD can be applied across modalities and settings to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and serve as a core component of broader compression pipelines. However, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, data regimes, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), how training is organized (offline, online, self-distillation), and how data is handled (original, augmented/synthetic, or data-free). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful student design, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance; nevertheless, its effectiveness depends on choices about transfer targets, data availability, teacher quality, and robustness under distribution shift. Open issues include aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and scaling distillation in data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer capability from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost, memory, and energy while preserving much of task performance. The literature shows a spectrum of methods — from soft-target matching to representation-level alignment, progressive module replacement, and data-free or adversarial sample synthesis — and emphasizes that distillation is most effective when combined with careful student initialization, architecture-aware alignment, and complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to align teacher and student capacities; open challenges include optimization dynamics, domain shift, privacy, and robustness under rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with representation-aware objectives, careful pre-training of compact models, and safeguards for robustness and privacy, KD enables production-ready reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher's performance. I argue that KD should be treated as a central tool in model-compression pipelines, not as a single recipe but as a family of methods to be combined with task-aware design choices for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly used approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—such as softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or many-to-many layer mappings—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of a teacher model’s performance. Effective distillation is context-sensitive: choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use or synthesize, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques determine outcomes. While KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy trade-offs in vision and language tasks, practical adoption requires engineered pipelines to manage capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness risks.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, implementation-friendly paradigm that should be treated as the central component of practical model-compression pipelines. By transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational signals from larger teachers to smaller students—and by integrating with complementary techniques like pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—KD enables strong size–performance trade-offs for real-world deployment. However, realizing those gains requires deliberate teacher–student co-design, careful data handling, and explicit safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used paradigm for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models into smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost while preserving much of predictive performance. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or no-data approaches), and workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, federated). Empirical and conceptual work emphasizes the importance of teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distillation signal, and combination with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Despite frequent success across vision, language, speech, and graphs, open challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect imitation, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, privacy-sensitive deployments, and adapting distillation to heterogeneous device or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central element of practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but it is not a standalone cure: to produce deployable, robust, and fair students practitioners must combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, architecture search, quantization), data- and curriculum-driven training, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias. This integrated approach yields efficient models suited to real-world constraints while managing known distillation failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Extensions, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, task- and deployment-aware toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable component — combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies (public, synthesized, or online), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization) — KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal fix: its practical success depends on careful teacher design, attention to student capacity and data regimes, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as distribution shift, poor rare-token transfer, federated-data heterogeneity, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal structure. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce latency and memory, adapt models to new domains, enable privacy- or data-constrained deployments, and condense ensembles into single deployable models. Effective distillation blends choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, layers), how to pretrain or adapt compact architectures, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance, achieving robust, fair, and domain-appropriate students requires careful design of teachers, student architectures, and distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. A practical KD toolkit includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-aware mapping, data-aware augmentation or synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When chosen to match student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss; important open problems remain in capacity mismatch, distribution shift, privacy, and biased transfer.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD consistently delivers large reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of a teacher's behavior, but it is inherently context-sensitive: success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, what data are used or synthesized, and how KD is combined with complementary compression steps. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a central component of a compression pipeline rather than a one-shot recipe, and it requires targeted remedies for capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy, distribution shift, and risks of transferring teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Making Knowledge Distillation a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and broadly applicable method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When paired with representation-level objectives, careful teacher design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture replacement, or low-precision numerics), KD yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability. The method has clear limits (e.g., rare-token behaviors, data or privacy constraints), but these are addressable with multi-stage pipelines, data-centered practices, and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the most practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, language, and other modalities. When applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), designing teacher-student pairs, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) — distillation recovers much of a teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD also serves beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve robustness and generalization, but it is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization differences, and risks of transferring biases or vulnerability must be managed through targeted practices and evaluations.

papers_seen.author: Mcdaniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables preservation of much of a teacher’s capabilities while meeting real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and power. Its practical value comes from the variety of signals it can transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure), the ability to combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), and adaptability to data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires deliberate engineering: matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing distributional and rare-token failures, and integrating KD into broader compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a central, flexible component of model‑compression pipelines rather than as a single canned technique. By transferring richer forms of supervision (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational or attention signals) and by being combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD enables deployment of compact models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful distillation requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. When applied with task‑aware design and safeguards against optimization and bias failure modes, KD provides a practical road for compressing large models for real‑world NLP and deep‑learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Careful, and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints; supports domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization; and can be combined with other compression techniques. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align layers and representations, how to generate or augment data for distillation, and how to mitigate propagated errors or biases from teachers.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring learned behavior beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logit-matching to a broad toolkit that includes representation- and feature-level imitation, flexible layer mappings, task-aware architecture search, and strategies for data-limited or deployment-constrained settings. Combining these techniques with careful teacher selection, sample or objective weighting, and deployment-aware choices (e.g., low-precision or privacy-preserving protocols) yields compact models that often retain much of the teacher's utility while meeting latency and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Best-Practices Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. When engineered to the task and deployment constraints and combined with complementary techniques (e.g., representation alignment, data strategies, pruning/quantization, and multi-teacher schedules), KD yields strong size–performance tradeoffs. However, practitioners must design distillation pipelines to address capacity mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, bias transfer, and data-privacy constraints to produce robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Branch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and ensemble guidance—and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and deployment-aware evaluation. Open challenges include preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, avoiding transferred biases, and principled data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires careful choice of distillation signals, attention to data and privacy constraints, and explicit evaluation of robustness and failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving most of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, integrates naturally with complementary compression strategies, and supports deployment under privacy- and resource-constrained settings. Realizing KD’s full potential requires attention to what signals are distilled (logits, features, relations), how data are managed or synthesized, and how teacher–student alignment and curricula are designed.

papers_seen.author: Villa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is most effective when treated as a central component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses architecture-aware design, data curricula, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Real-world success requires careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data regime, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes such as degraded rare-token modeling and privacy-sensitive transfer.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Is Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across domains and deployment constraints—multi-task learning, low-resource devices, federated settings, data-free scenarios, and generative or detection tasks—KD enables targeted transfer of behavior, representations, and robustness. However, realizing KD's potential requires task-aware choices: which teacher(s) to use, what intermediate signals to mimic, how to select or synthesize training samples, and whether to incorporate adversarial or ensemble strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, selective sample strategies, and representation-level objectives, KD produces compact models that are accurate, efficient, and more widely deployable than large models alone.

papers_seen.author: Woods
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but its success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and available data; known failure modes include capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, and degradation on rare or low-frequency phenomena. papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple models into smaller, faster models by leveraging softer training signals, intermediate representations, or alternate training protocols. Research has explored KD’s theoretical underpinnings, practical training strategies (including teacher-ensemble and teacher-free variants), privacy- and communication-aware settings, and extensions beyond classification to generation and structured prediction. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s ability to reduce deployment cost while retaining or sometimes even improving downstream performance, but trade-offs remain around data availability, representation matching, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Across vision, speech, and language tasks KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Best practice treats KD as a central element of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—and adapts targets, data, and curricula to task and deployment constraints. Key open issues include representation alignment across architectures, propagated teacher biases, robustness under domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on choices of teacher/student architecture, what is distilled (logits, layers, attention, representations), the optimization and data used for distillation, and constraints such as privacy or fairness. Carefully combining KD with techniques like multi-teacher schedules, layer-mapping strategies, task-adaptive compression, and privacy-preserving perturbations yields the best trade-offs for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be adopted as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. KD’s flexibility—matching softened outputs, aligning representations, and operating with or without original data—lets practitioners trade compute and memory for minimal accuracy loss when combined with complementary compression methods. Careful design around teacher quality, student capacity, and data regimes is necessary to avoid transferring biases or degrading robustness.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that high performance can be retained under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across modalities KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer transfers of internal features, attention, or relational structure, and it is usually combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthetic, or data-free). Empirical results show large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest accuracy loss in many settings, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche training trick into a broad, practically necessary toolkit for compressing large deep models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD variants enable compressing Transformer-based and convolutional architectures, transferring useful inductive biases, operating with limited or no access to original training data, and even addressing downstream concerns such as fairness. At the same time, KD has limitations in certain distributed or heterogeneous-data settings that require complementary methods or careful protocol design. A targeted combination of task-aware layer-wise methods, feature-level mimicking, adversarial/data-free generation, and attention to distributional heterogeneity yields the best practical results for NLP and other deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Representation- and Deployment-Aware Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective for real-world model compression when it goes beyond logits to transfer internal representations, adapts to data availability, and explicitly preserves robustness and deployment constraints. Combining feature- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive layer mapping, data-free synthesis when needed, and robustness-aware training yields compact students that better match teacher behavior across tasks and modalities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large, high‑capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and graph settings, KD enables substantial reductions in storage and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is a context‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When integrated into a pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning/quantization, data strategies, and robustness checks, KD is the most practical and versatile method for producing compact models suitable for real deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students. When applied beyond naive logit matching—by transferring intermediate representations, using selective or multi-stage schedules, and combining distillation with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design)—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Real-world use requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data regimes (including public or synthesized data), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-behavior fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable efficient deployment. In practice KD spans matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations, specialized layer- and channel-level transfers, and workflows that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or synthetic-data strategies. KD delivers substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while often improving student generalization, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle data or domain shifts. Open issues include robustness under distributional heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior in sequence models, and distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-centered paradigm for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations via signals that range from softened logits to intermediate features, attention maps, and relational objectives. KD is most effective when its signals, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints, and when it is combined with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design). Important practical concerns include robustness transfer, privacy when original data are sensitive or unavailable, and alignment when teacher and student use heterogeneous inputs or detectors. The field continues to refine methods for representation alignment, adversarial and privacy-preserving distillation, and modality-specific adaptations to close the gap between teacher and student performance while meeting real-world latency and memory limits.
