papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt large pretrained models to constrained settings. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how training data are handled (real, augmented, synthesized, or none), and how teachers and students are aligned architecturally and procedurally. When design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss; however, challenges remain for heterogeneous architectures, generative tasks, privacy-sensitive settings, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Practical, and Context‑Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central method for turning large, high‑performing models into compact students suitable for deployment. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures—KD yields large gains in latency, memory, and deployability while preserving much of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a one‑size‑fits‑all recipe: naive soft‑label matching often underperforms, data availability or privacy constraints can require data‑free or zero‑shot strategies, and representation or optimization mismatches can harm rare‑token behavior, robustness, and fairness. Effective pipelines therefore treat KD as a toolbox to be combined with architecture design, data strategies, and targeted regularization to meet specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically effective approach for producing compact models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When framed as a central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques and data strategies, KD yields strong size–performance trade-offs while enabling domain adaptation and robustness improvements. However, realizing those benefits in production requires careful design choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to diagnose and mitigate transferred biases and rare-case degradation.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and a Design Recipe
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student design, handling data constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. KD has clear failure modes (propagating teacher errors, difficulty with low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift, and robustness/privacy concerns) that require principled pipelines, diagnostics, and mitigation strategies. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines but only effective when integrated with representation-aware objectives, data-aware strategies, and robustness/privacy-aware techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core, context-aware component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary tools — pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies — KD enables meaningful reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive performance. Success depends on explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or privacy-sensitive data, and how to measure robustness and long-tail behavior; a principled, deployment-aware distillation pipeline yields the best tradeoffs between efficiency and utility.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for shrinking large models into deployable students. KD is flexible in what it transfers (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), interoperates with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and supports privacy- or data-constrained settings via synthesized or data-free protocols. However, KD is engineering-dependent: realizing its benefits requires matching distillation signals to student capacity and deployment goals, addressing optimization and distributional mismatches, and mitigating risks like propagated biases or degraded long‑tail/rare‑token behavior. I argue KD should be treated as the central tool in compression pipelines, but only when used with targeted practices and safeguards tailored to the task and operational constraints.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, distillation variants (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, layer mapping, online or multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware strategies) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair distillation with data augmentation, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression methods to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness to distribution shift, and preserving fairness and rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a family of methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). These approaches aim to retain predictive performance while reducing model size, latency, or enabling deployment under privacy or communication constraints. Recent work broadens distillation beyond logits to intermediate features, attention maps, multi-teacher setups, and data-limited or privacy-preserving regimes, producing task- and domain-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, graph, and language tasks, distillation techniques can be adapted to preserve logits, features, or relational structure, and can be extended into online, multi-teacher, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive settings. Effective use of distillation requires attention to what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, relational signals), how teachers and students are aligned (projectors, input alignment, progressive replacement), and operational constraints (scalability, privacy, domain shift). When these design choices are matched to the task, distillation yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource use.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Effective compression in practice requires matching the distillation technique to the deployment objective: using self-distillation or multi-teacher strategies to extract richer supervisory signals, combining KD with architecture search or pruning for task-specific efficiency, applying appropriate soft/hard label mixing informed by bias–variance tradeoffs, and controlling data and privacy considerations during distillation. When these elements are combined, KD can deliver substantial runtime and memory savings with minimal accuracy loss, making it central to deploying modern NLP systems under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, or relational signals, and are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. Empirical work shows that KD typically narrows the performance gap between teacher and student across modalities, but practical success depends on careful choices about distillation targets, teacher preparation, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in NLP: Effectiveness, Methods, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large pretrained models into smaller, deployable students in NLP. When combined with architecture-aware design, representation-level objectives, data strategies (including synthesis and curriculum choices), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token fidelity, and bias transfer. Careful method selection and evaluation are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone, and when combined with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and multi-teacher curricula) it enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to produce or augment training data, and how to align teacher and student architectures determine outcomes. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as a central tool in compression pipelines but tailors the pipeline to task constraints, data availability, and robustness/fairness goals.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Practical and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource-constrained settings. However, successful distillation requires attention to optimization dynamics, representation alignment, data availability and privacy, robustness, and social biases. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a suite of complementary techniques — including feature mimicking, input alignment, multi-teacher curricula, data-free synthesis, and adversarially-aware training — and outlines concrete best practices for applying KD in deep learning and NLP to maximize utility while minimizing harms.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students that meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD operates at multiple granularities — softened logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals — and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data‑free synthesis) to yield strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, its success is context dependent: KD can propagate teacher errors, struggle under domain shift or data scarcity, and interact with architectural or optimization mismatch. Thus, KD should be treated as the central tool in model compression pipelines, applied with explicit design choices, complementary compression methods, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A mature toolbox has emerged that includes soft-label/logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when teacher–student alignment, training curricula, and data availability are carefully addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, potential bias transfer, and robustness under distributional shifts; nonetheless, well‑designed KD pipelines routinely produce compact models that approach teacher performance across vision, language, speech, graph, and recommendation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD methods transfer information via soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals, or ensemble guidance. Effective KD pipelines combine appropriate distillation targets, teacher–student alignment (layer mapping or projectors), data strategies (public, augmented, or synthesized), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and attention to robustness and fairness. Best practice emphasizes task-aware choices, representation-level objectives, multi-stage or curriculum training, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Compression to Regularization, Robustness, and Generalization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often presented primarily as a model compression technique. Emerging work shows KD is also a flexible training paradigm that provides regularization, transfers internal representations, improves robustness to adversaries and domain shifts, and can be applied without a stronger teacher. This essay argues KD should be treated as a general-purpose tool for shaping student learning — one that can and should be combined with teacher-free methods, internal-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, careful data augmentation, and principled mixing of hard and soft targets to maximize performance in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals from a higher-capacity teacher to a compact student, KD enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of the original performance. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Branch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and ensemble guidance—and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and deployment-aware evaluation. Open challenges include preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, avoiding transferred biases, and principled data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Opportunities and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students and composes well with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. However, KD is not a turnkey solution—its real-world success requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to detect and mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, or biased transfer.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure so students meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The paradigm has evolved from matching soft logits to a broad toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data- or architecture-aware pipelines. Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability (including data-free alternatives), and careful alignment of signals and training dynamics. KD has been applied across domains (machine translation, recommender systems, 3D vision, text generation) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware practices; open issues remain around distribution shift, propagation of teacher artifacts, low-frequency behavior, fairness, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students so models can run with lower compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of their performance. The technique has diversified from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure, and it integrates naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher–student pairs, which data to use (real, public, or synthesized), and how to manage optimization, distribution shift, and societal risks (robustness, fairness, privacy). Ongoing work refines objectives, curricula, and data strategies to preserve rare or long-tail behaviors and to scale KD for modern large pretrained models across vision, language, and generative tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Responsible Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students so deployed systems meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely narrows the accuracy gap between large and compact models when its objectives, data strategy, and architecture choices are matched to the deployment goal. However, KD is not a turnkey fix: its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, available training data (or reliable synthesis), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. A practical compression pipeline treats KD as the central, composable element—used alongside pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—while adopting task-aware diagnostics and safeguards to avoid propagating teacher errors or brittle behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. By transferring supervisory signals beyond hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and safeguards for fairness and robustness. I argue KD should be treated as the central organizing method in practical compression pipelines, while noting concrete failure modes and recommending principled mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s utility under resource constraints, realizing its benefits in production requires deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred errors and biases. A pragmatic KD pipeline combines soft-target matching with representation-level supervision, architecture-aware adaptation, and complementary compression methods to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. It has been applied across supervised, self-supervised, multimodal and domain-adaptation settings to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Progress includes direct soft-target matching, feature- and relation-based imitation, self- and progressive-distillation strategies, and task- or domain-aware adaptations. Empirical work highlights both the power of KD to produce efficient models for deployment and important practical considerations—such as the value of pre-training, the role of data augmentation and sample selection, and computational bottlenecks—that shape effective distillation regimes. Despite advances, optimization mismatches, teacher–student capacity differences, and data-domain shift remain active challenges guiding current research and practice.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved from matching softened teacher outputs to a rich toolbox that includes intermediate representation transfer, attention or relation-level objectives, data-free and online methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when its signals, data strategy, and student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. Important open problems remain around capacity mismatch, long-tail or rare-token behaviors, distribution shift, and avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information that goes beyond hard labels. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a toolbox of techniques that include intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher curricula, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. This synthesis summarizes the principal methods, practical combinations with other compression techniques, and the main limitations and open problems that shape current research and deployment choices.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used set of techniques for training compact student models that capture much of a larger teacher model's behavior while reducing latency, memory, and energy costs. KD is instantiated through multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relational and layer-wise objectives), often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial deployability gains across NLP tasks (ranking, reading comprehension, multi-task models), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student architectures or training schedules are aligned; unresolved issues include optimization mismatch, bias transfer, rare-token fidelity, and robustness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Tool for Compression in NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher's performance. In natural language processing, KD can operate at multiple granularities — from logits to intermediate representations or entire modules — and can be combined with pre-training, pruning, and low-precision inference to meet real-world deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, mismatches in internal representations, and task-specific redundancies can limit benefits unless methods are adapted to the model size, pre-training regimen, and downstream objectives. When applied thoughtfully (e.g., pre-training compact students, selectively transferring internal features, and using task-aware layer-wise matching), KD yields efficient models that generalize well across tasks and settings.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to student capacity, data availability, and task constraints, KD can yield large reductions in latency, memory, and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher's performance. Its practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, integrating complementary compression techniques, and addressing data- and distribution-related limitations through task-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across modalities and constraints — including resource-limited devices, privacy- or data-constrained settings, distributed systems, and adversarial robustness requirements — KD and its variants enable trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and practicality. Best results arise when practitioners combine representation-level distillation, careful layer mapping, and appropriate pre-training or data-synthesis strategies to match the deployment scenario.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central element of practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but it is not a standalone cure: to produce deployable, robust, and fair students practitioners must combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, architecture search, quantization), data- and curriculum-driven training, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and bias. This integrated approach yields efficient models suited to real-world constraints while managing known distillation failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression — Practical Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, high-impact approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across NLP, speech, and vision. Treated as the central element of compression pipelines and combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs. However, realizing these gains in practice requires deliberate teacher–student co‑design, careful handling of data and augmentation, selective transfer of signals, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a flexible training paradigm that enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By choosing what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to generate or select data (real, public, or synthesized), and how to schedule and regularize student training, practitioners can shape trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy. KD’s effectiveness depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and data regime; when combined with multi-teacher strategies, adversarial data synthesis, or differential-privacy mechanisms, KD supports practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a model-compression trick but a central, practical paradigm for deploying high-performance deep and NLP models under real-world constraints. KD can compress large pre-trained models into lightweight students, transfer inductive biases, improve robustness and generalization, enable low-precision and privacy-aware deployments, and adapt to data- or compute-limited settings. Effective distillation couples soft-label transfer with representation-level alignment, task-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, augmentation). However, KD must be applied carefully: teacher–student mismatches, bias transfer, domain shift, and limited-data regimes require method choices such as feature mimicking, teacher ensembles, teacher-free objectives, or fairness-aware augmentations. The result is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with architectural and data strategies—makes high-quality, efficient models feasible for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and several data strategies (including data-free or privacy-aware workflows). KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware pretraining) and when practitioner choices align teacher signals, student capacity, and available data. While KD can recover much of teacher performance with large efficiency gains, it has known failure modes—optimization difficulty, teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena—that require tailored design, diagnostics, and hybrid pipelines to address.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller models by transferring predictive and representational information from teachers to students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical pipelines combine soft-target matching, representation-level imitation, architecture-aware design and search, and data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving synthesis). While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can enable students that are substantially faster and smaller, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and teacher quality; important open problems remain in robustness, domain shift, and theoretical explanation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students. In deep learning and NLP, KD enables practical deployment by reducing latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application requires: (1) combining KD with domain-aware pretraining of compact models, (2) adapting distillation to data-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and (3) integrating architectural and optimization improvements (e.g., feature projectors, mixed-precision) to close remaining gaps. When applied thoughtfully, KD is a key tool for making state-of-the-art models useful in real-world, resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable efficient deployment. In practice KD spans matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations, specialized layer- and channel-level transfers, and workflows that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or synthetic-data strategies. KD delivers substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while often improving student generalization, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle data or domain shifts. Open issues include robustness under distributional heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior in sequence models, and distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be Central to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths include multiple forms of transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational information), compatibility with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and applicability in data- and privacy-constrained settings. Realizing these benefits in practice requires careful choices about the signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, data management (real, augmented, or synthesized), and measures to detect and remedy robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift issues.

papers_seen.author: Johnston
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD encompasses output-level (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols. In practice KD is a composable component of compression pipelines and is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or synthetic-data strategies. While KD frequently retains much of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its effectiveness depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher and student co-design, data availability, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students. When applied beyond naive logit matching—by transferring intermediate representations, using selective or multi-stage schedules, and combining distillation with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design)—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Real-world use requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data regimes (including public or synthesized data), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-behavior fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The field has broadened from soft-logit matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, relational and attention-aware transfers, data-free synthesis, adversarially-aware objectives, and curriculum or multi-teacher schemes. Practical success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student architectural alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, maintaining robustness and privacy, and adapting distillation to domain shifts and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses behavioral and representational knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature presents a broad toolbox—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and meta-distillation, data-free or data-scarce strategies, and layer- or relation-focused transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical and conceptual work shows KD can also regularize students and sometimes improve generalization or robustness, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student capacities are aligned, and how data (real, augmented, or synthesized) are used. Open issues include distribution shift, rare-token behavior in sequence models, privacy constraints, and principled objectives for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and richer relational or layer-wise signals; it is often combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical results show KD frequently recovers much of a teacher’s performance and can improve generalization, but outcomes depend on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (or synthesis), and attention to robustness and bias. Important open problems include handling domain shift, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors in sequence models, principled data-free distillation, and privacy-aware pipelines.
