papers_seen.author: Burns
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, flexible route to compressing large deep models into deployable students. When combined with complementary compression techniques, careful choice of distilled signals, and data-aware procedures, KD reliably improves inference cost and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing KD’s potential requires attention to teacher–student alignment, preservation of internal representations and rare behaviors, and adaptations for domain shift and federated or heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher. Techniques extend beyond using teacher soft outputs (soft labels) to include internal representation matching, layer alignment, task-aware selection of teacher information, data-free synthesis, online mutual teaching, and architecture search guided by distillation. Practical work on NLP (especially BERT-family models), generative models, and domain- or modality-specific settings demonstrates that combining pre-training, architecture-aware search, and representation-level distillation often yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and downstream performance. Open challenges remain around imperfect teachers, optimization and capacity mismatch, data availability, and robustness/generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal structure. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce latency and memory, adapt models to new domains, enable privacy- or data-constrained deployments, and condense ensembles into single deployable models. Effective distillation blends choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, layers), how to pretrain or adapt compact architectures, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance, achieving robust, fair, and domain-appropriate students requires careful design of teachers, student architectures, and distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Methods range from matching softened logits to imitating internal representations, attention maps, or channel-wise activations, and can be combined with quantization, low-precision numerics, architecture-aware design, and data- or teacher-aware training regimes. In practice, distillation is a multifaceted toolkit that must be tailored to deployment goals (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness), and remaining challenges include principled sample selection, representation alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The method spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer strategies that align internal representations, use synthetic or unlabeled data, or apply curriculum and online schemes. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning or quantization, and deployment-aware data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and handling of optimization or distributional limits; careful method design and evaluation are required to produce robust, fair, and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification, or progressive module replacement) and paired with careful choices about what signals to transfer and which data to use, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Real-world use also requires attention to teacher design, optimization gaps, and risks such as propagated biases or degraded rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods range from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants that synthesize or reuse surrogate data. Applied across vision, speech, recommender systems, and NLP, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while enabling domain adaptation and robustness-focused objectives. Practical success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under storage, latency, and privacy constraints. The literature converges on a taxonomy of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, self-distillation), and data strategies (original data, augmented or synthetic data, and data-free approaches). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when matched to student capacity, but success depends on choices about distillation signals, layer alignment, data availability, and complementary compression tools. Open challenges include preserving robustness under distribution shift, handling low-frequency phenomena, and aligning heterogeneous architectures, motivating task-aware pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable models. Beyond raw compression, KD can be adapted to meet constraints of privacy, heterogeneous devices, low-precision hardware, and domain or modality shifts. When combined with complementary techniques such as pre-training, layer-level supervision, or ensemble teachers, distillation can retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while enabling production usage that would otherwise be impractical. This essay argues that KD should be a primary tool in the model-compression toolbox for both research and engineering deployments, and that best results come from tailoring distillation objectives and pipelines to application needs.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A mature toolbox has emerged that includes soft-label/logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when teacher–student alignment, training curricula, and data availability are carefully addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, potential bias transfer, and robustness under distributional shifts; nonetheless, well‑designed KD pipelines routinely produce compact models that approach teacher performance across vision, language, speech, graph, and recommendation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a dominant approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It operates by transferring information from a teacher to a student using a variety of signals and workflows, and it is routinely combined with other compression techniques to meet practical latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teachers performance, its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability or synthesis of data, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer useful knowledge from larger, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones so that deployed systems retain high performance under resource constraints. Approaches span logit-level supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, progressive module replacement, and data-augmentation or data-free strategies. Applications include compressing large language models, accelerating inference on edge devices, enabling multi-task and federated learning, and improving robustness or generalization. Practical deployments often combine KD with quantization, architecture design, or task-aware selection of teacher signals to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. These techniques are applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), deployment scenarios (edge devices, federated learning), and objectives (accuracy preservation, efficiency, interpretability, fairness). Advances include theoretical reframings that connect KD to regularization, a range of strategies for aligning outputs and internal representations, methods that restructure or progressively replace model components, and practical systems that enable heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments. Despite clear empirical gains, open problems remain in understanding when and why different distillation targets (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior) are most effective, and how to balance compression with robustness and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Sandoval
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a broad toolkit—logit and softened output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and tailored to student capacity and data availability, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. Practical deployment requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to teacher–student mismatches, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for shrinking large neural models into compact, deployable students. As a composable toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer softened outputs, intermediate features, and relational structure, and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical center of model compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably yields compact, lower-latency models while retaining much of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on deployment context. Best outcomes arise when KD is paired with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), careful choice of distillation signals, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones for deployment in constrained environments. KD techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational signals, and operating in data-limited or privacy-sensitive regimes via synthesized or public data. When combined with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, architecture search), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Persistent challenges include understanding the mechanisms of transfer, handling student–teacher capacity mismatch, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, and ensuring robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. It is applied across modalities and deployment constraints and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data and teacher design, and methods that address representation mismatch and optimization. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended practices for using KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is flexible across signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations), workflows (multi-stage, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. To realize reliable, production-ready compressed models, practitioners must pair KD with careful student pre-training, data strategies, mitigation of bias and rare-token failures, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with careful teacher–student engineering, appropriate distillation signals, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, its reliability depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, alignment of representations, and explicit mitigation of robustness, privacy, and rare-token or distribution-shift failures. I argue KD should be the core of any real-world compression strategy, but only when embedded in an engineering-aware pipeline that anticipates and corrects its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is empirically effective across modalities because it transfers richer signals than hard labels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational cues) and composes with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). However, KD is engineering-dependent: data availability, teacher quality, and student–teacher mismatch create failure modes that require task-aware choices. A pragmatic compression pipeline treats KD as one component among data strategies, architecture adaptation, and hardware-aware tuning to achieve reliable, high-fidelity compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data and augmentation strategies to use—KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation also has limits: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle with low-data or low-capacity students, and requires complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, pruning, or synthetic-data schemes) and careful evaluation to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other structural knowledge from teacher(s) to student(s). Approaches range from classic logit-matching to feature- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, data-free adversarial methods, and adaptations for distributed or heterogeneous settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing size and latency; practical success depends on choices like what form of knowledge to transfer, whether and how to augment or synthesize data, and how to handle heterogeneous compute or domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has expanded from simple logit matching to a rich toolbox including feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and progressive-distillation, ensemble compression, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and federated protocols. Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to handle teacher–student mismatches and optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s utility under resource constraints, realizing its benefits in production requires deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred errors and biases. A pragmatic KD pipeline combines soft-target matching with representation-level supervision, architecture-aware adaptation, and complementary compression methods to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD serves as a flexible training paradigm that can be combined with pre-training, privacy-preserving workflows, and architecture-aware mimicry to preserve task performance while meeting latency, memory, and device constraints. A pragmatic KD pipeline aligns the choice of distillation signal, teacher design, student pretraining, and data strategy to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and sometimes communication or privacy exposure. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention signals; it is commonly combined with complementary compression methods and with data or model-centric strategies to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and robustness and fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision and language tasks, the approach ranges from soft‑target/logit matching to feature‑ and layer‑wise alignment, attention or relational transfers, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑limited or data‑free regimes. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful design of teacher–student interactions, selection of distilled signals, management of data and optimization dynamics, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds when the distillation signals, data strategy, and architecture choices are matched to deployment constraints; its most reliable use combines logits-based supervision with representation-level alignment, multi-stage curricula, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful pipeline design is required to avoid transferring teacher errors, to handle low-frequency phenomena and domain shifts, and to meet privacy or data-limited requirements.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used paradigm for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching soft teacher logits to a versatile toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- or privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. Empirical and engineering work shows KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints, but practitioners must manage limits such as capacity mismatch, degraded modeling of rare phenomena, privacy and data availability, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables retention of teacher capabilities across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. Effective deployment requires matching distillation targets to student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy limits, and combining KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning or architecture search. This paper argues that KD should be the central component of modern compression pipelines and outlines practical principles to maximize its benefits and mitigate common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical tool for compressing deep and NLP models because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD excels when combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, but it is not a panacea: careful design choices are required to handle capacity mismatch, limited data, distribution shift, imperfect teachers, and transferred biases. A disciplined pipeline — choosing appropriate distillation signals, augmenting or synthesizing data when necessary, and aligning teacher–student architectures — yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The literature frames KD as a toolkit that includes soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-representation alignment, layer- or module-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and curriculum schedules, data-augmentation or data-free approaches, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance when signals, data, and architectures are chosen deliberately; however, limits arise from capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, distributional shift, and the potential to transfer undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, spurious correlations). Practical pipelines therefore co-design teachers and students, select appropriate transfer signals, and pair distillation with data and system-level strategies to meet deployment constraints. Remaining research directions include better theoretical understanding, distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, student-aware teacher design, and fairness-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible core of modern model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervisory signals from large teachers into smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of the teachers' capabilities. KD operates across multiple granularities (soft logits, internal features, attention or relational maps) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Despite strong empirical successes, open problems remain in handling data scarcity and distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, preserving rare or long-tail behavior, and providing principled theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Compression to Regularization, Robustness, and Generalization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often presented primarily as a model compression technique. Emerging work shows KD is also a flexible training paradigm that provides regularization, transfers internal representations, improves robustness to adversaries and domain shifts, and can be applied without a stronger teacher. This essay argues KD should be treated as a general-purpose tool for shaping student learning — one that can and should be combined with teacher-free methods, internal-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, careful data augmentation, and principled mixing of hard and soft targets to maximize performance in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains across domains by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or task-specific behaviors from teachers to students. Its strengths are practical: it supports deployment on constrained hardware, enables multi-teacher and cross-model transfer, and integrates with other compression tools. At the same time, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: theoretical and empirical work shows limits under data heterogeneity, imperfect teachers, and mismatched architectures, so KD must be applied with task-aware choices (signal type, layer alignment, teacher selection, and curricula) and often combined with complementary methods to realize reliable, high-fidelity compression.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Engineering Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate representations, relational signals—and when integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and optimization strategies it yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is context-sensitive: its benefits depend on what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token degradation, and bias transfer. Responsible deployment therefore requires engineering pipelines that combine tailored distillation objectives, curriculum-style schedules, targeted augmentation or data synthesis, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity 'teacher' models to smaller, efficient 'student' models so they can meet real-world constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy). KD methods operate at multiple granularities — softened output logits, intermediate feature or attention matching, relational and module-level objectives — and are frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or data synthesis). Empirically, KD routinely improves student performance compared to training from scratch and enables deployment across modalities and constrained settings, though challenges remain in robustness, low-frequency behavior, domain shift, and distillation without original data. This synthesis summarizes core methods, practical workflows, empirical benefits, and open problems to guide applied KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive and representational information from larger teacher models to smaller students so models can be deployed under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature spans simple soft-target matching to richer strategies—intermediate representation imitation, attention- and relation-based losses, curriculum and teacher-design methods, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning or architecture-aware compression. Practical success depends on choices about distillation signals, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression techniques; open issues include handling teacher imperfections, low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift, and privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller ones that meet deployment constraints. KD reduces storage, latency, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher signals are generated and trusted, and how distillation is combined with other compression methods and fairness or robustness constraints. Effective deployment requires task-aware decisions about targets (logits vs. features), data (original, augmented, or synthetic), architectural alignment, and additional safeguards for bias and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural models for deployment and domain-specialization. Beyond simple teacher-to-student label matching, modern KD techniques transfer intermediate representations, exploit synthetic or augmented data, operate without original training data, and incorporate privacy or distributed-training constraints. These variants enable retaining much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, supporting domain adaptation, improving generalization under limited-data regimes, and meeting privacy or latency requirements for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential approach for compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By transferring learned behavior from teachers to students, KD enables many deployment trade-offs while remaining compatible with complementary techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning, architecture search). However, to be robust and broadly useful in real systems, distillation must go beyond naive soft-label matching: effective pipelines combine logits with internal representation transfer, task- and layer-aware selection of signals, appropriate data strategies, and attention to distributional heterogeneity and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models to smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer objectives that align intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and it is commonly combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization. Success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, student capacity, training data (including synthesized or distilled datasets), and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. This article synthesizes core methods, empirical patterns, and practical recommendations that guide the use of KD in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD can be adapted across modalities and constraints—by matching soft logits, intermediate representations, or attention maps; by using ensembles or teacher optimization; and by operating with or without original training data—making it well suited to real-world deployment needs. Because its effectiveness depends on representation alignment, teacher–student design, and data regime, KD is best applied as a component in broader compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware choices) and selected to fit the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the most practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, language, and other modalities. When applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), designing teacher-student pairs, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) — distillation recovers much of a teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD also serves beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve robustness and generalization, but it is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization differences, and risks of transferring biases or vulnerability must be managed through targeted practices and evaluations.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Why and How Knowledge Distillation Enables Practical Compression for Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained and ensemble models deliver state-of-the-art accuracy in NLP and other deep learning domains but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide principled ways to transfer predictive behaviour and internal representations from expensive teachers into compact students. When combined with careful pre-training, feature-level matching, layer-mapping strategies, data augmentation, and curriculum design, distillation yields models that approach teacher accuracy while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude or more. This paper argues that KD is both necessary and practical for deploying high-quality compact models and outlines concrete, evidence-backed strategies to maximize its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer useful knowledge from larger, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones so that deployed systems retain high performance under resource constraints. Approaches span logit-level supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, progressive module replacement, and data-augmentation or data-free strategies. Applications include compressing large language models, accelerating inference on edge devices, enabling multi-task and federated learning, and improving robustness or generalization. Practical deployments often combine KD with quantization, architecture design, or task-aware selection of teacher signals to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal information. Methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features or relational structure, and KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows strong practical gains across vision and NLP, but challenges remain around representation alignment, robustness, rare-token fidelity, privacy, and data heterogeneity — motivating richer distillation targets and deployment-aware pipelines.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from one or more teacher models into smaller students so they retain much of the teacher’s capabilities with lower compute, memory, or latency. The literature spans a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and common integrations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pre-training of compact models). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and inductive biases, what data to use (or synthesize), and constraints around deployment, privacy, and domain shift.
