papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, composable component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD is versatile—able to transfer logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data-synthesis techniques to produce deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data and distributional constraints, and explicitly addressing fairness and robustness concerns. When designed and evaluated carefully, KD enables effective trade-offs between efficiency and task performance across modalities.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention/relational signals, and can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies (including synthesized or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely improves student performance when design choices are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints, but practitioners must address challenges such as distribution shift, low-frequency behavior loss, and transfer of undesirable teacher properties.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Cervantes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models that retain much of large-teacher performance. KD supports multiple transfer signals and workflows, composes effectively with orthogonal compression tools, and is adaptable to privacy- and deployment-sensitive contexts. Its real-world success depends on matching distilled signals and curricula to student capacity, combining KD with pruning/quantization or architecture design when appropriate, and explicitly addressing risks such as propagated biases, optimization mismatches, and long-tail or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Powerful but Not Sufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone, KD enables on-device deployment, domain adaptation, ensemble condensation, and improved efficiency with modest performance loss. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, transferred biases, poor handling of rare or low-frequency behaviors) and must be combined with complementary compression techniques, robust data strategies, and evaluation under deployment constraints to be reliably effective.

papers_seen.author: Collier
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. When paired with representation-aware objectives, student–teacher co-design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD enables deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while remaining competitive on real tasks. Real-world use requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability, and robustness to avoid common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. KD is effective across modalities (vision, speech, language, graphs) and settings (task-specific compression, data-limited or data-free transfer), and its strengths are amplified when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware replacement, pruning, low-precision numerics, adaptive teacher design, and careful input-side practices. To realize robust and fair compressed models, practitioners should treat KD as one tool within a pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, account for data constraints, use augmentation and curriculum where helpful, and combine KD with orthogonal compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Bias Transfer, and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a model compression trick: it is a practical mechanism for transferring inductive biases, regularizing students, enabling privacy- and data-constrained deployments, and adapting architectures or modalities. When paired with complementary techniques—data augmentation, curriculum schedules, teacher ensembles, or generative replay—KD consistently narrows the gap between compact students and large teachers while addressing real-world constraints such as limited labeled data, compute, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans a range of goals — shrinking model size and latency, preserving privacy, enabling distributed learning, and retaining task- or robustness-related properties — and a correspondingly diverse set of techniques including logit and feature matching, layer-wise and many-to-many mapping, adversarial generation of training examples, and architecture-aware pruning and replacement. Empirical work shows effective trade-offs across vision, multimodal, and language tasks, while recent methods also tackle practical constraints such as lack of original data, privacy requirements, and distributed communication budgets.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD comprises a family of methods — from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or privacy-prespecting variants — that together enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and power while retaining much of teacher performance. Its success in production settings depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle scarce or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign).

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive performance and internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Work in this area spans theoretical analyses, practical compression recipes for language and vision models, approaches that avoid access to original training data, and methods that target robustness, privacy, or device heterogeneity. The field balances trade-offs among student capacity, teacher imperfection, data availability, and downstream task requirements, producing a range of techniques—logit-level distillation, layer-wise and module-level matching, progressive replacement, data-free generation, and combined compression with low-precision numerics—that are evaluated across tasks from BERT compression to multimodal and 3D detection. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, motivations, and recurring challenges emerging from recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: What We Know about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features or layers, and from single-teacher offline distillation to multi-teacher, online, or data‑constrained variants. KD is typically combined with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware student design to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; open challenges include optimization mismatch, capacity and distributional gaps, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a central, flexible component of model‑compression pipelines rather than as a single canned technique. By transferring richer forms of supervision (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational or attention signals) and by being combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD enables deployment of compact models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful distillation requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. When applied with task‑aware design and safeguards against optimization and bias failure modes, KD provides a practical road for compressing large models for real‑world NLP and deep‑learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to produce smaller, faster models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generation), practitioners balance trade-offs among accuracy, efficiency, data availability, privacy, and fairness. Recent work extends classical logits-based distillation with feature- and layer-level objectives, projector modules, adversarial data generation for data-free settings, multi-teacher and meta-learned teachers, and privacy-aware perturbations. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight both practical gains and persistent issues—optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, data-mismatch effects, and modality-specific alignment problems—guiding current best practices for deploying distilled models in resource- and privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has expanded from simple logit matching to a rich toolbox including feature- and layer-level imitation, self- and progressive-distillation, ensemble compression, data-free or zero-shot approaches, and federated protocols. Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to handle teacher–student mismatches and optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Representation- and Deployment-Aware Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective for real-world model compression when it goes beyond logits to transfer internal representations, adapts to data availability, and explicitly preserves robustness and deployment constraints. Combining feature- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive layer mapping, data-free synthesis when needed, and robustness-aware training yields compact students that better match teacher behavior across tasks and modalities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The literature frames KD as a toolkit that includes soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-representation alignment, layer- or module-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and curriculum schedules, data-augmentation or data-free approaches, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance when signals, data, and architectures are chosen deliberately; however, limits arise from capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, distributional shift, and the potential to transfer undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, spurious correlations). Practical pipelines therefore co-design teachers and students, select appropriate transfer signals, and pair distillation with data and system-level strategies to meet deployment constraints. Remaining research directions include better theoretical understanding, distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, student-aware teacher design, and fairness-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: The Practical Case for Feature- and Representation-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large models into efficient students while retaining much of their accuracy. Beyond the classical logit-matching formulation, modern KD practices that match internal representations, use tailored projectors or selective sample strategies, and account for deployment constraints (e.g., no access to original data or adversarial threats) yield better student models across modalities and tasks. Combining these advances—feature mimicking, projector ensembles, selective distillation, data-free techniques, and robustness-aware training—produces compact models that are both performant and deployable.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression: Effective but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more hardware-friendly students while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness spans supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, but the choice of what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations, attention), how to measure discrepancy, and how to combine KD with pruning or quantization critically determines success. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolbox of complementary techniques whose components must be matched to task, teacher quality, and deployment constraints to obtain reliable and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Path to Deployable NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models deliver state-of-the-art results in many NLP tasks but are often too large or too costly for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques enable retaining much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and inference cost. Advances in task-aware, layer-wise, data-free, and adversarially-informed distillation methods demonstrate that KD can address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and heterogeneity in deployment environments, making it a central tool for practical NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their effectiveness. When combined with task-specific adaptations (layer mapping, data-free synthesis, federated protocols, quantization, or self-supervision), KD enables deployment in low-resource, privacy-sensitive, and domain-specific settings. Success depends on designing appropriate alignment mechanisms, data strategies, and fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across modalities and deployment settings KD techniques leverage soft targets, intermediate-feature matching, attention, generative synthesis, and architecture search to balance accuracy, size, privacy, and communication cost. Practical systems extend KD to settings with no original data, heterogeneous or private devices, multi-teacher ensembles, and task-adaptive compression. Key challenges remain in distribution shift of synthetic data, aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, preserving privacy under queries, and choosing effective distillation signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic pathway to produce compact, efficient models from large teachers while preserving much of their performance. When thoughtfully combined with complementary techniques—representation-level objectives, architecture-aware student design, data strategies including data-free or privacy-sensitive workflows, and targeted optimization—KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and data issues; failures and trade-offs are documented and can be managed with targeted practices.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target matching, feature and attention alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher curricula, data synthesis or augmentation, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation)—enables practical trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Empirical and theoretical work indicates distillation often acts both as an information transfer mechanism and a regularizer; success depends on student capacity, data availability, choice of distilled signals, and careful handling of robustness and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, KD functions as a toolbox: it can transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; be combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization; and operate with or without original training data. KD delivers substantial reductions in size and latency with modest performance loss when methods and signals are chosen to match student capacity, task requirements, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context-sensitive: success depends on handling teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness concerns, data availability, and optimization choices. The most reliable pipelines therefore combine multiple distillation signals, data-aware strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as bias transfer and rare-token degradation.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical center of model compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably yields compact, lower-latency models while retaining much of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on deployment context. Best outcomes arise when KD is paired with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), careful choice of distillation signals, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through multiple mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate representation transfer, and inductive-bias alignment) and yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary techniques and task-aware engineering. However, realizing KD’s value in production requires explicit handling of teacher imperfections, data- or privacy-limited regimes, and low-frequency behavior through careful signal choice, curriculum and sample selection, and architectural or optimization adjustments.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models across NLP and vision domains. When adapted to task and deployment constraints—via multi-teacher schedules, feature-level objectives, data-free synthesis, online protocols, or privacy-aware ensembles—KD both preserves quality and addresses communication, privacy, and compute bottlenecks. However, KD is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity and optimization mismatches can limit its effectiveness, so careful method selection and engineering are required for robust compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential, Combinable, and Context‑Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, enabling lower latency, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment when paired with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on data regime, teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, and the choice of distilled signals. A principled pipeline treats KD as a toolbox—combining logits and feature targets, multi‑teacher schedules, data synthesis or privacy‑aware protocols, and hardware‑aware compression—to produce robust, task‑appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data augmentation), and when adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance. At the same time, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are matched, and how to handle domain shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression—Essential but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It reliably yields substantial efficiency gains by transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. However, KD’s success in real-world deployments depends on alignment between teacher signals and student capacity, availability or synthesis of appropriate training data, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Therefore KD should be treated as the central component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, multi-stage or online schemes) and composes well with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints. KD enables many deployment goals (reduced latency/memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training), but its effectiveness is limited by optimization dynamics, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift for synthetic data, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or inductive biases. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD methods aim to preserve teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical pipelines combine distillation with architecture adaptations, data strategies, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization) and must address failure modes related to data mismatch, rare-token fidelity, teacher–student capacity gaps, and privacy or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layerwise and many-to-many mapping, relational and curriculum schemes, self- and multi-teacher approaches, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and tuned to deployment constraints (latency, memory, robustness, and privacy), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, though open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practical Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations, enabling reduced latency, memory footprint, and energy use while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective KD combines choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to supply or synthesize training data, and when to integrate complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization). Success depends on task- and data-aware engineering: careful teacher selection or synthesis, student capacity matching, and mitigation of distributional and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-purpose strategy for compressing large deep models while preserving performance. KD can be adapted to constraints common in NLP deployment—limited compute, privacy restrictions, low-latency requirements, and robustness demands—by pairing standard teacher-student training with techniques such as feature-level matching, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and teacher adaptation. Across domains (transformers for NLP, speech embeddings, graph models, generative models), KD consistently enables large reductions in model size or latency with modest accuracy loss, making it a primary method for productionization of deep models.

papers_seen.author: Matthews
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer objectives that align intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and layer mappings. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data synthesis) and applied with task- and data-aware design, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs in vision, language, graph, and multimodal settings. Yet KD has limits: capacity mismatch, optimization dynamics, teacher imperfection, distribution shift, and loss of rare or fine-grained behaviors require careful pipeline choices, diagnostics, and often hybrid methods to produce robust, deployable students.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, data augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies) and adapted to task- and data-specific constraints, KD frequently achieves large efficiency gains with modest performance loss. Practical success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data, robustness, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible core of modern model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervisory signals from large teachers into smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of the teachers' capabilities. KD operates across multiple granularities (soft logits, internal features, attention or relational maps) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Despite strong empirical successes, open problems remain in handling data scarcity and distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, preserving rare or long-tail behavior, and providing principled theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary component of practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it offers a flexible set of transfer signals and training regimes that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. However, KD is not a turnkey solution — its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When designers adopt representation-aware objectives, layer mappings, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit mitigation for capacity mismatch and long-tail behaviors, KD yields compact, deployable models that balance fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Villarreal
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of training paradigms that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. The literature frames KD as a multi-signal toolbox (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and frequent integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign). Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, handling available data (real, public, or synthesized), and adapting objectives and schedules to deployment constraints; open challenges remain in robustness, distributional shift, low-frequency behaviors, and the transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and module-level transfer, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, and integration with architecture search or federated training. Practical deployments balance what is transferred with student capacity, data availability, privacy constraints, and device heterogeneity; empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, smaller models, and domain specialization, but open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so that compact models can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data strategies (original data, public or synthesized data, and data-free or adversarial sample generation) has been developed. KD is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware search) and adapted to application domains (NLP, 2D/3D vision, federated settings). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match teacher and student capacity, and how to address distribution shift, rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across modalities and constraints — including resource-limited devices, privacy- or data-constrained settings, distributed systems, and adversarial robustness requirements — KD and its variants enable trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and practicality. Best results arise when practitioners combine representation-level distillation, careful layer mapping, and appropriate pre-training or data-synthesis strategies to match the deployment scenario.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students so models can run with lower compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of their performance. The technique has diversified from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure, and it integrates naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher–student pairs, which data to use (real, public, or synthesized), and how to manage optimization, distribution shift, and societal risks (robustness, fairness, privacy). Ongoing work refines objectives, curricula, and data strategies to preserve rare or long-tail behaviors and to scale KD for modern large pretrained models across vision, language, and generative tasks.
