papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, production-oriented approach that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a composable component within wider compression pipelines, KD enables effective trade-offs among accuracy, size, and deployment constraints; however, its practical success depends on careful design choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as distribution shift, bias transfer, and rare-token loss.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible core of modern model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervisory signals from large teachers into smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of the teachers' capabilities. KD operates across multiple granularities (soft logits, internal features, attention or relational maps) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Despite strong empirical successes, open problems remain in handling data scarcity and distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, preserving rare or long-tail behavior, and providing principled theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The KD toolkit ranges from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and it is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines with pruning, quantization, and student-aware architecture design. Practical success depends on careful engineering choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, which data to use or synthesize, and how to diagnose and mitigate limits such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and distribution shift. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher utility across vision, language, and domain-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Vaughan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as the practical core of model‑compression pipelines: a flexible family of supervision signals and training regimes that, when combined with data strategies and architecture‑aware design, delivers deployable models that approach teacher performance. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher utility, but it has clear limits — including the risk of transferring teacher errors, difficulty with low‑frequency phenomena and domain shift, and constraints from privacy or data scarcity — that demand principled pipeline design and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals from a higher-capacity teacher to a compact student, KD enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of the original performance. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to student capacity, data availability, and task constraints, KD can yield large reductions in latency, memory, and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher's performance. Its practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, integrating complementary compression techniques, and addressing data- and distribution-related limitations through task-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of targets and workflows—soft-output matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention or relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free variants—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware design choices. However, its success depends on careful choices about distillation signals, data strategies, architectural alignment, and mitigation of optimization and robustness failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Engineering Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities, but it is design-sensitive: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or domain shifts determine outcomes. Framing KD as the central tool within a broader compression pipeline — combined with feature-level objectives, multi-teacher or data-synthesis strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) — leads to more reliable and deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Principled Path to Efficient, Adaptable, and Responsible NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a general framework that enables smaller or specialized models to inherit useful behaviors from larger teachers while controlling generalization, efficiency, and social impact. When combined with layer-wise and representation-level matching, task-aware architecture search, thoughtful input augmentation, and deployment-aware protocols, KD supports high-performance, resource-frugal NLP systems that can be adapted to heterogeneous devices and sensitive application contexts.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Deployable NLP: Power, Patterns, and Pitfalls
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic route to shrinking large NLP models into deployable students that retain much of their teachers' performance. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables real-world tradeoffs among accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy. Realizing those gains requires pairing KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and targeted diagnostics to address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and rare-token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. I argue KD should occupy a central place in compression pipelines because it reliably improves size–performance tradeoffs, but it must be adapted to task- and deployment-specific constraints (data regime, privacy, robustness, and fairness) and combined with complementary techniques to deliver robust, real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Bias Transfer, and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a model compression trick: it is a practical mechanism for transferring inductive biases, regularizing students, enabling privacy- and data-constrained deployments, and adapting architectures or modalities. When paired with complementary techniques—data augmentation, curriculum schedules, teacher ensembles, or generative replay—KD consistently narrows the gap between compact students and large teachers while addressing real-world constraints such as limited labeled data, compute, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, and Practical Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring supervision that goes beyond hard labels. The approach encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and progressive or self-distillation schedules. In practice, distillation is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, and data strategies (including data-free and synthesized-data regimes). Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and optimization curricula, and evaluating robustness, rare-token behavior, and bias propagation to ensure reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level behaviors), teacher–student variants (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data regimes (full-data, few-shot, and data-free adversarial synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, progressive module replacement) and when practitioners attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Open challenges include distillation under severe data heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior, and principled guarantees about robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their effectiveness. When combined with task-specific adaptations (layer mapping, data-free synthesis, federated protocols, quantization, or self-supervision), KD enables deployment in low-resource, privacy-sensitive, and domain-specific settings. Success depends on designing appropriate alignment mechanisms, data strategies, and fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a broad toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical distillation success depends on aligning transferred signals to student capacity, handling data and privacy constraints, and designing optimization and evaluation protocols that preserve accuracy and robustness in deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: Practical Benefits, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated not simply as a single recipe for compression but as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines. KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, and it naturally composes with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and domain-adaptive procedures. To deploy reliable compressed models practitioners must pair KD with careful teacher/student design, data and sample-selection strategies (including data-free synthesis where necessary), evaluation for robustness and fairness, and complementary compression steps that meet hardware constraints. This paper argues for a pragmatic, pipeline-oriented view of KD and outlines targeted practices to maximize utility while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The approach has diversified into many methods (soft-target/logit matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, relational and feature-level objectives), workflows (offline multi-stage, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data regimes (data-rich, data-scarce, and data-free). In practice, distillation is treated as a toolkit that must be combined with student-aware architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints while managing challenges such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, data/privacy limitations, and preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically effective approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure) and workflows (single- and multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free or synthesized-data approaches). When combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining most of teacher performance. However, realizing these gains in practice requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive and representational information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature treats KD as a flexible toolkit—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention, using multi-teacher or online protocols, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—and recommends integrating KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-aware strategies. Practical success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, student–teacher alignment, data availability or synthesis, and evaluation of robustness, rare-case fidelity, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Understandings of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive or representational information from larger, more expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, cheaper models while retaining as much performance as possible. Recent work has expanded KD beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-layer supervision, task-adaptive architecture search, online and federated variants, teacher optimization, and careful consideration of data and augmentation strategies. These advances enable practical compression for NLP and wider deep-learning applications by improving efficiency, robustness, and suitability for resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with careful teacher–student engineering, appropriate distillation signals, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, its reliability depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, alignment of representations, and explicit mitigation of robustness, privacy, and rare-token or distribution-shift failures. I argue KD should be the core of any real-world compression strategy, but only when embedded in an engineering-aware pipeline that anticipates and corrects its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller models by transferring predictive and representational information from teachers to students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical pipelines combine soft-target matching, representation-level imitation, architecture-aware design and search, and data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving synthesis). While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can enable students that are substantially faster and smaller, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and teacher quality; important open problems remain in robustness, domain shift, and theoretical explanation.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful student–teacher alignment, and data strategies adapted to privacy or scarcity constraints. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, reliable deployment requires targeted engineering to manage capacity mismatch, robustness, bias transfer, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Beyond Compression to Fairness, Robustness, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to compress large models into smaller, faster students, but its potential extends much further. When applied thoughtfully—via feature-level mimicking, progressive module replacement, teacher selection and confidence-weighting, and by combining with automated search or divergence choices—KD can improve fairness, domain adaptation, generative model compression, and student robustness while preserving or even improving task performance. This essay argues that KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that should be matched to specific goals (efficiency, fairness, transferability, or generation), and gives concrete methodological recommendations informed by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. The literature characterizes KD by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, layer mappings), how teachers and students are aligned (architecture-aware mappings, progressive curricula, multi- or online-teachers), and which complementary steps are used (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis). KD functions both as a compression mechanism and a training paradigm that can improve regularization, calibration, and robustness when carefully designed, but it faces limits from data availability, teacher–student mismatch, optimization dynamics, and transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a component of a broader compression pipeline tailored to task, data, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed models (teachers) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models (students). KD has been used to (1) transfer inductive biases across architectures, (2) compress large pretrained language and vision models into task- or deployment-aware students, (3) combine and condense ensembles into single models, (4) enable privacy- or data-constrained distillation, and (5) improve student generalization via richer supervision beyond hard labels. Practical KD systems balance fidelity to the teacher, student capacity and architecture, data availability, privacy constraints, and deployment budgets; recent work addresses these trade-offs through architecture search, meta-learning teachers, multi-teacher designs, data-free synthesis, and specialized intermediate-feature matching losses. Despite broad empirical success, theoretical work highlights conditions where soft labels help (and when hard labels correct imperfect teachers), pointing to ongoing research directions in teacher design, student architecture search, privacy guarantees, and robust data-efficient distillation.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP and other modalities. KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs when its design is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, but it requires engineering choices and complementary techniques to address robustness, fairness, and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural models for deployment and domain-specialization. Beyond simple teacher-to-student label matching, modern KD techniques transfer intermediate representations, exploit synthetic or augmented data, operate without original training data, and incorporate privacy or distributed-training constraints. These variants enable retaining much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, supporting domain adaptation, improving generalization under limited-data regimes, and meeting privacy or latency requirements for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's behavior. A growing literature shows KD can act via soft-target matching, intermediate representation transfer, attention- or relation-based losses, self-distillation, online and data-free variants, and can be combined with pruning, layer-skipping, quantization, or architecture search. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, recommendation, and graphs) when its signal, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match the deployment constraints. Important open issues remain — handling rare or low-frequency behaviors, adapting across domains and heterogeneous architectures, and operating under strict privacy or data-availability constraints — but pragmatic pipelines that mix KD with complementary compression tools offer the most reliable path to deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful, Composable, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely produces favorable size–performance trade-offs when designed to match student capacity and data regimes, but its success depends on careful signal selection, data strategies, and safeguards to avoid optimization failures or the propagation of teacher harms. Effective deployments treat KD as a toolbox to be combined with complementary compression methods and monitoring practices.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a flexible training paradigm that enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By choosing what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to generate or select data (real, public, or synthesized), and how to schedule and regularize student training, practitioners can shape trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy. KD’s effectiveness depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and data regime; when combined with multi-teacher strategies, adversarial data synthesis, or differential-privacy mechanisms, KD supports practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Schwartz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to internal representations and relational objectives—KD composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Successful application requires careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit validation for robustness and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller or more usable forms while attempting to retain performance. Methods range from transferring soft targets to matching intermediate representations, to data-free and federated protocols that address privacy and communication constraints. These approaches have been applied across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks and are used both for deployment efficiency and for secondary goals such as interpretability or domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal structure. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce latency and memory, adapt models to new domains, enable privacy- or data-constrained deployments, and condense ensembles into single deployable models. Effective distillation blends choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, layers), how to pretrain or adapt compact architectures, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance, achieving robust, fair, and domain-appropriate students requires careful design of teachers, student architectures, and distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD is widely used across vision, speech, and language tasks to reduce latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance. Effective pipelines combine choices about what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), how to manage data (original, augmented, synthesized, or absent), and how to align teacher and student architectures and training schedules. Practical success requires addressing capacity mismatch, data or privacy limits, teacher imperfections, and robustness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool for Compression — Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. KD enables large reductions in inference cost while preserving much of a teacher model’s performance, and it composes well with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, data dependence, heterogeneous deployment constraints, and distributional or robustness concerns mean practitioners must design distillation pipelines carefully and combine KD with complementary techniques to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from one or more teacher models into smaller students so they retain much of the teacher’s capabilities with lower compute, memory, or latency. The literature spans a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and common integrations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pre-training of compact models). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and inductive biases, what data to use (or synthesize), and constraints around deployment, privacy, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Johnston
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD encompasses output-level (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols. In practice KD is a composable component of compression pipelines and is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or synthetic-data strategies. While KD frequently retains much of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its effectiveness depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher and student co-design, data availability, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD can preserve much of a teacher model’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. Real-world success depends on choosing what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data when needed, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. KD is highly effective in practice but requires careful engineering to avoid propagating teacher shortcomings or failing under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds when designers move beyond naive soft-label matching to combine multiple transfer signals (logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, pre-training, or synthetic data), and deployment-aware adaptations (layer mapping, capacity-aware objectives, and composition with pruning/quantization). Its power in practice comes from this flexibility, but realizing it requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance when its objectives, data regime, and teacher–student alignment are chosen to match deployment constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, careful combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-token or domain-shift behaviors. I argue KD should be treated as the central technique in model-compression pipelines, applied with engineering rigor and complementary methods to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practitioner-oriented technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones suitable for deployment. When paired with complementary methods (architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data augmentation, and privacy-aware protocols), KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to source or synthesize data, how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, and how to evaluate robustness and social harms under deployment constraints.
