papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while retaining most task performance. KD methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate representations, using synthesized or absent data, and adopting specialized training schedules or teacher designs; they are most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines that include architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data strategies. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness—so practitioners should treat KD as a core tool that must be adapted to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Effective compression in practice requires matching the distillation technique to the deployment objective: using self-distillation or multi-teacher strategies to extract richer supervisory signals, combining KD with architecture search or pruning for task-specific efficiency, applying appropriate soft/hard label mixing informed by bias–variance tradeoffs, and controlling data and privacy considerations during distillation. When these elements are combined, KD can deliver substantial runtime and memory savings with minimal accuracy loss, making it central to deploying modern NLP systems under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and settings, KD methods range from matching teacher soft targets (logits) to aligning intermediate representations, combining multiple teachers, synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable, and integrating with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical distillation must balance student capacity, the form of transferred knowledge, data availability and privacy constraints, and optimization strategies to produce compact models that preserve accuracy, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, high-impact way to compress large models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining most task performance. Modern KD methods extend beyond matching final logits to include layer- and feature-level imitation, task-aware selection of distilled information, data-free or few-shot regimes, and multi-teacher or self-distillation strategies. When combined with architecture-aware compression or search, KD enables task-adaptive, privacy-conscious, and efficient deployment of deep models in real-world NLP and vision applications.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones for deployment in constrained environments. KD techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational signals, and operating in data-limited or privacy-sensitive regimes via synthesized or public data. When combined with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, architecture search), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Persistent challenges include understanding the mechanisms of transfer, handling student–teacher capacity mismatch, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, and ensuring robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Sandoval
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a broad toolkit—logit and softened output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and tailored to student capacity and data availability, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. Practical deployment requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to teacher–student mismatches, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Pipeline-Oriented Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a practical, composable toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models. In real systems KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when it is chosen and tuned with respect to the student capacity, the distillation signals, available data, and deployment constraints. Robust, production-ready compression pipelines pair KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and use diagnostics and task-aware strategies to avoid pitfalls such as capacity mismatch, degraded long-tail behavior, and inadvertent bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: robust, fair, and private compression requires careful choice of distilled signals, layer/representation alignment, data strategies (including synthesis or privacy-aware protocols), and combination with complementary methods like pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is flexible across signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations), workflows (multi-stage, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. To realize reliable, production-ready compressed models, practitioners must pair KD with careful student pre-training, data strategies, mitigation of bias and rare-token failures, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD methods transfer information via soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals, or ensemble guidance. Effective KD pipelines combine appropriate distillation targets, teacher–student alignment (layer mapping or projectors), data strategies (public, augmented, or synthesized), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and attention to robustness and fairness. Best practice emphasizes task-aware choices, representation-level objectives, multi-stage or curriculum training, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, deployment-oriented family of techniques that transfer information from larger or multiple teachers into smaller students. KD can be applied at the level of logits, intermediate representations, or task-specific modules and is readily combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis methods to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teacher's performance in compressed models, realizing its benefits in NLP requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to mitigate optimization and data-shift issues. With thoughtful protocol design, KD enables wide deployment of powerful language models under realistic resource limits, but it remains important to pair distillation with representation-aware objectives and engineering practices to avoid degrading rare-token behavior or amplifying teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used framework for compressing large, high‑performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure), and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as capacity mismatch, robustness degradation, privacy leakage, and poor long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Case
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible route to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains when its objectives, data strategy, and student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: it must be treated as a context-sensitive toolbox that is combined with complementary compression and robustness practices to avoid degraded rare-case behavior, propagated teacher flaws, or distribution-shift failures.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, and Practical Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring supervision that goes beyond hard labels. The approach encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and progressive or self-distillation schedules. In practice, distillation is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, and data strategies (including data-free and synthesized-data regimes). Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and optimization curricula, and evaluating robustness, rare-token behavior, and bias propagation to ensure reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Context-Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential, versatile method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining softened-output supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies, and architecture-aware design—KD regularly yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, its success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of transfer signals, data availability, and deployment constraints determine outcomes. Real-world adoption therefore requires pipeline-oriented practices that combine KD with complementary compression techniques and targeted evaluation for robustness, domain shift, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. It is a broadly applicable and practical approach across modalities (vision, language, graphs, multimodal) that enables reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. Modern practice treats distillation as a toolkit—combining soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate representation matching, specialized architectures or projectors, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols—to fit deployment constraints. Despite empirical effectiveness, distillation faces persistent challenges including data availability and privacy, teacher–student mismatches, optimization instability, and preservation of rare-token or low-frequency behavior; practical pipelines must therefore be tailored to task, data, and hardware requirements.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from teachers to students and are effective across modalities and tasks when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Success depends on principled choices about distillation targets, student capacity, data selection or synthesis, and mitigation of distribution-shift, rare-token, and bias-amplification failures. KD therefore functions best as a central, design-sensitive component of end-to-end model-compression pipelines that balance accuracy, latency, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile empirical framework for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and structured prediction, KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (e.g., softened outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure) and is commonly integrated with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical pipelines emphasize task- and student-aware design, careful teacher selection or training, and data-management choices; when applied thoughtfully KD can recover much of a teacher's performance but still faces challenges in robustness, domain shift, fairness, and theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that high performance can be retained under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across modalities KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer transfers of internal features, attention, or relational structure, and it is usually combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthetic, or data-free). Empirical results show large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest accuracy loss in many settings, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for creating smaller, faster models from large, high‑performing teachers so deployments meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The KD literature has expanded from simple soft‑target matching to a toolbox of methods that transfer logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational structure; integrate with pruning, quantization, and architecture search; and adapt to settings with limited or private data. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data strategy, and careful alignment of transfer signals; persistent challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, distribution shift, and the risk of propagating teacher artifacts or biases.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: Practical Benefits, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated not simply as a single recipe for compression but as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines. KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, and it naturally composes with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and domain-adaptive procedures. To deploy reliable compressed models practitioners must pair KD with careful teacher/student design, data and sample-selection strategies (including data-free synthesis where necessary), evaluation for robustness and fairness, and complementary compression steps that meet hardware constraints. This paper argues for a pragmatic, pipeline-oriented view of KD and outlines targeted practices to maximize utility while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Gay
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Empirically, KD routinely yields strong size–accuracy trade-offs across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, but its success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals to student capacity, attention to data availability and domain shift, and checks for transferred biases and rare-token degradation. Remaining challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models, and robustly distilling across heterogeneous architectures or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core component of compression pipelines and combined with task-aware design, representation-level guidance, data strategies, and complementary compression (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), KD routinely yields large reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, reliable deployment requires addressing capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, and the risk of transferring teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A mature toolbox has emerged that includes soft-label/logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). Practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, potential bias transfer, and robustness under distributional shifts; nonetheless, well‑designed KD pipelines routinely produce compact models that approach teacher performance across vision, language, speech, graph, and recommendation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly used approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—such as softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or many-to-many layer mappings—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of a teacher model’s performance. Effective distillation is context-sensitive: choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use or synthesize, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques determine outcomes. While KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy trade-offs in vision and language tasks, practical adoption requires engineered pipelines to manage capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness risks.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven a practical route to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone — including softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure — and works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and curriculum choices. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its success depends on matching transferred signals to student capacity, preparing suitable data or synthetic examples, and explicitly measuring effects on robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Responsible Use
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations and synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable. While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, its effectiveness depends on choices about transfer targets, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design‑Sensitive Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment objectives and combined with complementary compression methods, KD can recover most of a teacher’s utility while delivering substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy. However, distillation is context‑sensitive: the distilled signals, student capacity, data regime, and privacy or fairness constraints all shape outcomes. Treating KD as an essential but configurable toolbox—rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm—yields the most reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high‑impact route to compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques—feature alignment, data strategies, projector or adversarial mechanisms, and hardware‑aware design—it achieves strong size/accuracy/latency tradeoffs. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose limits such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and rare‑token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior, representations, or inductive biases. A diverse set of distillation strategies—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free synthesis, and task-aware adaptations—has been developed to preserve performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practice-oriented work emphasizes matching the distillation technique to the task, addressing data or privacy limits via synthetic examples or adversarial generation, and combining distillation with architecture and optimization adjustments to close remaining gaps. Empirical successes across language, vision, speech, graphs, and ranking systems show substantial speed and size improvements, though limits remain around distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, and heterogeneous or federated data settings.

papers_seen.author: Tyler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching to include intermediate-feature and relational signals, multi-stage and online workflows, and data-aware variants (including data-free or synthesized-data regimes). In practice KD is most effective when treated as the central, composable element of a broader compression pipeline that also employs pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data or privacy constraints, and explicitly addressing robustness, distribution shift, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented suite of techniques that reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis), KD enables efficient, accurate models for real-world vision and language applications. KD is not a plug-and-play cure: practitioner success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, which data or synthetic examples to use, and how to mitigate transferred biases or distributional shifts. With thoughtful, context-sensitive design, KD is the most practical and general-purpose strategy for producing compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in NLP: Benefits, Techniques, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for transferring the capabilities of large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis, or curriculum learning), KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. However, its success depends on careful choice of what signals to transfer, availability or synthesis of training data, and explicit handling of domain shift, student capacity mismatches, and potential amplification of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD techniques include matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-level transfers, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and appropriate pre-training or data strategies, KD often yields compact models that approach teacher performance. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate robustness, bias, and capacity-mismatch issues.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Across vision, language, and other modalities, KD operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and module-level replacements) and can serve both as a compression mechanism and as a broader training paradigm that improves calibration, generalization, and domain adaptation. Practical variants address constraints such as limited or private data, mismatched architectures, and deployment latency; persistent challenges include optimization failure modes, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and aligning internal representations between heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and multifaceted approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to train, and how to supplement distillation with complementary compression methods, KD can preserve most of a teacher's utility while meeting constraints on latency, memory, and privacy. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its success depends on student capacity, the distilled signal, data availability (including data-free regimes), and mitigation of teacher imperfections and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention-based signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and when tuned for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch between teacher and student, preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors, transferred biases and brittleness, and distillation under data- or heterogeneity-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and careful training curricula), KD reliably improves size–performance tradeoffs while requiring design choices that address capacity mismatch, data availability, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The literature shows KD is a versatile toolbox—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-teacher or self-distillation schedules, and deploying data-aware or data-free workflows—to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical and conceptual work highlights both practical successes (on-device deployment, domain transfer, and reduced inference cost) and persistent limits (data heterogeneity, rare-token fidelity, transferred bias, and teacher–student capacity mismatch), suggesting KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful method selection.

papers_seen.author: Gross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, or relational signals, and are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. Empirical work shows that KD typically narrows the performance gap between teacher and student across modalities, but practical success depends on careful choices about distillation targets, teacher preparation, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. When matched to task needs and combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and robustness or privacy-aware adaptations, KD enables small models to retain much of teachers' performance across modalities. However, KD is context-sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the chosen distillation signal determine outcomes. A pragmatic pipeline blends logit and feature matching, targeted data augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods to achieve robust, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under storage, latency, and privacy constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and using synthesized or public data—enable large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Success depends on choices about the form of transferred knowledge, teacher–student capacity matching, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression tools. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and aligning heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or structural signals; they are commonly combined with complementary compression strategies such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD has been adapted for data-poor, privacy-sensitive, and federated settings and is used across modalities (language, vision, graphs) and tasks (classification, generation, sequence modeling). While KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, practical success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, student architecture and pretraining, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness and fairness; remaining research challenges include understanding optimization limits, handling teacher imperfection and capacity mismatch, and preserving long-tail or distribution-shift behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Mccann
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller ‘‘student’’ models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Empirically, distillation reduces inference cost, memory and latency while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Practical distillation is a toolbox: soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-stage or online schedules, and data-aware strategies are combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation to meet deployment constraints. Important limits include student–teacher capacity mismatch, optimization instability, degradation on low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift in synthetic-data setups, and possible transfer of teacher biases or errors. Effective pipelines align distillation objectives with student capacity, use representation-level supervision when appropriate, and employ complementary techniques (pretraining, augmentation, curriculum annealing) to bridge gaps and improve robustness.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is not a single recipe but a flexible toolbox: its success depends on teacher design, the choice of distilled signal, data availability, and combination with complementary compression methods. When matched to task and deployment constraints, KD enables real-world use of pretrained models across vision, language, speech, graphs, and structured prediction, while open challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Mcdonald
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Pitfalls, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical pathway to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful engineering, KD often preserves most of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy footprint. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and explicit handling of teacher imperfections and low‑frequency behaviors. I argue KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in model compression pipelines but used with task‑aware design, diagnostics, and safeguards.
