papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Case
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible route to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains when its objectives, data strategy, and student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: it must be treated as a context-sensitive toolbox that is combined with complementary compression and robustness practices to avoid degraded rare-case behavior, propagated teacher flaws, or distribution-shift failures.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The literature frames KD as a toolkit that includes soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-representation alignment, layer- or module-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and curriculum schedules, data-augmentation or data-free approaches, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance when signals, data, and architectures are chosen deliberately; however, limits arise from capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, distributional shift, and the potential to transfer undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, spurious correlations). Practical pipelines therefore co-design teachers and students, select appropriate transfer signals, and pair distillation with data and system-level strategies to meet deployment constraints. Remaining research directions include better theoretical understanding, distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, student-aware teacher design, and fairness-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mcguire
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, and especially NLP, distillation operates at multiple granularities — softened output distributions, intermediate feature or attention alignment, and relational or module-level transfers — and is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and student pretraining. While distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s utility in a fraction of the compute or memory cost, practical deployment requires addressing capacity mismatch, data- and domain-shift, rare-token degradation, and propagation of teacher biases through careful method choice and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer forms of transfer (intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, attention or relational signals), and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (public, synthetic, or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely narrows the gap between teacher and student performance across modalities, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate failures such as degraded rare-token behavior, robustness issues, and amplified biases.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployable approach for compressing large neural and language models into smaller, faster students. By transferring information beyond hard labels—through softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals, or self-generated examples—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Real-world success requires combining KD with task-aware objectives, data strategies, and hardware-aware compression methods; attention to representation alignment, rare-token fidelity, and robustness is necessary to avoid common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds when designers move beyond naive soft-label matching to combine multiple transfer signals (logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, pre-training, or synthetic data), and deployment-aware adaptations (layer mapping, capacity-aware objectives, and composition with pruning/quantization). Its power in practice comes from this flexibility, but realizing it requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The literature characterizes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), multiple training workflows (offline teacher supervision, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula), and data strategies (full-data, limited-data augmentation, and data-free synthesis). KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to task, student capacity, and deployment constraints. Key practical challenges remain: optimization and capacity mismatch, preservation of rare-token or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and the danger of propagating teacher biases or errors.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is empirically effective across modalities because it transfers richer signals than hard labels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational cues) and composes with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). However, KD is engineering-dependent: data availability, teacher quality, and student–teacher mismatch create failure modes that require task-aware choices. A pragmatic compression pipeline treats KD as one component among data strategies, architecture adaptation, and hardware-aware tuning to achieve reliable, high-fidelity compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What is known about knowledge distillation and model compression in deep learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for turning large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD techniques include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, many‑to‑many layer mapping, multi‑teacher and online/meta‑teaching schemes, and data‑ or privacy‑aware synthesis. KD delivers strong empirical size/latency gains when combined with architecture preparation and task‑aware choices, but its effectiveness is bounded by optimization mismatch, teacher imperfections, data or distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns. Best practices emphasize combining logits and feature objectives, addressing representation mismatch (layer mapping, pretraining), and using data‑aware or privacy‑preserving strategies for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for producing compact models that retain much of the accuracy, inductive bias, and robustness of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit-matching, KD encompasses feature- and layer-level alignment, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, and data-aware or data-free workflows that together enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. When combined with careful objectives, curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping, KD can serve both as a primary compression mechanism and as a general-purpose training paradigm for regularization and adaptation. However, realizing its full value requires attention to teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and the choice of distilled signals to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: French
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The approach spans matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and staged or online teacher–student schedules. KD is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or privacy-aware protocols), and complementary compression techniques such as pruning or quantization. Practical deployment requires addressing capacity mismatch, data or distributional shift, and the risk of propagating teacher errors; when these are handled, KD produces compact models that often retain much of the teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — via softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula — to produce compact models that trade only a small fraction of predictive performance for large gains in latency, memory, and deployability. Across modalities and tasks, KD is best applied as part of a broader compression pipeline (including pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design) and requires attention to teacher quality, distilled signals, data strategy, and evaluation for robustness and fairness to realize reliable production systems.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s behavior. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods vary by the form of transferred signal (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, or module behaviors), training setting (offline, online, federated, or data-free), and complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, selecting appropriate distillation objectives for the task and data regime, and mitigating distributional or token-frequency artifacts introduced during distillation. This synthesis summarizes major approaches, empirical findings, limitations, and practical strategies for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with task-aware design, representation-level objectives, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires careful choice of distillation signals, attention to data and privacy constraints, and explicit evaluation of robustness and failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The literature shows KD is a versatile toolbox—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-teacher or self-distillation schedules, and deploying data-aware or data-free workflows—to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical and conceptual work highlights both practical successes (on-device deployment, domain transfer, and reduced inference cost) and persistent limits (data heterogeneity, rare-token fidelity, transferred bias, and teacher–student capacity mismatch), suggesting KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful method selection.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Representation- and Deployment-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable core of compression pipelines and extended beyond logits to internal representations and deployment constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Effective application requires careful teacher/student design, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information that goes beyond hard labels. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a toolbox of techniques that include intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher curricula, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. This synthesis summarizes the principal methods, practical combinations with other compression techniques, and the main limitations and open problems that shape current research and deployment choices.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled, Practical, and Context-Sensitive Toolbox for NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable systems. When treated as a flexible framework rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and domain heterogeneity. However, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to adapt to new domains or architectures, and how to select or synthesize training signals for the student.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. It is a broadly applicable and practical approach across modalities (vision, language, graphs, multimodal) that enables reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. Modern practice treats distillation as a toolkit—combining soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate representation matching, specialized architectures or projectors, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols—to fit deployment constraints. Despite empirical effectiveness, distillation faces persistent challenges including data availability and privacy, teacher–student mismatches, optimization instability, and preservation of rare-token or low-frequency behavior; practical pipelines must therefore be tailored to task, data, and hardware requirements.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Careful, and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints; supports domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization; and can be combined with other compression techniques. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align layers and representations, how to generate or augment data for distillation, and how to mitigate propagated errors or biases from teachers.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature frames distillation as a multifaceted toolkit — including soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols — that is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and data constraints, and on explicitly addressing failure modes such as transferred biases, optimization mismatch, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed models (teachers) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models (students). KD has been used to (1) transfer inductive biases across architectures, (2) compress large pretrained language and vision models into task- or deployment-aware students, (3) combine and condense ensembles into single models, (4) enable privacy- or data-constrained distillation, and (5) improve student generalization via richer supervision beyond hard labels. Practical KD systems balance fidelity to the teacher, student capacity and architecture, data availability, privacy constraints, and deployment budgets; recent work addresses these trade-offs through architecture search, meta-learning teachers, multi-teacher designs, data-free synthesis, and specialized intermediate-feature matching losses. Despite broad empirical success, theoretical work highlights conditions where soft labels help (and when hard labels correct imperfect teachers), pointing to ongoing research directions in teacher design, student architecture search, privacy guarantees, and robust data-efficient distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring richer supervisory signals from larger teacher models to compact students. KD operates across multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals) and is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture design, data strategies, and complementary primitives such as pruning and quantization. Important practical concerns include teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), robustness and fairness, and task-aware evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so they meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. Across vision, language, generative, and structured prediction tasks, KD has been adapted from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate-layer supervision, multi-teacher schedules, student-aware teacher training, data- and augmentation-aware pipelines, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When applied with attention to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs, but its success depends on careful signal selection, teacher–student alignment, and strategies to mitigate capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods provide practical mechanisms to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students suitable for real-world deployment. Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners use KD to trade off capacity and efficiency while aiming to preserve task performance, often in combination with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Success depends on aligning teacher signals, student capacity, data strategy, and optimization schedules; remaining challenges include handling domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior, and operating under privacy or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with representation-aware objectives, careful pre-training of compact models, and safeguards for robustness and privacy, KD enables production-ready reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher's performance. I argue that KD should be treated as a central tool in model-compression pipelines, not as a single recipe but as a family of methods to be combined with task-aware design choices for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive capacity from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The field encompasses simple soft-target matching as well as richer forms of transfer such as intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while offering large gains in latency, memory, and deployability; theoretical and empirical analyses emphasize mechanisms including soft-target regularization, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics. Practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to use data (including synthetic or public data), and how to address robustness, fairness, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses techniques that transfer predictive behavior (soft logits), intermediate representations, and relational or structural signals; it can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployments extend KD to privacy-preserving, federated, and data-poor scenarios, and leverage online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths in producing compact models for NLP and vision, while also identifying limits related to optimization, teacher imperfection, data mismatch, and distributional shifts that must be addressed by careful engineering and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Fisher

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and several data strategies (including data-free or privacy-aware workflows). KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware pretraining) and when practitioner choices align teacher signals, student capacity, and available data. While KD can recover much of teacher performance with large efficiency gains, it has known failure modes—optimization difficulty, teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena—that require tailored design, diagnostics, and hybrid pipelines to address.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths include multiple forms of transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational information), compatibility with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and applicability in data- and privacy-constrained settings. Realizing these benefits in practice requires careful choices about the signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, data management (real, augmented, or synthesized), and measures to detect and remedy robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift issues.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. It succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (e.g., softened logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals), and by combining with complementary techniques (pruning, low-precision inference, architecture search, and data augmentation). KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to adapt teachers and students to deployment constraints. Thoughtful design — including feature-level transfer, curriculum or selective-sample strategies, augmentation, and data-free synthesis when needed — makes KD a practical cornerstone of model compression for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. When engineered carefully—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD yields large efficiency gains while preserving most task performance. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data and curriculum choices, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, enabling deployment under computation, memory, and latency constraints. A range of techniques—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-stage pipelines, and data synthesis—have been developed to address diverse practical needs such as on-device inference, privacy-sensitive releases, federated settings, and domain shifts. Combining KD with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapting distillation signals to task and deployment constraints yields the best real-world outcomes, while open challenges remain around handling distribution shift, data scarcity, and student–teacher capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller models that retain much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teachers. KD supports a spectrum of deployment goals — reduced latency and memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and robustness improvements — and works best when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, feature matching, synthetic-data generation, pruning, or quantization). However, KD is not a universal solution: outcomes depend on teacher quality, what signals are transferred, data fidelity, and design choices that align distilled knowledge to the downstream task. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices and awareness of KD failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural networks by training smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models. Across vision, language, speech and graph settings, KD variants—matching softened teacher logits, aligning intermediate features, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enable large reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Realizing these gains requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to map layers between architectures, how to select or synthesize training data, and how to balance regularization from soft targets with student capacity and robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hughes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD works across modalities by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, and relational signals, and it is most effective when integrated with architecture-aware compression, pre-training of compact architectures, data strategies, and explicit robustness and fairness checks. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a core component — not a standalone cure — and emphasizes signal selection, layer alignment, and safeguards for distributional or ethical failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students that meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD operates at multiple granularities — softened logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals — and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data‑free synthesis) to yield strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, its success is context dependent: KD can propagate teacher errors, struggle under domain shift or data scarcity, and interact with architectural or optimization mismatch. Thus, KD should be treated as the central tool in model compression pipelines, applied with explicit design choices, complementary compression methods, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment, domain adaptation, or constrained hardware. Research has explored matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, module-replacement strategies, data-augmented or data-free distillation, robustness-aware objectives, and task-aware selection of transferable knowledge. Empirical work spans language models (including BERT), reading comprehension, retrieval/ranking, and vision tasks, demonstrating trade-offs between compression ratio, accuracy retention, robustness, and required access to teacher training data. Best practices emphasize careful choice of distillation signal (logits, attention, hidden activations), augmentation or synthesis of training examples when data are scarce, and filtering or adapting teacher knowledge to the student’s capacity and target task.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing small, deployable models from large teachers. Treated as a core, composable element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, student capacity, and data availability; practitioners must also mitigate risks such as transferred biases, poor long‑tail behavior, and distributional shift. I argue that KD should be the default backbone of practical compression workflows, but applied in a context‑sensitive way and evaluated for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applied approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the last decade has expanded KD beyond simple logits matching into intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher and progressive curricula, data-aware and data-free workflows, and combinations with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). KD functions both as a compression mechanism and as a training paradigm that can improve calibration and generalization, but it has known failure modes—teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, domain shift, and degradation on rare or low-frequency phenomena—that require targeted diagnostics and hybrid pipelines. Practical deployment of KD therefore depends on matching distilled signals and protocols to student capacity, data availability, task constraints, and hardware targets.
