papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a flexible training paradigm that enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By choosing what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to generate or select data (real, public, or synthesized), and how to schedule and regularize student training, practitioners can shape trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy. KD’s effectiveness depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and data regime; when combined with multi-teacher strategies, adversarial data synthesis, or differential-privacy mechanisms, KD supports practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a family of methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). These approaches aim to retain predictive performance while reducing model size, latency, or enabling deployment under privacy or communication constraints. Recent work broadens distillation beyond logits to intermediate features, attention maps, multi-teacher setups, and data-limited or privacy-preserving regimes, producing task- and domain-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models by transferring information from larger teacher models, enabling deployment under computation, memory, or latency constraints. Across vision, speech, language, and recommendation systems, KD takes many forms — logit matching, feature mimicking, ensemble compression, and data-free synthesis — and is often combined with model pruning, architectural simplification, or curriculum strategies. Effective distillation requires choices about what to transfer (soft targets vs. intermediate features), how to supply or synthesize data, and how to schedule or regularize training; these choices shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research across computer vision, graph learning, and natural language processing has explored why distillation helps, when it fails, and how to improve it via soft labels, representation alignment, data augmentation, multi-teacher schemes, and teacher training strategies. Work also studies fairness, privacy, and domain-specific adaptations, showing that distillation is a flexible framework but one whose benefits depend strongly on optimization, data, and the design of teacher-student interactions.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—using richer targets than logits, aligning intermediate representations, and combining with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search—KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of a teacher's performance. KD also adapts to constrained settings (few-shot, federated, or data-free) and supports robustness and domain adaptation when pipelines are designed to match task and deployment constraints. Realizing KD's full value requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of approaches that trade off capacity, latency, and privacy to deploy high-performing deep models in constrained settings. Methods operate at different places in the training pipeline: compressing via soft-targets, transferring intermediate representations, searching or adapting compact architectures, or avoiding access to original data. Work across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and medical imaging) shows that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, relations, feature directions, layer mappings) and how to transfer it (attention, contrastive alignment, adversarial generators, or task-aware filters) determines final student performance. Practical concerns such as domain adaptation, federated and heterogeneous-device settings, and data augmentation interact strongly with distillation design choices. The literature suggests a clear pattern: representation-level and layer-aware transfers often outperform naive logits-only approaches for structured or pre-trained models, while teacher-free, data-free, and communication-efficient variants enable distillation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses techniques that transfer predictive behavior (soft logits), intermediate representations, and relational or structural signals; it can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployments extend KD to privacy-preserving, federated, and data-poor scenarios, and leverage online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths in producing compact models for NLP and vision, while also identifying limits related to optimization, teacher imperfection, data mismatch, and distributional shifts that must be addressed by careful engineering and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the most practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, language, and other modalities. When applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), designing teacher-student pairs, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) — distillation recovers much of a teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD also serves beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve robustness and generalization, but it is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization differences, and risks of transferring biases or vulnerability must be managed through targeted practices and evaluations.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. When applied with careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data and privacy constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks. KD is most effective when combined with complementary techniques—feature projectors, adversarial objectives, student-aware teacher training, and privacy-preserving mechanisms—so that compressed models meet real-world latency, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller models that retain much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teachers. KD supports a spectrum of deployment goals — reduced latency and memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and robustness improvements — and works best when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, feature matching, synthetic-data generation, pruning, or quantization). However, KD is not a universal solution: outcomes depend on teacher quality, what signals are transferred, data fidelity, and design choices that align distilled knowledge to the downstream task. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices and awareness of KD failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds when designers move beyond naive soft-label matching to combine multiple transfer signals (logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, pre-training, or synthetic data), and deployment-aware adaptations (layer mapping, capacity-aware objectives, and composition with pruning/quantization). Its power in practice comes from this flexibility, but realizing it requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD spans simple soft-target matching to a rich set of representation- and layer-level objectives and is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture/parameter search). Practical success requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When treated as a context-sensitive component of a compression pipeline, KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP and other modalities. KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs when its design is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, but it requires engineering choices and complementary techniques to address robustness, fairness, and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller or more usable forms while attempting to retain performance. Methods range from transferring soft targets to matching intermediate representations, to data-free and federated protocols that address privacy and communication constraints. These approaches have been applied across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks and are used both for deployment efficiency and for secondary goals such as interpretability or domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on task, data availability, optimization choices, and robustness or fairness requirements. Practical deployment requires tailored curricula, representation-aware objectives, and integration with methods like pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-stage or curriculum schemes, and combining distillation with other compression methods — and is widely used for deploying models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Success depends on matching distillation objectives and data strategies to deployment goals and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms — soft-target regularization, transfer of intermediate representations, and alignment of optimization/inductive bias — and is most reliable when integrated into engineering pipelines that account for data availability, teacher-student mismatch, and deployment constraints. While KD is not a silver bullet, its versatility and compatibility with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies make it the natural default for production-focused compression.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD comprises a family of methods — from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or privacy-prespecting variants — that together enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and power while retaining much of teacher performance. Its success in production settings depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle scarce or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign).

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Tyler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching to include intermediate-feature and relational signals, multi-stage and online workflows, and data-aware variants (including data-free or synthesized-data regimes). In practice KD is most effective when treated as the central, composable element of a broader compression pipeline that also employs pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data or privacy constraints, and explicitly addressing robustness, distribution shift, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Why and How Knowledge Distillation Enables Practical Compression for Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained and ensemble models deliver state-of-the-art accuracy in NLP and other deep learning domains but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide principled ways to transfer predictive behaviour and internal representations from expensive teachers into compact students. When combined with careful pre-training, feature-level matching, layer-mapping strategies, data augmentation, and curriculum design, distillation yields models that approach teacher accuracy while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude or more. This paper argues that KD is both necessary and practical for deploying high-quality compact models and outlines concrete, evidence-backed strategies to maximize its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-label matching and richer forms of transfer — intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data approaches, and online or mutual distillation. In practice, KD is most effective when its signal, data strategy, and architectural alignment are chosen with the task and deployment constraints in mind and when distillation is combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Despite strong empirical gains across modalities, limitations remain: teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and degradation on rare or low-frequency behaviors can reduce fidelity and robustness, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. The literature characterizes KD by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, layer mappings), how teachers and students are aligned (architecture-aware mappings, progressive curricula, multi- or online-teachers), and which complementary steps are used (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis). KD functions both as a compression mechanism and a training paradigm that can improve regularization, calibration, and robustness when carefully designed, but it faces limits from data availability, teacher–student mismatch, optimization dynamics, and transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a component of a broader compression pipeline tailored to task, data, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other structural knowledge from teacher(s) to student(s). Approaches range from classic logit-matching to feature- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, data-free adversarial methods, and adaptations for distributed or heterogeneous settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing size and latency; practical success depends on choices like what form of knowledge to transfer, whether and how to augment or synthesize data, and how to handle heterogeneous compute or domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and federated protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often yields substantial gains in student performance versus training from scratch and enables deployment under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy, but outcomes depend on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and checks for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD methods include matching soft teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention patterns, transferring relational structure, multi-teacher and staged pipelines, online or self-distillation, and data‑free or synthetic-data protocols. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when practitioners account for teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and deployment constraints. Despite routine empirical wins across vision, language, multimodal, and large-scale settings, persistent challenges remain: distribution shift and rare-token robustness, propagation of teacher biases, architectural mismatch, and privacy-sensitive or data‑scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models by transferring informative behavior from a teacher to a smaller student so the student can meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The approach includes matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention/relational signals, and using online, self-, curriculum- or data-free regimes. Practical success depends on the distilled signal, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of data, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Remaining challenges include teacher–student optimization mismatch, robustness and domain shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or severely data-limited settings.

papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds when designers move beyond naive soft-label matching to combine multiple transfer signals (logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, pre-training, or synthetic data), and deployment-aware adaptations (layer mapping, capacity-aware objectives, and composition with pruning/quantization). Its power in practice comes from this flexibility, but realizing it requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. When applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline it reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Achieving robust, fair, and private deployments requires combining KD with architecture-aware design, appropriate data strategies (including data-free alternatives), careful choice of distilled signals, and systematic evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple models into smaller, faster models by leveraging softer training signals, intermediate representations, or alternate training protocols. Research has explored KD’s theoretical underpinnings, practical training strategies (including teacher-ensemble and teacher-free variants), privacy- and communication-aware settings, and extensions beyond classification to generation and structured prediction. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s ability to reduce deployment cost while retaining or sometimes even improving downstream performance, but trade-offs remain around data availability, representation matching, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing which signals to transfer, matching student capacity to tasks, and combining distillation with architectural and data strategies—KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for on-device, latency-sensitive, and domain-specific NLP systems. Its advantages are balanced by contextual failure modes (teacher imperfections, distribution shift, rare-token fidelity) that require pipeline-level engineering, careful evaluation, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

A practical metric, the stddev of teacher\'s mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Evidence, and Practical Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft outputs, features, attention/relations), can be combined with pruning/quantization/architecture design, and generalizes across vision, speech, and NLP tasks. Real-world success requires attention to student capacity, data strategies, distributional shift, and mitigation of propagated biases or rare-token failures. Selective and staged distillation, teacher optimization, and task-aware engineering yield the best trade-offs between accuracy and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior), whether distillation is offline, online, or federated, and how it is combined with architecture search, pruning, or privacy mechanisms. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployments across on-device, distributed, and data-scarce settings; however, practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and addressing data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Vasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals—enabling students to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy. Its success in real systems depends on matching transfer targets to student capacity, supplying appropriate data or synthetic substitutes, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is powerful and production-ready, but not automatic: careful design, evaluation for robustness and fairness, and integration into broader compression pipelines are required to produce reliable, deployable models.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment goals—through careful choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression methods—KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and attention to robustness, privacy, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved from matching softened teacher outputs to a rich toolbox that includes intermediate representation transfer, attention or relation-level objectives, data-free and online methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when its signals, data strategy, and student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. Important open problems remain around capacity mismatch, long-tail or rare-token behaviors, distribution shift, and avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployable approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, resource-efficient students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD consistently yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when designers choose appropriate distilled signals, handle data limitations, and integrate KD with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not automatic: its practical success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, data availability (or synthetic-data substitutes), and task-aware training curricula. When combined with feature-level methods, projectors, curriculum strategies, and privacy- or device-aware protocols, KD enables compact models that remain useful in production while requiring careful engineering to avoid optimization and fairness pitfalls.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. A diverse toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, creating synthesized distillation data, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs across speech, vision, recommendation, graph, and language tasks, but practical success depends on careful choices about teacher signals, student capacity, data regimes, and evaluation of robustness and distributional behavior.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for shrinking large neural models into compact, deployable students. As a composable toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer softened outputs, intermediate features, and relational structure, and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Modern KD spans matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, layerwise and relational losses, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Empirical practice shows KD recovers much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design), careful data and curriculum choices, and explicit handling of capacity, optimization, and distribution-shift failure modes. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended workflows for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression — Central, Useful, but Not Enough Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When engineered to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD produces strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs and integrates well with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies. However, KD must be combined with representation-aware objectives, task-aware layer mapping, and safeguards for robustness and fairness to avoid transferring teacher imperfections and to preserve rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing appropriate distillation signals, handling data constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques — KD can recover most of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on student capacity, representation alignment, optimization schedules, and careful mitigation of teacher biases and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Recipes, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature or attention alignment, layer-mapping strategies, and combined pipelines that integrate pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models relative to training from scratch and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and quality, and careful alignment of teacher and student architectures. Ongoing challenges include robustly preserving teacher properties (robustness, fairness), operating under data scarcity or privacy limits, and automating architecture and signal selection for effective transfer.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language applications KD has been extended from simple soft-label matching to a wide set of techniques—intermediate-representation transfer, layer-aware alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free variants, and adversarial or projector-based feature matching—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD both preserves predictive performance and can improve generalization in many settings, while also raising practical challenges such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena that require targeted mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques that enables large deep models to be compressed into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance when applied with attention to what signals are transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teachers and students are aligned. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on deliberate pipeline design, complementary compression methods, and strategies for dealing with data scarcity, domain or modality mismatch, rare-token behavior, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains across domains by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or task-specific behaviors from teachers to students. Its strengths are practical: it supports deployment on constrained hardware, enables multi-teacher and cross-model transfer, and integrates with other compression tools. At the same time, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: theoretical and empirical work shows limits under data heterogeneity, imperfect teachers, and mismatched architectures, so KD must be applied with task-aware choices (signal type, layer alignment, teacher selection, and curricula) and often combined with complementary methods to realize reliable, high-fidelity compression.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (original, public, synthesized, or data-free) have been developed. Distillation is typically used as the central component of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, and architecture design; its practical success depends on matching transfer signals to student capacity, teacher quality, and data availability while attending to robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied as a design-sensitive set of techniques—combining soft-target transfer with representation-aware objectives, data strategies (including data-free synthesis and self-distillation), and complementary compression methods—KD delivers strong size/accuracy/latency trade-offs while supporting privacy- and deployment-aware constraints. KD is not a panacea: it can transfer teacher weaknesses and struggle under data or capacity mismatch, so responsible pipelines require careful choice of signals, staged training, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Mcdonald
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Pitfalls, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical pathway to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful engineering, KD often preserves most of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy footprint. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and explicit handling of teacher imperfections and low‑frequency behaviors. I argue KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in model compression pipelines but used with task‑aware design, diagnostics, and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is treated as a core, engineering-aware component of a broader compression pipeline — combined with careful choice of distillation signals, attention to data availability, and complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search — it reliably improves student efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance. To realize these benefits in practice, practitioners must align teacher and student capacity, select which teacher signals to transfer (logits, features, relations, or internal representations) according to task needs, manage data constraints with augmentation or generative strategies, and actively mitigate transferred weaknesses such as bias or low-frequency errors. This position argues that KD should be adopted as a context-sensitive, composable central strategy for model compression, accompanied by methodical safeguards and task-aware integration with other compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a broad toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical distillation success depends on aligning transferred signals to student capacity, handling data and privacy constraints, and designing optimization and evaluation protocols that preserve accuracy and robustness in deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, composable component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD is versatile—able to transfer logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data-synthesis techniques to produce deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data and distributional constraints, and explicitly addressing fairness and robustness concerns. When designed and evaluated carefully, KD enables effective trade-offs between efficiency and task performance across modalities.
