papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. It is a broadly applicable and practical approach across modalities (vision, language, graphs, multimodal) that enables reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. Modern practice treats distillation as a toolkit—combining soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate representation matching, specialized architectures or projectors, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols—to fit deployment constraints. Despite empirical effectiveness, distillation faces persistent challenges including data availability and privacy, teacher–student mismatches, optimization instability, and preservation of rare-token or low-frequency behavior; practical pipelines must therefore be tailored to task, data, and hardware requirements.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a highly practical, versatile technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller students that retain much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary compression primitives and designed for the student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields deployable models with substantially lower latency and memory. However, KD is not a universal cure: effectiveness depends on what is distilled, how data (real or synthetic) are used, and how risks such as bias transfer, robustness loss, and privacy exposure are managed. I argue KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines but applied with explicit mitigations and task‑aware engineering.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD can be adapted across modalities and constraints—by matching soft logits, intermediate representations, or attention maps; by using ensembles or teacher optimization; and by operating with or without original training data—making it well suited to real-world deployment needs. Because its effectiveness depends on representation alignment, teacher–student design, and data regime, KD is best applied as a component in broader compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware choices) and selected to fit the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations, transferring attention or relational signals, staged or progressive replacement strategies, and self-distillation. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data, teacher–student, and optimization choices to meet deployment constraints. Although KD often recovers much of teacher performance, persistent limits remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token behavior, bias transfer, and data- or privacy-constrained scenarios, so engineering and diagnostics are required for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD variants—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, self- and online-distillation, and data-free (zero-shot) synthesis—enable latency, memory, and privacy gains across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what signals are distilled, teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, and pipeline choices (layer mapping, curricula, and complementary compression). I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines, applied with task-aware design and combined with other methods to manage its limitations and maximize deployment utility.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language, KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature, attention, and relational imitation—are combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) and data strategies (using original, public, or synthesized data) to produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, composable component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD is versatile—able to transfer logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data-synthesis techniques to produce deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data and distributional constraints, and explicitly addressing fairness and robustness concerns. When designed and evaluated carefully, KD enables effective trade-offs between efficiency and task performance across modalities.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is flexible across signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations), workflows (multi-stage, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. To realize reliable, production-ready compressed models, practitioners must pair KD with careful student pre-training, data strategies, mitigation of bias and rare-token failures, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Mechanisms, Extensions, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-focused strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. Its practical value arises from multiple mechanisms — not only teacher imitation but also regularization, representation transfer, and optimization effects — and from combinations with data strategies and complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the central, engineering-ready backbone of compression pipelines, while practitioners explicitly address data regimes, privacy, domain shift, and bias transfer when designing distillation workflows.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Core of Model Compression — and How to Use It Safely
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high-impact approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller students suitable for deployment. KD can transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, or training dynamics to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. Effective, production-ready compression treats KD as the central engine but pairs it with complementary techniques (representation alignment, projectors, pruning/quantization, privacy-aware protocols and ensemble or multi-teacher strategies). KD yields strong size–performance tradeoffs in both vision and NLP when engineered for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; however, practitioners must also manage limitations such as transferred biases, capacity mismatch, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, module- or layer-wise mapping) and appear across domains including NLP, vision, multimodal, federated, and graph settings. Practical pipelines combine KD with data strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, teacher imperfections, and preserving properties such as low-frequency token fidelity, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When executed as the centerpiece of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (representation matching, data strategies, and hardware-aware design), KD routinely yields strong size/accuracy/latency trade-offs. However, KD is not automatic: realizing its benefits requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose robustness and fairness risks.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal problems, KD is used alone or combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-centric strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Empirical and analytical work highlights mechanisms behind KD’s success, practical recipes for improving student fidelity, and persistent challenges (data mismatch, rare-token behavior, robustness, and optimization). This synthesis summarizes methods, applications, practical recommendations, and key open problems reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and online protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical application of KD requires matching the distilled signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; addressing failure modes such as transferred biases or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena; and integrating distillation into a broader compression pipeline to meet latency, memory, and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Responsible Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD shines when combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, but its reliability depends on careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data or robustness constraints are handled. I argue KD should be treated as a central instrument in compression pipelines, used with explicit engineering and ethical practices to manage its limits.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for producing compact models that retain much of the accuracy, inductive bias, and robustness of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit-matching, KD encompasses feature- and layer-level alignment, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, and data-aware or data-free workflows that together enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. When combined with careful objectives, curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping, KD can serve both as a primary compression mechanism and as a general-purpose training paradigm for regularization and adaptation. However, realizing its full value requires attention to teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and the choice of distilled signals to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's capability. KD is flexible: it can match logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; it can be combined with augmentation, architecture search, pruning, or task adaptation; and it can operate with or without original training data. When applied with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to address data or optimization mismatches, KD enables practical deployment of compact models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central component of any compression strategy and summarizes concrete practices to maximize its effectiveness and mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds when the distillation signals, data strategy, and architecture choices are matched to deployment constraints; its most reliable use combines logits-based supervision with representation-level alignment, multi-stage curricula, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful pipeline design is required to avoid transferring teacher errors, to handle low-frequency phenomena and domain shifts, and to meet privacy or data-limited requirements.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Path to Deployable NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models deliver state-of-the-art results in many NLP tasks but are often too large or too costly for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques enable retaining much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and inference cost. Advances in task-aware, layer-wise, data-free, and adversarially-informed distillation methods demonstrate that KD can address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and heterogeneity in deployment environments, making it a central tool for practical NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible pathway to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD frameworks span matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when distillation targets and training protocols are chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. KD therefore forms an indispensable but context-sensitive core of modern model-compression toolkits for NLP and deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and multimodal tasks, distillation techniques—including self-distillation, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, and teacher adaptation—enable substantial reductions in model size and compute with limited accuracy loss. KD is complementary to other compression strategies (e.g., pruning and architecture search) and benefits from careful choices in intermediate-target selection, data augmentation, and teacher-student alignment. When combined thoughtfully with task adaptation and hardware-aware techniques, KD unlocks feasible deployment of advanced models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Power, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques and careful engineering it can deliver substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a drop-in cure: success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to prepare teachers and students, how to handle data scarcity or privacy constraints, and how to preserve robustness and fairness. This essay argues that KD should be treated as a flexible core of compression pipelines, and it summarizes practical strategies and caveats for effective, responsible deployment.

papers_seen.author: Villa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is most effective when treated as a central component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses architecture-aware design, data curricula, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Real-world success requires careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data regime, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes such as degraded rare-token modeling and privacy-sensitive transfer.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods form a broad set of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. These techniques are applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), deployment scenarios (edge devices, federated learning), and objectives (accuracy preservation, efficiency, interpretability, fairness). Advances include theoretical reframings that connect KD to regularization, a range of strategies for aligning outputs and internal representations, methods that restructure or progressively replace model components, and practical systems that enable heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments. Despite clear empirical gains, open problems remain in understanding when and why different distillation targets (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior) are most effective, and how to balance compression with robustness and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of learned structure so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes feature- and representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Practical application requires task- and deployment-aware choices that balance accuracy, latency, data availability, and social/robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is flexible across signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations), workflows (multi-stage, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. To realize reliable, production-ready compressed models, practitioners must pair KD with careful student pre-training, data strategies, mitigation of bias and rare-token failures, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Responsible Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD reduces latency, memory use, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance when practitioners choose appropriate distillation targets, match student capacity, combine KD with complementary compression methods, and evaluate for robustness and fairness. KD is most effective when treated as part of a compression pipeline—using representation-aware objectives, staged training, and data strategies (including synthesis or privacy-aware protocols)—but it is not a universal cure: capacity mismatch, teacher artifacts, rare-token behaviors, and distribution shift remain important failure modes that must be addressed by design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching into a flexible toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention-level objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free workflows, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When applied with task- and deployment-aware design choices (what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and what data or augmentations to use), KD routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs in vision and NLP. Practical deployments require careful engineering to handle capacity mismatch, imperfect teachers, privacy constraints, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: A Practical, Multifaceted Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central, practical tool for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a multifaceted framework—combining soft-label supervision, intermediate representation matching, data- and task-aware training, and architecture-aware design—distillation reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, distillation must be applied carefully: teacher imperfections, low-frequency token behavior, data scarcity, and domain shifts can undermine student quality unless addressed via targeted strategies such as exposing raw data, tailoring teacher signals, and integrating complementary compression methods. With careful engineering and principled choices about what and how to transfer, distillation enables high-performing, efficient models across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach that enables deploying large deep and language models by training smaller students to retain much of the teacher’s performance. When combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data strategies, and teacher–student alignment, KD delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy with modest accuracy loss. However, KD requires task-aware choices, diagnostic checks, and mitigation for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones for deployment in constrained environments. KD techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational signals, and operating in data-limited or privacy-sensitive regimes via synthesized or public data. When combined with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, architecture search), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Persistent challenges include understanding the mechanisms of transfer, handling student–teacher capacity mismatch, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, and ensuring robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models by transferring information from larger teacher models, enabling deployment under computation, memory, or latency constraints. Across vision, speech, language, and recommendation systems, KD takes many forms — logit matching, feature mimicking, ensemble compression, and data-free synthesis — and is often combined with model pruning, architectural simplification, or curriculum strategies. Effective distillation requires choices about what to transfer (soft targets vs. intermediate features), how to supply or synthesize data, and how to schedule or regularize training; these choices shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile paradigm for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match deployment constraints—by selecting suitable distillation signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, its success is not automatic: capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and fine-grained or rare-behavior preservation require targeted design choices and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods enable transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teachers to smaller students so models can be deployed under computation, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature shows a spectrum of approaches — from matching softened output distributions to feature- and layer-level imitation, attention-guided alignment, data-free or zero-shot synthesis of training examples, and distributed or privacy-aware protocols — and demonstrates successful applications across vision, speech, recommendation, and many NLP tasks. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distillation signal, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student architecture alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include handling imperfect teachers, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and maintaining robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade, practitioners have developed a spectrum of distillation signals and pipelines—ranging from soft-logit matching to representation and attention alignment, data-free synthesis, and integrated workflows that combine pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design—to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical practice shows distillation routinely improves compact models relative to training from scratch, but its success is engineering-dependent and sensitive to student capacity, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical tool for compressing deep and NLP models because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD excels when combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, but it is not a panacea: careful design choices are required to handle capacity mismatch, limited data, distribution shift, imperfect teachers, and transferred biases. A disciplined pipeline — choosing appropriate distillation signals, augmenting or synthesizing data when necessary, and aligning teacher–student architectures — yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information that goes beyond hard labels. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a toolbox of techniques that include intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher curricula, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. This synthesis summarizes the principal methods, practical combinations with other compression techniques, and the main limitations and open problems that shape current research and deployment choices.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Engineering-Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer outputs, intermediate representations, relationships, or curricula and supports data-free, multi-teacher, and online variants. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation) and careful teacher–student alignment, KD reliably reduces inference cost and storage while often preserving generalization. However, its success depends on design choices—what to transfer, how to handle limited or private data, and how to align capacities and optimization—so KD should be treated as a core component of a compression pipeline rather than a plug-and-play remedy.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. The literature identifies several methodological families — soft-label/logit matching, intermediate representation or feature mimicking, layer-wise and many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data-free/synthetic-data strategies — and shows that KD often works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to the task and deployment constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, while practical deployment raises challenges in data availability, teacher-student architecture mismatch, robustness, and privacy in federated or distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller models that retain much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teachers. KD supports a spectrum of deployment goals — reduced latency and memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and robustness improvements — and works best when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, feature matching, synthetic-data generation, pruning, or quantization). However, KD is not a universal solution: outcomes depend on teacher quality, what signals are transferred, data fidelity, and design choices that align distilled knowledge to the downstream task. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices and awareness of KD failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, practitioners use soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher or online schedules, and data-aware strategies (including synthetic or augmented data) to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical pipelines combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, limited or private data, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving low-frequency or fairness-critical behaviors. The field emphasizes task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select data, and how to align teacher and student for dependable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. It is applied across modalities and deployment constraints and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data and teacher design, and methods that address representation mismatch and optimization. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended practices for using KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Pillar for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables deployment on resource-limited devices, supports privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, and combines effectively with pre-training, data augmentation, and structured compression. I argue that KD should be a default component of any production-aware model compression pipeline, augmented by task- and data-aware techniques to preserve robustness and accuracy.
