papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. The practice has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift challenges.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. The approach spans simple soft-target matching to richer strategies that align intermediate features, use online or multi-teacher schemes, and combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When applied with attention to teacher design, student capacity, data availability, and fairness/robustness checks, KD provides an effective toolkit for producing compact models suited to real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The KD toolkit ranges from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and it is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines with pruning, quantization, and student-aware architecture design. Practical success depends on careful engineering choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, which data to use or synthesize, and how to diagnose and mitigate limits such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and distribution shift. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher utility across vision, language, and domain-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-centered paradigm for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations via signals that range from softened logits to intermediate features, attention maps, and relational objectives. KD is most effective when its signals, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints, and when it is combined with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design). Important practical concerns include robustness transfer, privacy when original data are sensitive or unavailable, and alignment when teacher and student use heterogeneous inputs or detectors. The field continues to refine methods for representation alignment, adversarial and privacy-preserving distillation, and modality-specific adaptations to close the gap between teacher and student performance while meeting real-world latency and memory limits.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. By transferring supervisory signals beyond hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and safeguards for fairness and robustness. I argue KD should be treated as the central organizing method in practical compression pipelines, while noting concrete failure modes and recommending principled mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student so the student retains much of the teacher’s predictive power while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature has expanded KD beyond matching teacher soft-labels to include intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, online/self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and combinations with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical results across vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and ranking show that distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but practical success depends on choices like teacher design, student capacity, layer alignment, data availability, and training schedules. Remaining challenges include handling low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, optimization and capacity mismatch, matching heterogeneous architectures, and distilling under privacy or data-scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for NLP Model Compression: Promise, Proofs, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large NLP and deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques—such as architecture-aware compression, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis—KD can deliver much of a teacher model’s performance while greatly reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation is not without limits: it can propagate teacher biases, depends on careful choice of what and how to transfer, and requires task- and data-aware engineering to be robust in low-data or privacy-sensitive settings. A pragmatic pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies for representation alignment, sample selection, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compress large neural models for real-world deployment. When applied carefully — via multi-stage pipelines, layer-aware mappings, internal-representation transfer, self-distillation, or even without original data — KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. KD also composes effectively with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet diverse resource constraints. These properties make KD a central technique for bringing large pretrained models into production in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for creating smaller, faster models from large, high‑performing teachers so deployments meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The KD literature has expanded from simple soft‑target matching to a toolbox of methods that transfer logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational structure; integrate with pruning, quantization, and architecture search; and adapt to settings with limited or private data. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data strategy, and careful alignment of transfer signals; persistent challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, distribution shift, and the risk of propagating teacher artifacts or biases.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment goals—through careful choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression methods—KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and attention to robustness, privacy, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Practical Role and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers so that high-performing systems can be deployed under storage, latency, or privacy constraints. KD succeeds across modalities by transferring soft outputs, internal representations, or relational structure, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and thoughtful data or curriculum design. However, distillation has inherent limitations—optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and sensitivity to data selection—that require methodical engineering (choice of signals, projectors, augmentation, and, where necessary, data-free procedures) to realize robust, fair, and efficient students in real-world NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, and Practical Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring supervision that goes beyond hard labels. The approach encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and progressive or self-distillation schedules. In practice, distillation is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, and data strategies (including data-free and synthesized-data regimes). Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and optimization curricula, and evaluating robustness, rare-token behavior, and bias propagation to ensure reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Deployable NLP: Power, Patterns, and Pitfalls
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic route to shrinking large NLP models into deployable students that retain much of their teachers' performance. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables real-world tradeoffs among accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy. Realizing those gains requires pairing KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and targeted diagnostics to address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and rare-token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Duarte
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables large gains in inference efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression techniques and task‑aware engineering. However, KD is not a silver bullet: success depends on what is distilled, how teacher and student are matched, how data or privacy constraints are handled, and how robustness and fairness are evaluated and mitigated.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach has expanded from soft-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, self-distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical deployments succeed when distillation objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and task-aware choices are tuned to the application; remaining challenges include preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, handling distribution shift and data scarcity, and ensuring robustness and privacy in deployed students.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of learned structure so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes feature- and representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Practical application requires task- and deployment-aware choices that balance accuracy, latency, data availability, and social/robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Holt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The toolbox includes matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-free or synthetic-data generation. KD is frequently combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tailored training curricula to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, access to suitable data (or reliable synthetic substitutes), and attention to optimization, robustness, and fairness; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transfer of rare or biased behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention/relational signals, and can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies (including synthesized or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely improves student performance when design choices are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints, but practitioners must address challenges such as distribution shift, low-frequency behavior loss, and transfer of undesirable teacher properties.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential, Combinable, and Context‑Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, enabling lower latency, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment when paired with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on data regime, teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, and the choice of distilled signals. A principled pipeline treats KD as a toolbox—combining logits and feature targets, multi‑teacher schedules, data synthesis or privacy‑aware protocols, and hardware‑aware compression—to produce robust, task‑appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language, KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature, attention, and relational imitation—are combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) and data strategies (using original, public, or synthesized data) to produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When used as the central, composable component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies), KD routinely delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. Its real-world success requires task‑aware choices about which signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention or relational maps), how to align teacher and student capacity, what data to use or synthesize, and what safeguards to adopt for robustness, fairness, and privacy. I argue that KD should be treated as the core tool in model compression but applied with explicit diagnostics, curricula, and integration with other compression techniques to manage its known failure modes and maximize practical utility.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What is known about knowledge distillation and model compression in deep learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for turning large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD techniques include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, many‑to‑many layer mapping, multi‑teacher and online/meta‑teaching schemes, and data‑ or privacy‑aware synthesis. KD delivers strong empirical size/latency gains when combined with architecture preparation and task‑aware choices, but its effectiveness is bounded by optimization mismatch, teacher imperfections, data or distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns. Best practices emphasize combining logits and feature objectives, addressing representation mismatch (layer mapping, pretraining), and using data‑aware or privacy‑preserving strategies for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s utility under resource constraints, realizing its benefits in production requires deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred errors and biases. A pragmatic KD pipeline combines soft-target matching with representation-level supervision, architecture-aware adaptation, and complementary compression methods to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, distillation variants (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, layer mapping, online or multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware strategies) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair distillation with data augmentation, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression methods to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness to distribution shift, and preserving fairness and rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be adopted as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. KD’s flexibility—matching softened outputs, aligning representations, and operating with or without original data—lets practitioners trade compute and memory for minimal accuracy loss when combined with complementary compression methods. Careful design around teacher quality, student capacity, and data regimes is necessary to avoid transferring biases or degrading robustness.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly used approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—such as softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or many-to-many layer mappings—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of a teacher model’s performance. Effective distillation is context-sensitive: choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use or synthesize, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques determine outcomes. While KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy trade-offs in vision and language tasks, practical adoption requires engineered pipelines to manage capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness risks.

papers_seen.author: Sampson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD operates by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (for example softened logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals), and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task- or data-aware training protocols. Practical success requires matching distillation signals to student capacity and deployment goals, careful handling of data availability (including data‑free or synthesized approaches), and safeguards for robustness, long‑tail behavior, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information that goes beyond hard labels. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a toolbox of techniques that include intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher curricula, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. This synthesis summarizes the principal methods, practical combinations with other compression techniques, and the main limitations and open problems that shape current research and deployment choices.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller models by transferring predictive and representational information from teachers to students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical pipelines combine soft-target matching, representation-level imitation, architecture-aware design and search, and data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving synthesis). While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can enable students that are substantially faster and smaller, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and teacher quality; important open problems remain in robustness, domain shift, and theoretical explanation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teacher models. KD works by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (architecture-aware compression, pruning, quantization) and careful data and evaluation practices. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, what signals are distilled, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices, staged training, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD comprises a family of methods — from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or privacy-prespecting variants — that together enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and power while retaining much of teacher performance. Its success in production settings depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle scarce or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign).

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer performance and representational properties from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. Across tasks in vision, language, graph learning, and generative modeling, researchers have developed strategies that extend beyond matching final logits: layer-wise and representation matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, private/distilled deployment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and task-adaptive compression. These approaches trade off fidelity, privacy, and computational cost, and they have been shown to enable real-world deployment of pretrained language models and other deep systems while revealing open challenges in distribution shift, heterogeneous data, and preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible strategy for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. However, KD is not a panacea: its benefits depend on teacher quality, signal selection, data availability, and task alignment; therefore practitioners should adopt task-aware distillation targets, careful teacher–student alignment, and evaluation on robustness and long-tail behaviors.

The literature shows a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline teacher supervision, online/self-distillation, adversarial objectives), and practical integrations with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies. Success depends on aligning distillation targets to student capacity, choosing appropriate data or synthesis techniques, and explicitly addressing robustness, bias, and domain-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. A diverse toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, creating synthesized distillation data, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs across speech, vision, recommendation, graph, and language tasks, but practical success depends on careful choices about teacher signals, student capacity, data regimes, and evaluation of robustness and distributional behavior.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller or more usable forms while attempting to retain performance. Methods range from transferring soft targets to matching intermediate representations, to data-free and federated protocols that address privacy and communication constraints. These approaches have been applied across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks and are used both for deployment efficiency and for secondary goals such as interpretability or domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, KD functions as a toolbox: it can transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; be combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization; and operate with or without original training data. KD delivers substantial reductions in size and latency with modest performance loss when methods and signals are chosen to match student capacity, task requirements, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context-sensitive: success depends on handling teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness concerns, data availability, and optimization choices. The most reliable pipelines therefore combine multiple distillation signals, data-aware strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as bias transfer and rare-token degradation.

papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful, Composable, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely produces favorable size–performance trade-offs when designed to match student capacity and data regimes, but its success depends on careful signal selection, data strategies, and safeguards to avoid optimization failures or the propagation of teacher harms. Effective deployments treat KD as a toolbox to be combined with complementary compression methods and monitoring practices.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers while meeting deployment constraints on latency, memory, and privacy. KD encompasses a variety of supervision targets (softened outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and workflows (offline teacher-based training, online/multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free regimes). When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and appropriate pre-training or data strategies, KD often yields substantial size/efficiency gains. However, its success depends on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, handling data and distributional mismatch, and addressing robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Landscape of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models by transferring useful information from a teacher to a student, enabling deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention maps, relations) and how (feature matching, channel- or layer-wise alignment, augmentation, self- or data-free schemes). Distillation also serves broader roles beyond compression—regularization, bias transfer or mitigation, domain adaptation, and enabling multi-task or modality conversions. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signal, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and deployment constraints; these choices shape trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. The approach spans simple soft-target matching to richer strategies that align intermediate features, use online or multi-teacher schemes, and combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When applied with attention to teacher design, student capacity, data availability, and fairness/robustness checks, KD provides an effective toolkit for producing compact models suited to real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Domains, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer knowledge from larger, costly models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students) so that the students retain much of the teachers' accuracy while meeting deployment constraints. Across vision, language, graphs, and generative models, researchers have developed complementary approaches — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, channels, and global embedding topologies — and combined distillation with architecture search, pruning, and continual adaptation. Empirical work shows distillation can produce compact models that preserve or even improve task performance, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher-student inputs/representations, task- and domain-specific strategies, and trade-offs such as bias–variance effects introduced by soft labels. Important challenges remain around layer mismatches, low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and fundamental limits of compressibility for certain model families.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems meet deployment constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations or attention, and using multi-stage or data-aware pipelines. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware pretraining) and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy/latency trade-offs. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, robustness, and the risk of transferring teacher shortcomings; thus KD is best treated as the central tool inside a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad set of techniques has been developed — matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, mapping teacher layers to student layers, and operating in online, offline, multi-teacher, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is typically combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data, selective sampling). In practice, distillation often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory, but its success depends on student capacity, representation alignment, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that meet real-world constraints while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. When properly designed, KD extends beyond matching soft labels to include feature- and layer-level transfers, pre-training of small architectures, multi-stage curricula, and coordination with architecture search and other compression techniques. Careful attention to data, teacher–student capacity, and deployment objectives turns KD from a heuristic into a reliable engineering approach for compressing deep and NLP models.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods provide practical mechanisms to convert large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students suitable for real-world deployment. Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners use KD to trade off capacity and efficiency while aiming to preserve task performance, often in combination with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, or architecture adaptation. Success depends on aligning teacher signals, student capacity, data strategy, and optimization schedules; remaining challenges include handling domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior, and operating under privacy or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary component of practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it offers a flexible set of transfer signals and training regimes that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. However, KD is not a turnkey solution — its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When designers adopt representation-aware objectives, layer mappings, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit mitigation for capacity mismatch and long-tail behaviors, KD yields compact, deployable models that balance fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile paradigm for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match deployment constraints—by selecting suitable distillation signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, its success is not automatic: capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and fine-grained or rare-behavior preservation require targeted design choices and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is flexible across signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations), workflows (multi-stage, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. To realize reliable, production-ready compressed models, practitioners must pair KD with careful student pre-training, data strategies, mitigation of bias and rare-token failures, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Landscape of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models by transferring useful information from a teacher to a student, enabling deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention maps, relations) and how (feature matching, channel- or layer-wise alignment, augmentation, self- or data-free schemes). Distillation also serves broader roles beyond compression—regularization, bias transfer or mitigation, domain adaptation, and enabling multi-task or modality conversions. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signal, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and deployment constraints; these choices shape trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and deployment cost while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensembles), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Across vision and NLP tasks, distillation enables practical deployment of compact models but requires careful handling of representation mismatch, data availability, optimization schedules, and potential amplification of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes representation- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation variants, data-aware and data-free workflows, and curriculum or online schedules. In practice KD is most powerful when composed with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign or search) and when its targets, data, and training schedules are adapted to deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and robustness. Important open issues remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token/long-tail behaviors, and propagation of teacher biases; addressing these requires methodic engineering, careful evaluation, and continued empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach that enables deploying large deep and language models by training smaller students to retain much of the teacher’s performance. When combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data strategies, and teacher–student alignment, KD delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy with modest accuracy loss. However, KD requires task-aware choices, diagnostic checks, and mitigation for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented approach for shrinking large models into deployable students. When applied as a toolbox — not a single recipe — KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while meeting real-world constraints. Practical effectiveness hinges on choosing which signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Careful pipelines that address data availability, optimization mismatch, domain shift, and bias/robustness concerns enable KD to be the central component of reliable compression workflows.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted, Practical Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick of copying a stronger model but as a multifaceted training paradigm that can compress, regularize, and adapt models for deployment. When practitioners choose the right distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention mappings), tailor objectives to data and privacy constraints, and combine KD with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis), they can produce compact students that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness requirements. Effective use of KD requires attention to representation alignment, optimization schedules, and the constraints of the deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, faster students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across modalities, KD includes matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and distilling relational or attention signals; it is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Effective KD requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distillation targets, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and evaluation for robustness and fairness. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, and preserving long-tail behaviors, which motivate context-sensitive, pipeline-oriented compression practices.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved from matching softened teacher outputs to a rich toolbox that includes intermediate representation transfer, attention or relation-level objectives, data-free and online methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when its signals, data strategy, and student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. Important open problems remain around capacity mismatch, long-tail or rare-token behaviors, distribution shift, and avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. KD is effective across modalities (vision, speech, language, graphs) and settings (task-specific compression, data-limited or data-free transfer), and its strengths are amplified when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware replacement, pruning, low-precision numerics, adaptive teacher design, and careful input-side practices. To realize robust and fair compressed models, practitioners should treat KD as one tool within a pipeline: design student-friendly teachers, account for data constraints, use augmentation and curriculum where helpful, and combine KD with orthogonal compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Responsible Use
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations and synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable. While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, its effectiveness depends on choices about transfer targets, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Engineering Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile foundation for compressing deep and language models: it enables much smaller, faster students to capture substantial teacher performance while supporting deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD excels when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful engineering (choice of transferred signals, data augmentation, teacher selection). However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: it can propagate teacher imperfections, struggle with rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and face difficulties under heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data regimes. Treating KD as the central tool in a compression pipeline — but one that requires task-aware design and diagnostics — yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logit matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate‑representation transfer, attention and relational matching, multi‑teacher and online schemes, and data‑aware variants (including data‑free approaches). When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful engineering, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, choice of distillation signals, data strategies, and mitigation of robustness and bias issues.
