papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible pathway to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD frameworks span matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when distillation targets and training protocols are chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. KD therefore forms an indispensable but context-sensitive core of modern model-compression toolkits for NLP and deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Path to Model Compression in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. When applied thoughtfully — using layer-aware alignment, attention-guided feature matching, dynamic multi-teacher strategies, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols — distillation enables substantial speedups, reduced footprint, and cross-modal or cross-device applicability with small drops (or even gains) in task performance. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Make Knowledge Distillation the Default Compression Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP (with Practical Safeguards)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central technique for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students because it consistently delivers strong size–performance trade-offs while remaining flexible across tasks and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a single recipe: best results come from combining soft-targets with representation-level supervision, sensible student pre-training, data-aware curricula or synthesis, and complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization). Practitioners must also mitigate risks—transfer of teacher biases, optimization and capacity mismatches, and degradation on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena—through multi-teacher designs, careful signal selection, and validation under deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a highly practical, versatile technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller students that retain much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary compression primitives and designed for the student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields deployable models with substantially lower latency and memory. However, KD is not a universal cure: effectiveness depends on what is distilled, how data (real or synthetic) are used, and how risks such as bias transfer, robustness loss, and privacy exposure are managed. I argue KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines but applied with explicit mitigations and task‑aware engineering.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and production-ready approach for turning large, high-performing teachers into smaller, deployable students. Beyond pure parameter reduction, KD can regularize training, transfer internal representations, and enable privacy- or resource-aware workflows. Its practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps), how to prepare the student model and data, and which complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to apply. KD is therefore best treated as a flexible, context-sensitive toolkit rather than a single algorithm: when matched to student capacity, data constraints, and deployment goals, KD yields strong size–performance trade-offs; when misapplied it can amplify teacher biases, struggle on rare phenomena, or fail under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Approaches include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, mapping or projecting teacher layers to student layers, and operating in offline, online, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and designing curricula or multi-stage pipelines that reflect deployment needs. While distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance, open challenges remain in representation mismatch, amplifying teacher biases, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to lightweight students. Over the last decade KD has diversified from matching teacher soft-labels to a broad set of techniques—feature- and layer-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher/self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols. Empirical work shows KD frequently yields large reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to obtain or generate training data, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques. Important open issues include preserving rare-token behaviors, avoiding amplification of teacher biases, ensuring privacy in distributed settings, and understanding optimization dynamics that govern when and how distilled signals help.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be adopted as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. KD’s flexibility—matching softened outputs, aligning representations, and operating with or without original data—lets practitioners trade compute and memory for minimal accuracy loss when combined with complementary compression methods. Careful design around teacher quality, student capacity, and data regimes is necessary to avoid transferring biases or degrading robustness.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, teacher selection strategies, data-aware techniques, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD yields compact models that recover much of teacher utility while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Real-world success requires attention to student capacity, data mismatch, optimization dynamics, and societal risks such as bias or privacy leakage.

papers_seen.author: Walker

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. When paired with task-aware objectives, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary compression techniques, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective use of KD requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, which data to use or synthesize, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible core of modern model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervisory signals from large teachers into smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of the teachers' capabilities. KD operates across multiple granularities (soft logits, internal features, attention or relational maps) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Despite strong empirical successes, open problems remain in handling data scarcity and distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, preserving rare or long-tail behavior, and providing principled theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted strategy for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases. KD sits at the center of practical model compression pipelines: it can produce latency- and memory-efficient models for on-device or large-scale services, be combined with quantization and pruning, and be adapted for privacy-, data-, or compute-constrained settings. Effective distillation requires choices about what to transfer (soft labels vs. features), how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. When designed carefully, KD yields compact models that retain most of a teacher’s capabilities while meeting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven a practical route to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone — including softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure — and works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and curriculum choices. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its success depends on matching transferred signals to student capacity, preparing suitable data or synthetic examples, and explicitly measuring effects on robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs, and it integrates naturally with feature-level matching, data-free synthesis, online and federated protocols, and teacher-design strategies. However, its effectiveness depends on what is distilled (logits, features, attention), data availability and domain match, teacher–student capacity alignment, and objectives like robustness, privacy, and fairness. Real-world deployment requires matching distillation techniques to constraints and explicitly addressing robustness, bias, and data-privacy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-friendly family of techniques that enables large neural models to be converted into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When paired with complementary compression tools and careful data or curriculum design, KD supports real-world constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data scarcity and teacher bias, and evaluating robustness under distribution shifts.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The approach has diversified into many methods (soft-target/logit matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, relational and feature-level objectives), workflows (offline multi-stage, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data regimes (data-rich, data-scarce, and data-free). In practice, distillation is treated as a toolkit that must be combined with student-aware architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints while managing challenges such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, data/privacy limitations, and preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Pollard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer signals than hard labels. The method family includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature and attention alignment, structure- and channel-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data strategies ranging from heavy use of unlabeled data to data-free adversarial synthesis. Best practice couples distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware choices (pretraining, augmentation, privacy or federated protocols). Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints; open challenges include preserving long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Representation- and Deployment-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable core of compression pipelines and extended beyond logits to internal representations and deployment constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Effective application requires careful teacher/student design, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and using synthesized or augmented data—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Vasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals—enabling students to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy. Its success in real systems depends on matching transfer targets to student capacity, supplying appropriate data or synthetic substitutes, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is powerful and production-ready, but not automatic: careful design, evaluation for robustness and fairness, and integration into broader compression pipelines are required to produce reliable, deployable models.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high-impact strategy for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and tasks by transferring soft targets, internal representations, and relational signals; it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; and it supports production constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. When applied as a carefully designed pipeline—choosing appropriate distilled signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, and addressing data or domain gaps—KD enables pragmatic trade-offs that make compression feasible in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be Central to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths include multiple forms of transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational information), compatibility with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and applicability in data- and privacy-constrained settings. Realizing these benefits in practice requires careful choices about the signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, data management (real, augmented, or synthesized), and measures to detect and remedy robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift issues.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Across vision, language, and other modalities, KD operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and module-level replacements) and can serve both as a compression mechanism and as a broader training paradigm that improves calibration, generalization, and domain adaptation. Practical variants address constraints such as limited or private data, mismatched architectures, and deployment latency; persistent challenges include optimization failure modes, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and aligning internal representations between heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target matching, feature and attention alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher curricula, data synthesis or augmentation, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation)—enables practical trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Empirical and theoretical work indicates distillation often acts both as an information transfer mechanism and a regularizer; success depends on student capacity, data availability, choice of distilled signals, and careful handling of robustness and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-friendly family of techniques that enables large neural models to be converted into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When paired with complementary compression tools and careful data or curriculum design, KD supports real-world constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data scarcity and teacher bias, and evaluating robustness under distribution shifts.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation can transfer teacher weaknesses (biases, brittleness, low-frequency errors) and requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations across heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Practical deployment therefore calls for method selection tailored to task and constraints, plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural networks by training smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models. Across vision, language, speech and graph settings, KD variants—matching softened teacher logits, aligning intermediate features, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enable large reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Realizing these gains requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to map layers between architectures, how to select or synthesize training data, and how to balance regularization from soft targets with student capacity and robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable models. Beyond raw compression, KD can be adapted to meet constraints of privacy, heterogeneous devices, low-precision hardware, and domain or modality shifts. When combined with complementary techniques such as pre-training, layer-level supervision, or ensemble teachers, distillation can retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while enabling production usage that would otherwise be impractical. This essay argues that KD should be a primary tool in the model-compression toolbox for both research and engineering deployments, and that best results come from tailoring distillation objectives and pipelines to application needs.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables reduced storage and faster inference while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle when training data are unavailable or misaligned with deployment distributions, and interact subtly with optimization and architecture mismatch. A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies—feature- and layer-level objectives, data-free or synthesized-data protocols when needed, curriculum or sample-weighting policies, and hardware-aware pruning or architecture search—to maximize efficiency without sacrificing robustness or task-specific fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted, Practical Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick of copying a stronger model but as a multifaceted training paradigm that can compress, regularize, and adapt models for deployment. When practitioners choose the right distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention mappings), tailor objectives to data and privacy constraints, and combine KD with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis), they can produce compact students that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness requirements. Effective use of KD requires attention to representation alignment, optimization schedules, and the constraints of the deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision and language tasks. A broad family of KD variants—matching teacher logits, aligning intermediate features, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, data augmentation and data‑free synthesis, and architecture-aware co-design—enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Success depends on principled choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle limited or shifted data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques and fairness/privacy checks. KD is best treated as a central, adaptable component of a production compression pipeline rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. A broad toolkit has emerged—matching logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and training dynamics; using multi-stage or online pipelines; operating with or without original data; and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distillation reliably reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when the distillation signals, student capacity, and data regime are carefully matched. Practical deployment balances transfer choices, student architecture design, data or privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, using signals beyond hard labels to preserve generalization while reducing compute and memory. Modern work expands KD beyond soft logits to intermediate features, layer mappings, adversarial and attention-based objectives, and data- or resource-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech and NLP show that tailored distillation strategies can recover much of a teacher's performance in compact models, though challenges remain in data-free scenarios, handling imperfect teachers, and preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Why and How Knowledge Distillation Enables Practical Compression for Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained and ensemble models deliver state-of-the-art accuracy in NLP and other deep learning domains but are often too large or slow for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide principled ways to transfer predictive behaviour and internal representations from expensive teachers into compact students. When combined with careful pre-training, feature-level matching, layer-mapping strategies, data augmentation, and curriculum design, distillation yields models that approach teacher accuracy while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude or more. This paper argues that KD is both necessary and practical for deploying high-quality compact models and outlines concrete, evidence-backed strategies to maximize its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach that enables deploying large deep and language models by training smaller students to retain much of the teacher’s performance. When combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data strategies, and teacher–student alignment, KD delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy with modest accuracy loss. However, KD requires task-aware choices, diagnostic checks, and mitigation for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Combinations, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and pragmatic method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving much of a teacher’s performance, but its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), how teacher–student alignment is addressed, and how distillation is integrated with pre-training, architecture design, and other compression tools. I argue that KD should be treated as the central component of an engineering pipeline for efficient NLP and deep-learning systems: it provides flexible transfer mechanisms, enables many successful combinations (multi-teacher, layer mapping, data synthesis), and yields strong practical results, yet it must be paired with complementary strategies and careful choices to manage teacher imperfections, representation mismatch, data limitations, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and sometimes communication or privacy exposure. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention signals; it is commonly combined with complementary compression methods and with data or model-centric strategies to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and robustness and fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and using synthesized or augmented data—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and are most effective when combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful, deployment-aware engineering. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data, robustness, and privacy constraints are handled.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach for turning large pretrained models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher’s capability. When combined with representation-aware objectives, student pre-training, and complementary compression techniques, KD delivers substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy use while enabling deployment across language, vision, and multimodal tasks. Real-world success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, managing data (or synthesizing it), and applying safeguards for robustness and privacy, but the accumulated evidence recommends treating distillation as a central, configurable tool in compression pipelines rather than an isolated recipe.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven a practical route to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone — including softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure — and works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and curriculum choices. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its success depends on matching transferred signals to student capacity, preparing suitable data or synthetic examples, and explicitly measuring effects on robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary component of practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it offers a flexible set of transfer signals and training regimes that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. However, KD is not a turnkey solution — its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When designers adopt representation-aware objectives, layer mappings, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit mitigation for capacity mismatch and long-tail behaviors, KD yields compact, deployable models that balance fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teacher models. KD works by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (architecture-aware compression, pruning, quantization) and careful data and evaluation practices. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, what signals are distilled, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices, staged training, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used paradigm for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models into smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost while preserving much of predictive performance. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or no-data approaches), and workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, federated). Empirical and conceptual work emphasizes the importance of teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distillation signal, and combination with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Despite frequent success across vision, language, speech, and graphs, open challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect imitation, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, privacy-sensitive deployments, and adapting distillation to heterogeneous device or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and inductive biases across modalities and architectures, enabling large reductions in latency and memory with modest performance loss when applied thoughtfully. Realizing KD's benefits in production requires attention to what signals are transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, data selection or synthesis strategies, and safeguards for robustness and privacy. KD should be treated as a central component of compression pipelines but combined with complementary techniques and careful evaluation to address its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so that compact models can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data strategies (original data, public or synthesized data, and data-free or adversarial sample generation) has been developed. KD is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware search) and adapted to application domains (NLP, 2D/3D vision, federated settings). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match teacher and student capacity, and how to address distribution shift, rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Considerations, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A mature toolkit includes softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-singleton transfer, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Empirical practice shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned (architecturally and in optimization), and how data constraints, distribution shift, and downstream robustness or fairness needs are handled.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad family of KD methods—ranging from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals—enables practitioners to trade model size and latency for retained performance. In practice, KD is combined with data-aware strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. While KD is effective across vision and language tasks, success depends on careful choices about distilled signals, student capacity, data availability, and handling of domain shifts or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Pennington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Techniques vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression methods; practical success depends on aligning signals to student capacity and deployment constraints while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and are most effective when combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful, deployment-aware engineering. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data, robustness, and privacy constraints are handled.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Is Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across domains and deployment constraints—multi-task learning, low-resource devices, federated settings, data-free scenarios, and generative or detection tasks—KD enables targeted transfer of behavior, representations, and robustness. However, realizing KD's potential requires task-aware choices: which teacher(s) to use, what intermediate signals to mimic, how to select or synthesize training samples, and whether to incorporate adversarial or ensemble strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, selective sample strategies, and representation-level objectives, KD produces compact models that are accurate, efficient, and more widely deployable than large models alone.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals from a higher-capacity teacher to a compact student, KD enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of the original performance. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic training trick into a broadly applicable, practical toolkit for compressing large models for deployment in constrained environments. KD enables substantial size and latency reductions while retaining much of teacher performance; it supports different transfer signals (logits, features, attention), works with or without original training data, and can be adapted to preserve robustness or meet privacy constraints. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students (including pre-training), how to handle limited or heterogeneous data, and how to mitigate transferred biases or adversarial vulnerability. Combining distillation with complementary strategies—layer-aware matching, feature-level mimicry, data synthesis or augmentation, teacher optimization, and robustness-aware objectives—gives the most reliable practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic, widely applicable pathway to convert large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and by combining with complementary compression primitives, KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success is design-sensitive: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness determine whether distillation yields reliable, production-ready models.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. When engineered carefully—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD yields large efficiency gains while preserving most task performance. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data and curriculum choices, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models by transferring useful information from one or more teacher models to a smaller student model, enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and domain- or deployment-specific adaptation. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), teacher-management strategies (ensembles, multi-teacher weighting, teacher-training), data strategies (data-aware curricula, data-free synthesis), and complementary techniques (projector layers, adversarial objectives, curriculum schedules). Empirical work shows that careful selection of what to transfer and how to align teacher and student—balanced with attention to optimization dynamics and data constraints—produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, privacy, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure so students meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The paradigm has evolved from matching soft logits to a broad toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data- or architecture-aware pipelines. Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability (including data-free alternatives), and careful alignment of signals and training dynamics. KD has been applied across domains (machine translation, recommender systems, 3D vision, text generation) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware practices; open issues remain around distribution shift, propagation of teacher artifacts, low-frequency behavior, fairness, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher. Techniques extend beyond using teacher soft outputs (soft labels) to include internal representation matching, layer alignment, task-aware selection of teacher information, data-free synthesis, online mutual teaching, and architecture search guided by distillation. Practical work on NLP (especially BERT-family models), generative models, and domain- or modality-specific settings demonstrates that combining pre-training, architecture-aware search, and representation-level distillation often yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and downstream performance. Open challenges remain around imperfect teachers, optimization and capacity mismatch, data availability, and robustness/generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The literature frames KD as a toolkit that includes soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-representation alignment, layer- or module-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and curriculum schedules, data-augmentation or data-free approaches, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance when signals, data, and architectures are chosen deliberately; however, limits arise from capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, distributional shift, and the potential to transfer undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, spurious correlations). Practical pipelines therefore co-design teachers and students, select appropriate transfer signals, and pair distillation with data and system-level strategies to meet deployment constraints. Remaining research directions include better theoretical understanding, distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, student-aware teacher design, and fairness-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Lee

Research across vision and language shows KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal structure via multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, layer mappings) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that, when adapted to student capacity and data regimes, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, but its success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, data strategies, and optimization curricula. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a flexible toolbox to be composed with complementary compression methods and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Farrell

Beyond simple logit-matching, KD encompasses feature- and layer-level alignment, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, and data-aware or data-free workflows that together enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. When combined with careful objectives, curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping, KD can serve both as a primary compression mechanism and as a general-purpose training paradigm for regularization and adaptation. However, realizing its full value requires attention to teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and the choice of distilled signals to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Peterson

Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Cook
