papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The field encompasses a range of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), training workflows (single- and multi-stage, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and practical integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical and conceptual work points to several mechanisms that make distillation effective (soft-target regularization, representation alignment, and inductive-bias transfer) and identifies recurring deployment concerns such as architecture mismatch, data availability, domain shift, and robustness. Best practices emphasize matching distillation signals to student capacity, using layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods for realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger pretrained or ensemble teachers in deep learning and NLP. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and aligning teacher and student architectures — KD recovers much of the teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioners explicitly guard against capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, and the propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated via soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data-aware schemes. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data or augmentation choices, KD frequently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Practical success requires tailoring distillation signals, addressing teacher–student capacity and representation mismatches, and attending to data quality and distributional issues.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD can be adapted across modalities and constraints—by matching soft logits, intermediate representations, or attention maps; by using ensembles or teacher optimization; and by operating with or without original training data—making it well suited to real-world deployment needs. Because its effectiveness depends on representation alignment, teacher–student design, and data regime, KD is best applied as a component in broader compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware choices) and selected to fit the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to the match between distilled signals and student capacity, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods, KD consistently yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Responsible deployment requires explicit handling of optimization gaps, distributional shift, rare-token behavior, privacy constraints, and fairness concerns. I argue KD should be treated as the practical centerpiece of compression pipelines, but only when used as a context‑sensitive toolbox combined with principled safeguards and complementary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a highly practical, versatile technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller students that retain much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary compression primitives and designed for the student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields deployable models with substantially lower latency and memory. However, KD is not a universal cure: effectiveness depends on what is distilled, how data (real or synthetic) are used, and how risks such as bias transfer, robustness loss, and privacy exposure are managed. I argue KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines but applied with explicit mitigations and task‑aware engineering.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When framed as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output transfer with intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies, teacher-aware optimization, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design)—KD enables deployment of high-performing, smaller models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity, attention to data and distributional issues, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and rare-token failures.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models across NLP and vision domains. When adapted to task and deployment constraints—via multi-teacher schedules, feature-level objectives, data-free synthesis, online protocols, or privacy-aware ensembles—KD both preserves quality and addresses communication, privacy, and compute bottlenecks. However, KD is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity and optimization mismatches can limit its effectiveness, so careful method selection and engineering are required for robust compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance of large teachers while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When applied thoughtfully—using representation-level targets, projector layers, multi-teacher or curriculum schedules, and data-aware workflows—KD consistently outperforms training small models from scratch for many NLP tasks. However, KD is not a panacea: mismatches in capacity, teacher imperfections, data heterogeneity, and distributional shifts require targeted remedies and careful evaluation. This essay argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of model compression in deep learning and NLP, paired with specific design choices to mitigate its limits.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD can be adapted across modalities and constraints—by matching soft logits, intermediate representations, or attention maps; by using ensembles or teacher optimization; and by operating with or without original training data—making it well suited to real-world deployment needs. Because its effectiveness depends on representation alignment, teacher–student design, and data regime, KD is best applied as a component in broader compression pipelines (combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware choices) and selected to fit the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Extensions, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple teacher–student logit matching to a rich set of strategies that address data availability, privacy, distributed settings, architecture mismatches, and task-specific compression needs. Advances include data-free and zero-shot distillation, federated and privacy-aware distillation, representational and layer-mapping techniques for pre-trained language models, and practical combinations with quantization and architecture search to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Landscape of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models by transferring useful information from a teacher to a student, enabling deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention maps, relations) and how (feature matching, channel- or layer-wise alignment, augmentation, self- or data-free schemes). Distillation also serves broader roles beyond compression—regularization, bias transfer or mitigation, domain adaptation, and enabling multi-task or modality conversions. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signal, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and deployment constraints; these choices shape trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students by providing richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD appears to work through a mix of mechanisms — soft targets acting as regularizers, matching intermediate representations, and reducing effective data complexity — and can be combined with data augmentation, privacy-preserving noise, and architecture-aware projectors. Practical research highlights trade-offs related to teacher quality, which samples to transfer, robustness, and device heterogeneity; current methods address these by selective sample transfer, contrastive or feature-level alignment, adversarial objectives, and pre-training compact students before distillation. Key open directions include principled selection of distilled samples, theoretical characterization of when distilled soft targets help versus hurt, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression approaches for deployment on constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervisory signals richer than hard labels. A broad toolkit exists—soft logits, intermediate-feature alignment, attention or relational signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data strategies that range from using original datasets to synthetic or data-free approaches. KD is most effective when treated as a composable part of a compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign, and when distillation objectives and curricula are matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining practical challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, degraded long-tail or rare-token behavior, distribution shift, privacy constraints, and the potential propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones for deployment in constrained environments. KD techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational signals, and operating in data-limited or privacy-sensitive regimes via synthesized or public data. When combined with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, architecture search), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Persistent challenges include understanding the mechanisms of transfer, handling student–teacher capacity mismatch, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, and ensuring robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Representation- and Deployment-Aware Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective for real-world model compression when it goes beyond logits to transfer internal representations, adapts to data availability, and explicitly preserves robustness and deployment constraints. Combining feature- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive layer mapping, data-free synthesis when needed, and robustness-aware training yields compact students that better match teacher behavior across tasks and modalities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. It succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (e.g., softened logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals), and by combining with complementary techniques (pruning, low-precision inference, architecture search, and data augmentation). KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to adapt teachers and students to deployment constraints. Thoughtful design — including feature-level transfer, curriculum or selective-sample strategies, augmentation, and data-free synthesis when needed — makes KD a practical cornerstone of model compression for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment in resource-constrained environments. Distillation methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals, and are effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful data- or task-aware engineering. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance, its success depends on choices about what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data limitations, domain shifts, and fairness or robustness concerns are addressed.

papers_seen.author: Pollard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer signals than hard labels. The method family includes soft-target (logit) matching, feature and attention alignment, structure- and channel-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data strategies ranging from heavy use of unlabeled data to data-free adversarial synthesis. Best practice couples distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware choices (pretraining, augmentation, privacy or federated protocols). Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints; open challenges include preserving long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Armstrong
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to include intermediate-representation and attention transfer, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, data-aware curricula, and combinations with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher’s utility across vision and language when its signals, data, and student capacity are chosen deliberately; remaining challenges center on capacity mismatch, distribution shift, robustness, fairness, and data- or privacy-limited regimes. Best practices emphasize aligning distilled signals with student capacity, using pre-training for compact students, and integrating KD with complementary compression techniques for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated via soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data-aware schemes. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data or augmentation choices, KD frequently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Practical success requires tailoring distillation signals, addressing teacher–student capacity and representation mismatches, and attending to data quality and distributional issues.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, faster students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across modalities, KD includes matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and distilling relational or attention signals; it is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Effective KD requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distillation targets, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and evaluation for robustness and fairness. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, and preserving long-tail behaviors, which motivate context-sensitive, pipeline-oriented compression practices.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research has produced diverse approaches that transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models via softened outputs, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise alignment, module replacement, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis. These methods have been applied across modalities (vision, speech, language, multi-modal), combined with quantization and architecture search, and adapted for settings with limited or private data. Empirical and theoretical work highlights why distillation can improve generalization, how inductive biases or teacher strength influence transfer, and practical strategies to make students more robust and efficient. Challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving task-relevant representations, and designing principled distillation objectives for varied downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, distillation enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when combined with careful choices of transfer target, student architecture, and complementary compression techniques. Practical success depends on data strategies, layer-matching or projector design, and attention to optimization dynamics and teacher–student capacity mismatch; open problems include principled data synthesis or selection, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical element of model-compression pipelines: a flexible toolbox that transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a context-sensitive process—choosing what signals to transfer, adapting teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and retained performance. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires explicit attention to data availability and privacy, robustness and fairness, capacity mismatch, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, broadly applied set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across vision and language modalities KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when matched to student capacity; its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or shifted data. Practical deployment benefits from combining distillation with complementary compression methods and careful training protocols to mitigate failure modes such as loss of rare-token behavior or mismatched architectures.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. Approaches vary from traditional teacher-to-student soft-label transfer to data-free (zero-shot) distillation, online and mutual distillation among peers, meta-learned teachers, and internal-representation matching. Empirical work shows KD can improve student generalization, speed, and footprint but also introduces dataset-specific artifacts (e.g., degraded modeling of low-frequency tokens) and optimization mismatches that require complementary strategies such as exposing raw data, augmentations, adaptive teacher selection, or distillation of intermediate representations. Practical systems (federated or large-scale distributed training) benefit from variants like online or zero-shot distillation to respect privacy and device heterogeneity, while research continues to study why KD works and how to align teacher and student beyond output probabilities.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, graph, and speech tasks, KD variants (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational transfer, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware procedures) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair KD with pretraining, sample-selection, and complementary compression techniques to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; however, challenges remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger pretrained or ensemble teachers in deep learning and NLP. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and aligning teacher and student architectures — KD recovers much of the teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioners explicitly guard against capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, and the propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and settings, KD methods range from matching teacher soft targets (logits) to aligning intermediate representations, combining multiple teachers, synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable, and integrating with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical distillation must balance student capacity, the form of transferred knowledge, data availability and privacy constraints, and optimization strategies to produce compact models that preserve accuracy, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Nelson

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature frames distillation as a multifaceted toolkit — including soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols — that is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and data constraints, and on explicitly addressing failure modes such as transferred biases, optimization mismatch, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Vasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals—enabling students to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy. Its success in real systems depends on matching transfer targets to student capacity, supplying appropriate data or synthetic substitutes, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is powerful and production-ready, but not automatic: careful design, evaluation for robustness and fairness, and integration into broader compression pipelines are required to produce reliable, deployable models.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When executed as the centerpiece of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (representation matching, data strategies, and hardware-aware design), KD routinely yields strong size/accuracy/latency trade-offs. However, KD is not automatic: realizing its benefits requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose robustness and fairness risks.

Combining feature- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive layer mapping, data-free synthesis when needed, and robustness-aware training yields compact students that better match teacher behavior across tasks and modalities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Weiss

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, pragmatic approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with careful teacher–student co-design, representation-level objectives, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of the original performance. At the same time, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on data availability, capacity matching, and mitigation of robustness and fairness risks, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible core of a broader compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful engineering (data selection, projectors, curriculum), but persistent challenges remain in heterogeneous architectures, data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, and rare-token behavior.

While distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s utility in a fraction of the compute or memory cost, practical deployment requires addressing capacity mismatch, data- and domain-shift, rare-token degradation, and propagation of teacher biases through careful method choice and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels — from softened outputs to intermediate representations — KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its greatest practical value lies in being a flexible, composable tool: KD integrates with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet diverse deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution; careful design is required to address data scarcity and privacy, teacher–student mismatch, optimization instability, and the preservation of rare-token or long-tail behavior. Practical pipelines therefore combine task-aware distillation targets, teacher–student co-design, staged training, and robustness and fairness evaluation to realize reliable compressed systems.

papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Effective, Flexible, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully—matching what is transferred to student capacity, combining logits- and feature-level objectives, and integrating complementary techniques like low-precision numerics or architectural redesign—KD consistently yields compact models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints such as privacy or heterogeneity, so practitioners must adapt KD components and pipelines to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and integrating complementary compression methods — KD frequently yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: careful engineering is required to handle capacity mismatch, data scarcity, low-frequency behaviors, and the risk of propagating teacher biases. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline that is adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD methods span matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures for target tasks. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory, success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, robustness and privacy needs, and architecture alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful behavior or representations. Across vision, language, generative, and graph domains, KD operates via multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or ensemble knowledge) and is typically combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can both convey additional task signal and act as a regularizer that improves student generalization relative to training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability or synthesis, teacher quality, and deployment constraints. Practical use requires tailoring distillation recipes to student capacity and application-specific constraints (latency, privacy, domain shift), and open problems remain around optimization mismatches, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive or heterogeneous-data settings.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and federated protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often yields substantial gains in student performance versus training from scratch and enables deployment under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy, but outcomes depend on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and checks for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is not a single recipe but a flexible toolbox: its success depends on teacher design, the choice of distilled signal, data availability, and combination with complementary compression methods. When matched to task and deployment constraints, KD enables real-world use of pretrained models across vision, language, speech, graphs, and structured prediction, while open challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing neural models to smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A spectrum of distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), training regimes (data-driven, data-free, federated, self-distillation), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) has been developed to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints in vision and language applications. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance while enabling substantial runtime and size improvements, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and optimization. Open problems include handling distribution shift, rare-token behavior, teacher–student mismatch, and robust/fair transfer under heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Data Regimes, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or data/privacy constraints. Over the last decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching into diverse objectives and workflows — including feature- and layer-wise matching, self- and online-distillation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and task-aware layer mapping — that together form practical compression toolkits across vision and NLP. Effective distillation depends on careful choice of transferred signals, data strategy, and alignment between teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths come from flexibility in what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, optimization signals), its compatibility with architecture search and other compression primitives, and its ability to operate under constrained or private-data scenarios. KD is not a one-size-fits-all remedy: practitioners should select KD variants and complementary techniques guided by task requirements, data availability, and deployment constraints to balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.
