papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. When engineered carefully—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD yields large efficiency gains while preserving most task performance. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data and curriculum choices, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations through soft targets, feature alignment, and layer-aware signals. While it reliably improves compact-model performance relative to training from scratch, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires adapting KD to task constraints, diagnosing failure modes (e.g., capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token degradation, biased transfer), and using engineering practices such as curriculum-style annealing, targeted augmentation, and hybrid losses.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, pragmatic approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with careful teacher–student co-design, representation-level objectives, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of the original performance. At the same time, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on data availability, capacity matching, and mitigation of robustness and fairness risks, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible core of a broader compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Applications of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more costly models to smaller, deployable models. Modern work expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include distillation of internal representations, feature-level imitation, privacy-preserving and data-free strategies, task-adaptive compression, and adaptations to specialized architectures (e.g., GANs, detectors, and transformers). These methods aim to preserve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency (compute, memory, or communication) while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices or in privacy-sensitive and distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Power, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques and careful engineering it can deliver substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a drop-in cure: success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to prepare teachers and students, how to handle data scarcity or privacy constraints, and how to preserve robustness and fairness. This essay argues that KD should be treated as a flexible core of compression pipelines, and it summarizes practical strategies and caveats for effective, responsible deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach that enables deploying large deep and language models by training smaller students to retain much of the teacher’s performance. When combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data strategies, and teacher–student alignment, KD delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy with modest accuracy loss. However, KD requires task-aware choices, diagnostic checks, and mitigation for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, distillation enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when combined with careful choices of transfer target, student architecture, and complementary compression techniques. Practical success depends on data strategies, layer-matching or projector design, and attention to optimization dynamics and teacher–student capacity mismatch; open problems include principled data synthesis or selection, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student so the student retains much of the teacher’s predictive power while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature has expanded KD beyond matching teacher soft-labels to include intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, online/self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and combinations with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical results across vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and ranking show that distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but practical success depends on choices like teacher design, student capacity, layer alignment, data availability, and training schedules. Remaining challenges include handling low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, optimization and capacity mismatch, matching heterogeneous architectures, and distilling under privacy or data-scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is not a single recipe but a flexible toolbox: its success depends on teacher design, the choice of distilled signal, data availability, and combination with complementary compression methods. When matched to task and deployment constraints, KD enables real-world use of pretrained models across vision, language, speech, graphs, and structured prediction, while open challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. When combined with representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware strategies, and architecture-aware design, KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency. Its effectiveness depends on careful handling of data availability, teacher-student mismatch, and ethical or robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Evidence, and Practical Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft outputs, features, attention/relations), can be combined with pruning/quantization/architecture design, and generalizes across vision, speech, and NLP tasks. Real-world success requires attention to student capacity, data strategies, distributional shift, and mitigation of propagated biases or rare-token failures. Selective and staged distillation, teacher optimization, and task-aware engineering yield the best trade-offs between accuracy and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The family of methods includes matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures. KD is frequently combined with orthogonal compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work across vision, speech, and language demonstrates that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost, though practical success depends on student capacity, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Across vision, speech, and language tasks KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Best practice treats KD as a central element of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—and adapts targets, data, and curricula to task and deployment constraints. Key open issues include representation alignment across architectures, propagated teacher biases, robustness under domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds when the distillation signals, data strategy, and architecture choices are matched to deployment constraints; its most reliable use combines logits-based supervision with representation-level alignment, multi-stage curricula, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful pipeline design is required to avoid transferring teacher errors, to handle low-frequency phenomena and domain shifts, and to meet privacy or data-limited requirements.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Best-Practices Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. When engineered to the task and deployment constraints and combined with complementary techniques (e.g., representation alignment, data strategies, pruning/quantization, and multi-teacher schedules), KD yields strong size–performance tradeoffs. However, practitioners must design distillation pipelines to address capacity mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, bias transfer, and data-privacy constraints to produce robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, multi-stage or online schemes) and composes well with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints. KD enables many deployment goals (reduced latency/memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training), but its effectiveness is limited by optimization dynamics, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift for synthetic data, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable student models. KD techniques range from classic teacher-to-student soft-target training to recent advances including data-free distillation, multi-teacher strategies, meta-learned teachers, and compression combined with pruning or structural sparsity. In NLP applications KD is used to shrink pre-trained transformers, accelerate inference for production systems, enable non-autoregressive generation, and adapt large models to resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while producing models with far lower latency and storage cost, but theoretical understanding, sensitivity to data and teacher quality, and robustness under distributional shifts remain active research areas.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP and other modalities. KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs when its design is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, but it requires engineering choices and complementary techniques to address robustness, fairness, and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The KD toolkit ranges from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and it is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines with pruning, quantization, and student-aware architecture design. Practical success depends on careful engineering choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, which data to use or synthesize, and how to diagnose and mitigate limits such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and distribution shift. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher utility across vision, language, and domain-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. It succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (e.g., softened logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals), and by combining with complementary techniques (pruning, low-precision inference, architecture search, and data augmentation). KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to adapt teachers and students to deployment constraints. Thoughtful design — including feature-level transfer, curriculum or selective-sample strategies, augmentation, and data-free synthesis when needed — makes KD a practical cornerstone of model compression for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: A Practical, Multifaceted Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central, practical tool for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a multifaceted framework—combining soft-label supervision, intermediate representation matching, data- and task-aware training, and architecture-aware design—distillation reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, distillation must be applied carefully: teacher imperfections, low-frequency token behavior, data scarcity, and domain shifts can undermine student quality unless addressed via targeted strategies such as exposing raw data, tailoring teacher signals, and integrating complementary compression methods. With careful engineering and principled choices about what and how to transfer, distillation enables high-performing, efficient models across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods reduce the computational and memory cost of large neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller students. Approaches vary from using soft logits to matching internal representations, attention maps, or generator outputs; they have been adapted for modality transfer, privacy- or bandwidth-constrained settings, and specialized architectures (e.g., transformers, GANs). Empirical work shows that representation-level objectives, architectural design of the student/bridge modules, and careful training protocols can preserve most of the teacher’s performance while dramatically reducing size and runtime. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, deploying under strict privacy/bandwidth constraints, and automating architecture search for compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The practice has evolved from logits matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When matched to task requirements, student capacity, and data constraints, distillation reliably improves size–performance trade-offs for vision and language models, though practical success requires careful design to manage capacity mismatch, distribution shift, privacy, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students so systems meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets — softened logits, intermediate features and attention maps, relational structure, and iterative or multi-teacher curricula — and complementary methods such as pruning, layer skipping, module replacement, and data synthesis. Practical success depends on aligning what is transferred to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with architecture-aware design and validation to avoid optimization mismatches and unwanted bias transfer. Remaining gaps include robustness under domain shift, principled selection of distilled signals, and theoretical accounts that predict when KD will provide large gains.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field encompasses a range of techniques—from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals—and integrates with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, the availability and curation of data (real or synthesized), and deployment constraints such as latency, memory, robustness, and privacy. Persistent challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and ensuring generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s behavior. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods vary by the form of transferred signal (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, or module behaviors), training setting (offline, online, federated, or data-free), and complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, selecting appropriate distillation objectives for the task and data regime, and mitigating distributional or token-frequency artifacts introduced during distillation. This synthesis summarizes major approaches, empirical findings, limitations, and practical strategies for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer behavior from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision and language, practitioners match softened outputs, align internal representations, or transfer relational signals, often combining distillation with quantization, architecture adaptation, or data selection to meet deployment constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the distilled signals chosen, data availability or synthesis, and strategies for aligning heterogeneous architectures and preserving robustness.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Malone
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a central element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques, KD enables deployments that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing those gains in practice requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to data and optimization mismatches, and explicit evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. The practice has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift challenges.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Engineering Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive behavior and representations while reducing latency, memory, and sometimes improving generalization in resource-constrained or domain-specific settings. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of distilled signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and attention to robustness, rare-token fidelity, and privacy. Best results come from treating KD as a central but composable component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses architecture-aware design, data curricula, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Washington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across NLP and other modalities, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware design and other compression methods to achieve favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Effective deployment requires choices about distilled signals, data regimes, teacher–student alignment, and mitigation of transferred harms such as bias and privacy leakage.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression: Effective but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more hardware-friendly students while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness spans supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, but the choice of what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations, attention), how to measure discrepancy, and how to combine KD with pruning or quantization critically determines success. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolbox of complementary techniques whose components must be matched to task, teacher quality, and deployment constraints to obtain reliable and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical cornerstone for compressing large deep models into deployable, lower-latency students while retaining much of their predictive capacity. KD methods span simple soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level transfer, and they can operate in constrained settings (limited data, heterogeneous architectures, cross-modal scenarios). However, the effectiveness of KD depends on what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how KD is combined with complementary compression strategies. Careful design—addressing teacher errors, domain shift, data availability, and architecture mismatch—yields compact models that meet real deployment constraints without disproportionate loss in quality.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully and combined with complementary techniques—layer- and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis or privacy-aware protocols, and hardware-aware downstream optimization—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's utility. However, its practical success is engineering-dependent: careful choices about distilled signals, student preparation, data availability, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases are required to realize reliable, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Opportunities and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students and composes well with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. However, KD is not a turnkey solution—its real-world success requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to detect and mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, or biased transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly used approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—such as softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or many-to-many layer mappings—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of a teacher model’s performance. Effective distillation is context-sensitive: choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use or synthesize, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques determine outcomes. While KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy trade-offs in vision and language tasks, practical adoption requires engineered pipelines to manage capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness risks.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Landscape of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models by transferring useful information from a teacher to a student, enabling deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention maps, relations) and how (feature matching, channel- or layer-wise alignment, augmentation, self- or data-free schemes). Distillation also serves broader roles beyond compression—regularization, bias transfer or mitigation, domain adaptation, and enabling multi-task or modality conversions. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signal, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and deployment constraints; these choices shape trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, enabling deployment under computation, memory, and latency constraints. A range of techniques—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-stage pipelines, and data synthesis—have been developed to address diverse practical needs such as on-device inference, privacy-sensitive releases, federated settings, and domain shifts. Combining KD with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapting distillation signals to task and deployment constraints yields the best real-world outcomes, while open challenges remain around handling distribution shift, data scarcity, and student–teacher capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.
