papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Combinations, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and pragmatic method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving much of a teacher’s performance, but its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), how teacher–student alignment is addressed, and how distillation is integrated with pre-training, architecture design, and other compression tools. I argue that KD should be treated as the central component of an engineering pipeline for efficient NLP and deep-learning systems: it provides flexible transfer mechanisms, enables many successful combinations (multi-teacher, layer mapping, data synthesis), and yields strong practical results, yet it must be paired with complementary strategies and careful choices to manage teacher imperfections, representation mismatch, data limitations, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for reducing the computational and memory footprint of large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Work in this area has diversified beyond the original teacher-to-student soft-label matching to include self-distillation, online and distributed distillation, feature- and representation-level transfer, multi-teacher selection, and data-augmentation-aware distillation. These methods are applied across modalities (vision, speech, NLP, and graphs) and contexts (domain adaptation, continual learning, large-scale training, and on-device deployment), yielding a range of practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and model size. Current advances emphasize richer forms of knowledge (internal representations, relational signals), adaptive teacher weighting, and training-time strategies that improve student generalization, but challenges remain in reliably transferring rare-word or low-frequency behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and scaling distillation to extremely large datasets and models.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural models for deployment and domain-specialization. Beyond simple teacher-to-student label matching, modern KD techniques transfer intermediate representations, exploit synthetic or augmented data, operate without original training data, and incorporate privacy or distributed-training constraints. These variants enable retaining much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, supporting domain adaptation, improving generalization under limited-data regimes, and meeting privacy or latency requirements for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Branch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and ensemble guidance—and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and deployment-aware evaluation. Open challenges include preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, avoiding transferred biases, and principled data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables reduced storage and faster inference while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle when training data are unavailable or misaligned with deployment distributions, and interact subtly with optimization and architecture mismatch. A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies—feature- and layer-level objectives, data-free or synthesized-data protocols when needed, curriculum or sample-weighting policies, and hardware-aware pruning or architecture search—to maximize efficiency without sacrificing robustness or task-specific fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s capabilities. KD spans simple logit-matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, supports multi-stage and teacher-ensemble strategies, and integrates with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Practical success depends on careful choices about distilled signals, data and curricula, and alignment between teacher and student; persistent limits include handling low-frequency behavior, architecture mismatch, data scarcity, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Extensions, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple teacher–student logit matching to a rich set of strategies that address data availability, privacy, distributed settings, architecture mismatches, and task-specific compression needs. Advances include data-free and zero-shot distillation, federated and privacy-aware distillation, representational and layer-mapping techniques for pre-trained language models, and practical combinations with quantization and architecture search to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary methods and adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables significant reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of a teacher model’s task performance. However, realizing these gains in real systems requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as propagation of teacher biases or degraded modeling of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and multimodal tasks, distillation techniques—including self-distillation, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, and teacher adaptation—enable substantial reductions in model size and compute with limited accuracy loss. KD is complementary to other compression strategies (e.g., pruning and architecture search) and benefits from careful choices in intermediate-target selection, data augmentation, and teacher-student alignment. When combined thoughtfully with task adaptation and hardware-aware techniques, KD unlocks feasible deployment of advanced models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt large pretrained models to constrained settings. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how training data are handled (real, augmented, synthesized, or none), and how teachers and students are aligned architecturally and procedurally. When design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss; however, challenges remain for heterogeneous architectures, generative tasks, privacy-sensitive settings, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free protocols—that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student co-design, yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of robustness and bias risks.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. When matched to task needs and combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and robustness or privacy-aware adaptations, KD enables small models to retain much of teachers' performance across modalities. However, KD is context-sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the chosen distillation signal determine outcomes. A pragmatic pipeline blends logit and feature matching, targeted data augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods to achieve robust, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become core methods for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, practitioners compress models by transferring teacher behavior to smaller students, by architectural replacement, or by searching for task-specific compact architectures. Techniques differ in what is transferred (logits, intermediate representations, inter-class relations), how training data are used (original data, distilled targets, or synthetic data), and how robustness and task-specificity are preserved. Empirical work shows strong trade-offs between model size, runtime, and task performance; recent advances focus on task-adaptive compression, improved layer-mapping, data-free approaches, and preserving robustness under adversarial or distributional shifts. Important open challenges remain in handling domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous teacher ensembles, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: Practical Benefits, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated not simply as a single recipe for compression but as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines. KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, and it naturally composes with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and domain-adaptive procedures. To deploy reliable compressed models practitioners must pair KD with careful teacher/student design, data and sample-selection strategies (including data-free synthesis where necessary), evaluation for robustness and fairness, and complementary compression steps that meet hardware constraints. This paper argues for a pragmatic, pipeline-oriented view of KD and outlines targeted practices to maximize utility while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible pathway to deploy high-performing deep learning and NLP models under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases from large or multi-modal teachers to smaller students, distillation enables task- and domain-specific compression, faster inference, privacy-preserving distributed training, and architectural simplification. Effective distillation requires methods that match the target deployment needs—task-awareness, layer alignment, careful use of data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and scaling strategies for large datasets and distributed settings. When designed deliberately, distillation yields compressed models that retain much of the teacher's capability while meeting latency, size, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature frames distillation as a multifaceted toolkit — including soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols — that is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and data constraints, and on explicitly addressing failure modes such as transferred biases, optimization mismatch, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. A diverse set of KD variants—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or reusing data, or adapting student architectures—has been developed. These methods are applied across modalities and combine effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to achieve favorable size/accuracy trade-offs. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select training data, and how to align teacher and student architectures; open challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and integrating complementary compression methods — KD frequently yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: careful engineering is required to handle capacity mismatch, data scarcity, low-frequency behaviors, and the risk of propagating teacher biases. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline that is adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential approach for compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By transferring learned behavior from teachers to students, KD enables many deployment trade-offs while remaining compatible with complementary techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning, architecture search). However, to be robust and broadly useful in real systems, distillation must go beyond naive soft-label matching: effective pipelines combine logits with internal representation transfer, task- and layer-aware selection of signals, appropriate data strategies, and attention to distributional heterogeneity and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and a Design Recipe
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student design, handling data constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. KD has clear failure modes (propagating teacher errors, difficulty with low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift, and robustness/privacy concerns) that require principled pipelines, diagnostics, and mitigation strategies. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines but only effective when integrated with representation-aware objectives, data-aware strategies, and robustness/privacy-aware techniques.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and language tasks, KD transfers information from teachers to students using softened outputs, intermediate representations, or auxiliary signals; it is commonly combined with data augmentation, architecture adaptation, and privacy-preserving or data-free procedures. When applied with care to teacher signals, data selection, and student capacity, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s performance, but meaningful limitations remain (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases) that must be managed in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Gay
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple granularities — softened outputs, intermediate feature or attention alignment, relational signals, and synthesized or public-data training — and are often combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, curriculum, or data-free synthesis). Empirically, KD routinely yields strong size–accuracy trade-offs across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, but its success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals to student capacity, attention to data availability and domain shift, and checks for transferred biases and rare-token degradation. Remaining challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models, and robustly distilling across heterogeneous architectures or privacy constraints.

However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned, data quality and selection, and deployment constraints.

Advances in task-aware, layer-wise, data-free, and adversarially-informed distillation methods demonstrate that KD can address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and heterogeneity in deployment environments, making it a central tool for practical NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Practical KD spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, multi‑teacher schedules, and data-aware or data‑free workflows, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and deployment‑aware design. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical strengths, typical failure modes, and best practices for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Across vision, speech, and language tasks KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Best practice treats KD as a central element of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—and adapts targets, data, and curricula to task and deployment constraints. Key open issues include representation alignment across architectures, propagated teacher biases, robustness under domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD techniques include matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-level transfers, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and appropriate pre-training or data strategies, KD often yields compact models that approach teacher performance. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate robustness, bias, and capacity-mismatch issues.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Deployment Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels — from softened outputs to intermediate representations — KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its greatest practical value lies in being a flexible, composable tool: KD integrates with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet diverse deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution; careful design is required to address data scarcity and privacy, teacher–student mismatch, optimization instability, and the preservation of rare-token or long-tail behavior. Practical pipelines therefore combine task-aware distillation targets, teacher–student co-design, staged training, and robustness and fairness evaluation to realize reliable compressed systems.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works through multiple mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate representation transfer, and inductive-bias alignment) and yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary techniques and task-aware engineering. However, realizing KD’s value in production requires explicit handling of teacher imperfections, data- or privacy-limited regimes, and low-frequency behavior through careful signal choice, curriculum and sample selection, and architectural or optimization adjustments.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers learned behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and sometimes improve regularization and robustness. A diverse toolkit has emerged—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention and channel-wise supervision, data-aware strategies including synthetic or public-data distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical deployment emphasizes task-aware choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers and data, and how to combine compression techniques), while open problems include theory of when distillation helps, handling rare-token behavior in NLP, distributional shift, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across modalities and constraints — including resource-limited devices, privacy- or data-constrained settings, distributed systems, and adversarial robustness requirements — KD and its variants enable trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and practicality. Best results arise when practitioners combine representation-level distillation, careful layer mapping, and appropriate pre-training or data-synthesis strategies to match the deployment scenario.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, higher‑capacity teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Methods span matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, designing teacher training to ease transfer, selecting or synthesizing distillation data, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can retain much teacher performance when carefully applied, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to handle student capacity and data heterogeneity, and how to mitigate teacher imperfections and robustness or fairness tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to lightweight students. Over the last decade KD has diversified from matching teacher soft-labels to a broad set of techniques—feature- and layer-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher/self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols. Empirical work shows KD frequently yields large reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to obtain or generate training data, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques. Important open issues include preserving rare-token behaviors, avoiding amplification of teacher biases, ensuring privacy in distributed settings, and understanding optimization dynamics that govern when and how distilled signals help.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical strategy for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the last decade has extended KD from simple softened-logit matching into a flexible toolkit that transfers soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure, and curriculum or ensemble signals. In practice KD is typically combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies) and used with task-aware choices about distilled signals and training data. KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic, flexible pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. As a composable toolset rather than a single recipe, KD transfers soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational signals; composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; and can be adapted for multi-teacher, data-limited, and privacy-aware regimes. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, designing layer-aware objectives and curricula, and mitigating known failure modes such as data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, robustness degradation, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level transfer, augmentation or synthesized data, and orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD delivers strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to optimization dynamics, data availability, privacy, and known failure modes (e.g., low-frequency token degradation), and so KD should be applied as part of an integrated, responsible compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teacher models. KD works by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (architecture-aware compression, pruning, quantization) and careful data and evaluation practices. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, what signals are distilled, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices, staged training, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, practitioners apply KD to reduce model size, latency, and resource cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Variants of KD extend beyond soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, cross-modal transfer, and data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. Effective distillation typically combines careful choice of transfer target, student architecture and pre-training, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization). Open challenges include principled data selection or synthesis for distillation, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, preserving robustness and fairness, and scaling distillation to large distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with careful teacher–student engineering, appropriate distillation signals, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, its reliability depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, alignment of representations, and explicit mitigation of robustness, privacy, and rare-token or distribution-shift failures. I argue KD should be the core of any real-world compression strategy, but only when embedded in an engineering-aware pipeline that anticipates and corrects its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, faster models that retain much of the capability of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit matching, modern KD leverages internal representation transfer, selective data strategies, and integration with pruning, architecture search, or federated protocols to meet latency, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables efficient deployment across modalities while posing clear methodological trade-offs and open challenges that guide future research.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (original, public, synthesized, or data-free) have been developed. Distillation is typically used as the central component of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, and architecture design; its practical success depends on matching transfer signals to student capacity, teacher quality, and data availability while attending to robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical Strategy for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are indispensable for deploying high-capacity deep and language models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, practitioners can achieve large reductions in model size and latency while retaining most task performance. However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, context‑sensitive mechanism in practical model compression. When carefully designed and combined with complementary tools — pruning, quantization, architecture search, synthetic or privacy‑aware data, and task‑aware curricula — KD produces compact models that retain much of a teacher’s performance across modalities and deployment constraints. However, KD is not automatic: success requires explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate harmful teacher behaviors. A principled KD pipeline that adapts to task, data, and hardware needs yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and utility.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so that compact models can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data strategies (original data, public or synthesized data, and data-free or adversarial sample generation) has been developed. KD is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware search) and adapted to application domains (NLP, 2D/3D vision, federated settings). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match teacher and student capacity, and how to address distribution shift, rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and language tasks, KD transfers information from teachers to students using softened outputs, intermediate representations, or auxiliary signals; it is commonly combined with data augmentation, architecture adaptation, and privacy-preserving or data-free procedures. When applied with care to teacher signals, data selection, and student capacity, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s performance, but meaningful limitations remain (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases) that must be managed in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary methods and adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables significant reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of a teacher model’s task performance. However, realizing these gains in real systems requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as propagation of teacher biases or degraded modeling of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks, researchers combine KD with architectural compression, pre-training, privacy mechanisms, and data-free approaches to address inference cost, dataset availability, and domain-specific challenges. Empirical work shows that careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, layers), how to train teachers and students, and how to incorporate task or data constraints strongly determine final student quality.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students so models can run with lower compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of their performance. The technique has diversified from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure, and it integrates naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher–student pairs, which data to use (real, public, or synthesized), and how to manage optimization, distribution shift, and societal risks (robustness, fairness, privacy). Ongoing work refines objectives, curricula, and data strategies to preserve rare or long-tail behaviors and to scale KD for modern large pretrained models across vision, language, and generative tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted, Practical Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick of copying a stronger model but as a multifaceted training paradigm that can compress, regularize, and adapt models for deployment. When practitioners choose the right distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention mappings), tailor objectives to data and privacy constraints, and combine KD with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis), they can produce compact students that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness requirements. Effective use of KD requires attention to representation alignment, optimization schedules, and the constraints of the deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical tool for compressing deep and NLP models because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD excels when combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, but it is not a panacea: careful design choices are required to handle capacity mismatch, limited data, distribution shift, imperfect teachers, and transferred biases. A disciplined pipeline — choosing appropriate distillation signals, augmenting or synthesizing data when necessary, and aligning teacher–student architectures — yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds when designers move beyond naive soft-label matching to combine multiple transfer signals (logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, pre-training, or synthetic data), and deployment-aware adaptations (layer mapping, capacity-aware objectives, and composition with pruning/quantization). Its power in practice comes from this flexibility, but realizing it requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables reduced storage and faster inference while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle when training data are unavailable or misaligned with deployment distributions, and interact subtly with optimization and architecture mismatch. A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies—feature- and layer-level objectives, data-free or synthesized-data protocols when needed, curriculum or sample-weighting policies, and hardware-aware pruning or architecture search—to maximize efficiency without sacrificing robustness or task-specific fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer information from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. This synthesis summarizes methodological families (soft-label distillation, representation distillation, adversarial and decision-boundary approaches, data-free and domain-adaptive strategies), theoretical insights about when and why distillation helps, and practical considerations including robustness, privacy, and architecture-aware compression. It highlights representative results and trade-offs reported across recent work, and outlines open directions for improving optimization, preserving robustness, and adapting distillation to domain and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing which signals to transfer, matching student capacity to tasks, and combining distillation with architectural and data strategies—KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for on-device, latency-sensitive, and domain-specific NLP systems. Its advantages are balanced by contextual failure modes (teacher imperfections, distribution shift, rare-token fidelity) that require pipeline-level engineering, careful evaluation, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical element of model-compression pipelines: a flexible toolbox that transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a context-sensitive process—choosing what signals to transfer, adapting teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and retained performance. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires explicit attention to data availability and privacy, robustness and fairness, capacity mismatch, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. As a practical compression primitive it integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis techniques to meet deployment constraints across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. KD is not a plug-and-play cure—its success depends on what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data or privacy constraints are handled—but when designed carefully it delivers an effective balance of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.
